artigo.texto: In recent days, a Ukrainian drone strike hit Russia’s largest data center, owned by bank and technology company Sberbank. The strike came after Ukraine hit three data centers belonging to the tech giant Yandex, which is often referred to as “Russia’s Google.” After those attacks, Yandex’s traffic dropped 94%. Its users experienced heavy disruption to features such as email, search, navigation, music, ride-hailing, marketplace and financial services. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the strikes had made it “easier to breathe on many social media platforms”, by reducing Russian disinformation and bot activity. Later reports have cast doubt on Zelensky’s claim. Either way, the incident highlights the role of physical communication infrastructure in the online world. It also raises questions over what “digital sovereignty” really means, and hints at a way to fight disinformation. Data in the line of fire Data centers are an unconventional military target. However, that may be changing as their importance grows. Attacking data centers may disrupt an enemy’s military operations, as well as the ordinary civilian services that rely on these facilities. In Russia, these disruptions may slow down the economy in the long term, undermining its ability to continue the war. Ukraine’s strikes came after Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centers and internet service providers. They also follow a precedent set by Iran earlier this year when it hit data centers in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain in response to American attacks. The Middle East data centers were run by Amazon Web Services, the world’s biggest cloud computing company with facilities around the globe. Typically, data centres use redundancy and backups to make sure losing a single facility does not have permanent negative consequences. Even so, the Iranian strikes resulted in long-term degradation of services and irrecoverable loss of some data. Russian data centres may have less in the way of international redundancy options. This is due to a particular vision of “digital sovereignty”, which Moscow has actively championed over the past decade. The idea that nations should have autonomy and control over their own digital data and infrastructure is a sound one. However, Russia’s pursuit of “sovereignty” has enabled it to censor online information and isolate Russian users from global internet services. Russia passed laws requiring certain data to be stored locally in 2015. These were followed by international sanctions after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. As a result, Russia’s options for maintaining backup infrastructure abroad have been significantly limited. Disinformation and influence Disinformation is often considered as the strategic spreading of deliberate falsehoods. Governments have often tried to fight it by removing or debunking these falsehoods on the platforms where they circulate. However, influence operations work in many different ways. Not all of them propagate falsehoods. Most of them aim to undermine public trust and delegitimise democratic processes and institutions. In Australia’s 2023 referendum on an Indigenous Voice to Parliament, for example, campaigners generated plausible competing narratives to exacerbate political polarisation. In New Zealand, influence operations have involved avalanches of misogynistic abuse to derail public support for policy initiatives. Russia is known for its orchestrated interventions in democratic politics around the world. The goal of these interventions has often been to sow dissent, distrust and dismay. Supporting candidates with pro-Russian stances can also be a goal. Civil society and activist communities have developed creative approaches to tackling this problem. These have included debunking, prebunking (preemptively countering false claims), reporting misleading content to platforms, or strategically using humor and memes. Digital sovereignty can create points of weakness The data center attacks in Russia are a reminder that Russian internet services – including influence operations – depend on physical infrastructure. Whether or not the strikes have led to a significant reduction in disinformation bot activity this time around, targeting the physical sources of disinformation may still be an effective way to contain it. There are over 100 data centers operating on Russian territory. Few of them have backups and resilience plans in place. Concentrating all digital operations in a relatively small number of physical sites creates a vulnerability. Once this infrastructure is hit, rebuilding can be slow and challenging, especially as Russia is reliant on China to supply advanced semiconductors. Lessons for democracies What does this mean for efforts to counter Russian disinformation and influence operations more broadly? One set of solutions might involve imposing physical or regulatory limits (such as sanctions) on Russian-based platforms and services such as Telegram. Other solutions would require international cooperation to undermine Russia’s capability to inflict harm in the digital environments. This may include supporting Ukraine’s efforts on the battlefront through bilateral security agreements. In any case, the recent events have shown that Russia’s digital influence extensively relies on physical infrastructures: data centers, scarce semiconductor materials and a domestic platform ecosystem that has been splintered from the world wide web. As the Kremlin continues to isolate itself in the name of sovereignty, it is also becoming more vulnerable to attacks and disruptions. Democracies can draw lessons from these events. Digital sovereignty is not achieved through isolation and vertical control over digital infrastructures. Instead, it is constantly negotiated through geographically distributed backups, frameworks for risk and governance, and strategic alliances that keep critical systems running and make them resilient to attacks. Olga Boich

artigo.texto: - Firefly currently offers only a 42.1-kWh battery pack. The new pack will deliver a CLTC range of 560 kilometers. - The new pack will be available as an upgrade for new and existing owners, with details to be announced on October 23. Nio Inc (NYSE: NIO) will launch a 60-kWh battery pack for its small electric vehicle brand Firefly on October 23, offering new and existing owners a larger-capacity battery option. Pu Yang, Firefly's head of brand marketing, disclosed the plan at a user gathering in Zhengzhou, Henan province, on Friday, according to a video shared by Weibo blogger Arthur Shen. The 60-kWh pack is a long-life battery from CATL (HKEX: 3750) that will give Firefly a range of 560 kilometers, Pu said. The pack will be available to both new and existing Firefly owners, with details to be announced at the October 23 launch event, Pu added. Firefly supports battery swapping and currently offers only a 42.1-kWh battery pack. The larger option will expand the small EV's suitability for longer trips beyond its core urban commuting use. Upgrades to the 60-kWh pack by customers who purchased the standard-range Firefly could also generate additional revenue for Nio Inc. The 42.1-kWh pack uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry, while the 60-kWh pack is expected to use ternary lithium chemistry to provide more capacity within the same dimensions. The upgrade will give Firefly a choice of battery capacities, bringing it in line with the group's 2 other brands. The Nio main brand currently offers 75-kWh and 100-kWh packs, while Onvo offers 60-kWh and 85-kWh packs. The battery upgrade plan follows Firefly's integration into Nio's battery swap network. On August 7, Nio began operating its first fifth-generation swap stations in 7 cities, supporting Firefly vehicles for the first time. Firefly had been unable to use Nio's fourth-generation stations because of its shorter body and wheelbase. The fifth-generation stations allow vehicles from all 3 brands — Nio, Onvo and Firefly — to share these facilities. The product update also comes as Firefly's deliveries grow. The brand said Friday that a ceremony marking its 90,000th vehicle delivery was held in Zhengzhou, about 1.5 months after it reached the 80,000-vehicle milestone at the end of August. Firefly delivered a record 7,327 vehicles in September, up 26.9% year-on-year and 25.2% from August, according to data compiled by CnEVPost. In the first 9 months of this year, Firefly delivered 48,122 vehicles, accounting for 16.02% of Nio Inc's total deliveries and supporting the group's expansion into the small-car market.

artigo.texto: De rainhas de bateria a baianas: flash mob reúne as 12 escolas do Grupo Especial na Praça Mauá para anunciar sambas de 2027 Apresentação com mais de 50 sambistas surpreendeu quem passava pela região central do Rio; álbum oficial será lançado nas plataformas digitais em 29 de outubro Atualizado Rainhas de bateria, baianas, passistas, ritmistas e outros representantes das 12 escolas de samba do Grupo Especial do Rio se reuniram na tarde desta quinta-feira na Praça Mauá, no Centro, para anunciar o lançamento do álbum oficial dos sambas-enredo do Carnaval de 2027. A apresentação, em formato de flash mob, mobilizou mais de 50 sambistas e marcou a contagem regressiva para a chegada das músicas às plataformas digitais, prevista para o próximo dia 29 de outubro. - Idosa baleada: Leblon teve alta de 46% nos roubos a pedestre este ano, segundo dados do ISP - Rivaldo Barbosa, Álvaro Lins e Marcus Amim: quem são os ex-chefes da Polícia Civil do Rio que já foram presos Organizada pela Liga Independente das Escolas de Samba do Rio de Janeiro (Liesa), a ação reuniu integrantes de diferentes segmentos das agremiações, entre eles mestres de bateria, intérpretes, casais de mestre-sala e porta-bandeira, integrantes das velhas guardas e das comissões de frente. A apresentação foi planejada para surpreender cariocas e turistas que passavam por um dos principais cartões-postais da cidade. A coreografia ficou a cargo de Priscilla Mota e Rodrigo Nery, da Viradouro, atual campeã do Grupo Especial. A trilha sonora contou com uma prévia do samba-enredo da escola de Niterói, que abrirá o álbum de 2027, seguindo a tradição de reservar a primeira faixa à campeã do Carnaval anterior. - Thiago Gomide: As histórias esquecidas de São Gonçalo — Foi uma missão muito especial reunir pessoas de todas as escolas. A ideia foi fazer o encontro da cidade com o Carnaval. Quem ama Carnaval ficará ainda mais curioso para ouvir o samba da sua escola — afirmou Priscilla Mota. O presidente da Liesa, Gabriel David, destacou que a apresentação foi uma forma de aumentar a expectativa dos sambistas para a divulgação das músicas que serão levadas à Avenida no próximo ano. — O lançamento do álbum do Rio Carnaval é um dos momentos mais aguardados do ano. Por isso, resolvemos preparar esse momento inédito para divulgar a data do lançamento e deixar todo mundo ainda mais ansioso! Todos podem esperar um álbum sensacional — disse. Gravado em setembro, logo após a definição dos sambas-enredo nas quadras das escolas, o álbum foi produzido em formato ao vivo, com realização da Edimusa e produção musical de Alceu Maia. Segundo a organização, as transmissões dos concursos de samba pela Rio Carnaval TV somaram mais de 3 milhões de visualizações. A apresentação na Praça Mauá também foi registrada em vídeo, com imagens divulgadas nos canais oficiais do Rio Carnaval nas redes sociais. Os desfiles do Grupo Especial em 2027 estão marcados para os dias 7, 8 e 9 de fevereiro, na Marquês de Sapucaí. Já o Sábado das Campeãs será realizado em 13 de fevereiro.

artigo.texto: Vietnam Eyes Battery Storage to Unlock Rooftop Solar Potential Industry groups and policymakers identify energy storage infrastructure as critical bottleneck for distributed generation expansion across residential and commercial buildings. - ·Vietnam's rooftop solar expansion depends on battery storage deployment to address grid integration limits and intermittency challenges affecting distributed generation. - ·The Ministry of Industry and Trade is developing regulatory frameworks including time-of-use tariffs and capacity payments to incentivise storage systems alongside photovoltaic installations. - ·Lithium-ion battery costs fell 14 per cent globally in 2025 to USD 139 per kilowatt-hour, improving project economics for solar-plus-storage systems in Vietnam's industrial zones. Storage Gap Slows Distributed Generation Vietnam's rooftop solar sector faces a structural constraint that battery storage systems could resolve, according to industry stakeholders and government officials assessing the country's renewable energy transition. The Southeast Asian nation installed significant rooftop photovoltaic capacity during earlier subsidy programmes, but grid integration limits and the absence of storage infrastructure now restrict further expansion. Electricity demand in Vietnam grew 9.8 per cent year-on-year in the first eight months of 2025, driven by manufacturing export growth and rising household consumption. Rooftop solar offers a distributed generation pathway that reduces transmission losses and defers grid upgrade costs, yet the technology's intermittent output creates operational challenges for state utility Electricity of Vietnam without accompanying storage. Battery systems allow building owners to capture midday generation peaks and discharge during evening demand surges, smoothing supply curves and reducing strain on distribution networks. The technology also enables self-consumption models that improve project economics for commercial and industrial users facing higher tariff structures. Policy Framework Under Development Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade is evaluating regulatory mechanisms to incentivise storage deployment alongside rooftop solar installations. Current feed-in tariff structures do not differentiate between solar-plus-storage projects and standalone photovoltaic systems, removing financial incentives for developers to add batteries despite grid benefits. Policymakers are examining time-of-use tariffs and capacity payment schemes that would reward storage operators for providing grid services. Such frameworks exist in Thailand and the Philippines, where battery systems participate in frequency regulation and peak shaving programmes. The ministry has not announced a timeline for new regulations, though industry participants expect pilot programmes to launch in major industrial zones during 2027. Manufacturing hubs in the southern provinces of Binh Duong and Dong Nai present logical test cases, given high daytime electricity consumption and existing rooftop solar penetration. Cost Trajectory Improves Economics Lithium-ion battery prices declined 14 per cent globally in 2025, reaching USD 139 per kilowatt-hour at the pack level. Analysts project further reductions as Chinese manufacturers expand production capacity and new chemistries enter commercial deployment. Vietnam imports most battery storage components, primarily from China and South Korea, with domestic assembly limited to a handful of renewable energy firms. Lower equipment costs improve payback periods for solar-plus-storage projects, though financing remains constrained for small and medium enterprises without access to green credit facilities. State-owned commercial banks have increased lending for renewable energy projects under central bank directives, yet loan terms typically require collateral exceeding project asset values. Development banks and multilateral lenders are exploring guarantee mechanisms to reduce perceived risks for rooftop solar storage investments. Grid Modernisation Parallel Track Energy storage deployment must proceed alongside broader grid infrastructure upgrades if Vietnam is to meet its 2030 renewable energy targets. The national power development plan calls for 47,000 megawatts of solar capacity by the end of the decade, with rooftop systems expected to contribute approximately one-third of that total. Transmission congestion in southern provinces already curtails utility-scale solar output during low-demand periods, a problem that distributed generation with storage could partially alleviate. However, distribution network operators lack real-time monitoring systems and advanced inverter controls necessary to manage high penetrations of behind-the-meter generation. International donors have committed funding for smart meter rollouts and grid management software, though implementation timelines extend beyond 2028 in most provinces. The sequencing challenge requires storage incentives to align with grid readiness, avoiding stranded assets or curtailment that undermines project viability. Vietnam's rooftop solar trajectory will depend on how quickly storage costs fall and whether policy frameworks create sufficient returns for combined systems. The country's manufacturing sector offers substantial demand for daytime generation paired with evening storage discharge, positioning industrial rooftops as the most viable near-term market segment.

artigo.texto: It was as if Connie Lane were standing on the precipice of the Grand Canyon, she said, staring in disbelief at its enormity. The hyperscale data center near Milwaukee, where Lane had been visiting with friends from law school for a June reunion, left her incredulous. “I can’t begin to describe the scope. They brought in these huge lines to feed them electricity. I was stunned. It’s one thing when you read about it; it’s another thing to see it,” she said. Lane, a Democratic state representative, is running for reelection in Merrimack District 13, or Concord’s Ward 2. In her response to the Monitor’s general election survey, she cited energy policy and the feared effect of data centers on the power grid and ratepayers as one of the most salient issues facing the state of New Hampshire. There are currently ten data centers in New Hampshire, four of which are clustered in Manchester, according to the tracking platform Data Center Map. Proposals in Bow and Nottingham have spurred public outcry that, in the latter case, prompted the developer to withdraw his plan just hours before the town’s planning board was scheduled to review it. That opposition is hardly exclusive to the Granite State. Data centers have unified Democrats and Republicans, progressives and conservatives, in forceful resistance as local disputes over land use, municipal transparency, tax incentives and environmental impacts repeat themselves nationwide. “They’re going to come in, electricity is going to soar, and are we really ready for this vast use of our land? Is this the way we really want to develop acres and acres and acres?” Lane said. Earlier this year in New Hampshire, a group of Republican lawmakers inverted an effort to affirm municipalities’ ability to regulate data centers, amending the language of the bill, Senate Bill 439, to do the opposite: allow data centers by right in areas zoned for commercial or industrial development. The bill was ultimately tabled and didn’t advance further. Gov. Kelly Ayotte, a Republican, told WMUR at the time that she opposed those alterations to the bill. In the months since, she’s stated she will impose a moratorium on new data center developments with the upcoming state budget, citing concern that, at an average energy consumption of 100 megawatts, even one hyperscale development could overburden the regional grid. “I’ve been clear that I oppose siting data centers in New Hampshire, including the proposed projects in Nottingham and Bow. Data centers would drive up our already too-high energy costs, and I share the concerns raised about their impact on our water and environment,” she said in a statement to the Monitor. Her gubernatorial challenger, Democrat Cinde Warmington, said she doubts the governor’s intentions based on her perceived lack of leadership on data center-related bills, like SB 439, and that she would like to see the state act more expediently. If elected, Warmington said she would impose a temporary moratorium on the permitting of new data centers on “day-one.” Her campaign’s “data center bill of rights” outlines some of the safeguards she’d push for in a regulatory framework: limits on noise pollution, requirements that construction draw on local labor through protected agreements and protections for clean air and water. “I think it is really hypocritical that Gov. Ayotte now suddenly is calling for a moratorium,” Warmington told the Monitor. “Now she says she’s for a moratorium in her budget next year — by next year we could have a massive data center in our state. We know there’s one proposed in Bow. So too little, too late, and pretty disingenuous.” Imagining how the legislature might devise more permanent regulations on data centers, Lane told the Monitor the state “would certainly want to do a lot of study” to inform the drafting process, but that “personally, I don’t want them at all.” The hyperscale data centers recently proposed in New Hampshire provide a window into the rabid acceleration of development to keep pace with artificial intelligence’s demand for computing power, and the imposing dimension of data centers being built in other parts of the country. One colossal data center development, imagined by technology company Fermi America for the Texas Panhandle and dubbed “Project Matador”, is expected to have a capacity of 17 gigawatts. The development’s first power-generating equipment, three 480,000-pound gas turbines, arrived on site near Amarillo last month, according to local reporting. By comparison, the proposal that public filings indicate is in the very early, exploratory stages of being permitted for development in Bow could draw between 200 and 350 megawatts of power — two percent of that capacity. William Lynch, the Democratic candidate for Merrimack District 10, which includes Hooksett and Dunbarton, said he worries not only about the unmistakable environmental consequences of such large developments but the possibility that, if the AI bubble bursts, today’s enormous investments will produce warehouses full of data storage no one uses tomorrow. “I’ve seen commitments to build out data centers that progress as far as building. But some data centers are not keeping pace with their commitments, and I’m concerned that it might come to a point, in two or three years, where the overall investment and use of the computing power won’t keep up,” he said. Lynch had an eight-year career with tech giant Oracle, a major cloud and AI data center operator. He described his work — first as a cloud applications engineer, then pivoting to health applications — as building the software infrastructure on top of which other software engineers iterate. His software could be adapted for use on websites like Facebook or the New York Times, or it could be deployed into traditional data centers. artigo.texto: Microsoft desiste de acordo para data center no Reino Unido em momento crucial para planos de IPO da Nscale Segundo o jornal The Telegraph, não foram apresentados os motivos para que a gigante americana abandonasse o acorfo referente ao empreendimento em Loughton, no condado de Essex A Microsoft desistiu de um acordo para um data center no Reino Unido com a britânica Nscale, especializada em infraestrutura de computação em nuvem para inteligência artificial, em um momento crucial para as perspectivas de abertura de capital da startup, informou o jornal The Telegraph. O jornal não apresentou uma razão específica para a decisão da gigante americana de tecnologia de abandonar o acordo referente ao empreendimento em Loughton, no condado de Essex, mas afirmou que o projeto vem enfrentando uma série de atrasos. Segundo a publicação, as autoridades informaram à Nscale que não esperam fornecer energia à instalação antes da década de 2030. O principal empreendimento da Nscale na Noruega também está seis meses atrasado, com apenas 6,4 megawatts dos 30 megawatts de capacidade previstos para o data center em operação. De acordo com um documento apresentado no âmbito dos preparativos para o IPO, a Nscale depende da Microsoft e da Anthropic para cerca de 85% de seus contratos. A Microsoft estava prestes a se tornar a principal cliente do primeiro data center britânico da Nscale, em Essex. A saída da Microsoft representaria um revés para a empresa, que pretende captar até US$ 3 bilhões em uma oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês), possivelmente ainda neste mês, e que já vinha enfrentando a apreensão dos investidores em relação aos riscos da expansão mais ampla da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. A Nscale é uma das empresas mais proeminentes do segmento conhecido como neocloud, formado por companhias que buscam construir enormes complexos computacionais voltados à inteligência artificial. Essas empresas querem aproveitar os centenas de bilhões de dólares que as gigantes de tecnologia se comprometeram a investir nessa área e representam um elo fundamental na cadeia de suprimentos que sustenta o boom da IA. Um porta-voz da Nscale disse ao The Telegraph: “Continuamos comprometidos com o projeto de Loughton e com o Reino Unido, e estamos estudando fontes alternativas de energia para o local, além de outros locais para expansão no país. “Nossa relação com a Microsoft continua sólida e é de longo prazo, e esse lamentável problema na rede elétrica de Londres não afeta nossos outros contratos.” A Microsoft não comentou o assunto ao The Telegraph e não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Bloomberg feito fora do horário comercial habitual. O cenário para os planos de abertura de capital da Nscale ficou mais desfavorável nos últimos dias. Na semana passada, a também neocloud CoreWeave ganhou destaque depois que seu cofundador afirmou que a empresa estava estudando formas de captar recursos nos mercados de dívida com grau de investimento, que oferecem amplos volumes de capital provenientes de investidores como seguradoras. Os investidores já vinham demonstrando cautela em relação aos fornecedores de capacidade computacional para IA, diante das dezenas de bilhões de dólares em empréstimos contraídos por essas empresas e por seus clientes para financiar a enorme expansão da capacidade dos data centers. As ações da CoreWeave despencaram nas três primeiras sessões da semana e depois se recuperaram parcialmente. Na sexta-feira, porém, as preocupações voltaram a pesar sobre os papéis, provocando a pior semana da empresa desde novembro, com uma queda de 25%. O episódio também ocorreu após a australiana Firmus, do setor de data centers, abandonar seus planos de abertura de capital porque a oferta não conseguiu atrair apoio suficiente ao preço das ações proposto ao mercado.

artigo.texto: BYD has launched a new EV at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, but it's one Australians might find a little familiar. The BYD Atto 8 launched this week is an electric version of the 2026 BYD Sealion 8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) launched in Australia recently. Set to top the BYD range in Europe, the Atto 8/ Sealion 8 EV is the first in that market to feature cutting-edge 'flash charging'. Read more - 2027 BYD Sealion 8: Mega upgrades could be on the way for strong-selling hybrid seven-seat rival to the Toyota Kluger and Hyundai Santa Fe - BYD Sealion 8 2026 review: Premium AWD - Signs BYD is starting a new price war: $4000 cashback on 2026 BYD Sealion 7 electric SUV, Shark 6 ute, Seal 6 sedan and more The new feature allows the large SUV to go from 10 per cent battery capacity to 97 per cent in just nine minutes, a feature yet to launch in Australia. BYD's local arm told CarsGuide the Sealion 8 PHEV is, for now, the range-topper given how recently it launched, with no immediate plans to bring the EV version here. "We only launched Sealion 8 earlier this year and it's ticking all the boxes for us at the moment so we're not thinking too far ahead at this stage," a BYD spokesperson said. The BYD Sealion 8 plug-in hybrid launched at the start of 2026 with a starting price of $56,990 before on-roads for its front-wheel drive base model, with a top-spec all-wheel drive grade at $70,990. In its home market of China, the Sealion 8 or Atto 8 is called the 'BYD Tang L' What does the BYD Atto 8 EV get? The base Atto 8 has a front-drive setup with 340kW and 365Nm, with a 115kWh battery and a WLTP range of 652km, while the top-spec AWD version has 570kW and 775Nm with a range of 602km but an impressive 0-100km/h sprint of 4.6 seconds. A huge 26-inch widescreen head-up display, a 15.6-inch central multimedia touchscreen, a 10.25-inch digital instrument display and a seven-seat layout with heating and cooling in the front two (outboard) rows join tri-zone climate control, dual wireless phone chargers, numerous USB-C ports and a front refrigerator/heating compartment. In each grade, the seat upholstery is all genuine leather. What is flash charging? With "3000 stations to be installed across Europe by the end of 2027", flash charging is about to become a much more common thing in the EU. The system allows as much as 1500kW to juice the EV's battery, in this case the Atto 8's 115kWh battery, to near-full much faster than usual. In the Atto 8, this means 10 to 97 per cent in nine minutes, though in severely cold temperatures that normally limit charging the flash system still allows 20 to 97 per cent in 12 minutes, not bad. Just five minutes of charging is said to add 60 per cent (from 10 to 70 per cent) to the battery - all resulting in BYD's line of 'ready in 5, full in 9, cold add 3'.

artigo.texto: The compact electric kei car expands beyond Japan with a 320km driving range, two LFP battery options and seating for four passengers. BYD has introduced its compact Racco electric car in Sri Lanka, marking the model’s first market entry outside Japan. The small electric vehicle is available at an introductory price of 11,450,000 Sri Lankan rupees, equivalent to approximately $34,615. The introductory offer is scheduled to remain valid until November 9, 2026. According to BYD’s local representatives, the price may increase after the promotional period ends. Macau is also expected to receive the electric kei car as the automaker expands its presence in additional right-hand-drive markets. Price Difference Between Japan and Sri Lanka The Sri Lankan price is considerably higher than the vehicle’s cost in its original market. When the Racco debuted in Japan in July 2026, its prices ranged from 2,140,000 yen to 2,497,000 yen, equivalent to approximately $13,555 to $15,815. The difference reflects the additional costs associated with importing vehicles into Sri Lanka, where taxes and import duties can substantially increase retail prices. For comparison, the petrol-powered Toyota Yaris Cross is priced at approximately 19,950,000 Sri Lankan rupees, or $60,315, in the country. The Racco has already attracted attention in Japan, reportedly receiving more than 1,000 orders within two weeks of its launch. Battery Options and Driving Range The BYD Racco features a box-shaped exterior designed around the compact dimensions of Japan’s kei car category. It measures 3,395mm in length, 1,475mm in width and 1,800mm in height, with a 2,520mm wheelbase. The front-wheel-drive electric vehicle is powered by a motor producing 47kW, or approximately 63 horsepower, and 160Nm of torque. Buyers can choose between two lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery packs with capacities of 22.4kWh and 35.84kWh. Depending on the selected battery, the Racco delivers a claimed driving range of 210km to 320km. The maximum figure is based on Japan’s WLTC testing cycle. Compact Design for Urban Mobility Inside, the Racco accommodates four occupants and offers 280 litres of luggage capacity. Its minimum turning radius of 4.8 metres is intended to make manoeuvring through narrow streets and crowded urban areas easier. With its compact footprint, electric powertrain and multiple battery configurations, the BYD Racco adds another option to the growing small-EV segment as the company extends the model beyond its home market.

artigo.texto: BYD’s Shark plug-in hybrid pick-up has secured a maximum five-star safety rating from Euro NCAP, strengthening its position as a technology-packed alternative to conventional pick-up trucks. The result highlights the model’s crash protection, child safety features and advanced driver assistance systems as BYD continues expanding its European vehicle lineup. The BYD Shark DMO achieved strong results across all four Euro NCAP assessment categories, including an 86% score for Child Occupant Protection and 87% for Safety Assist. The pick-up also recorded 82% for Adult Occupant Protection and 74% for Vulnerable Road User Protection. The rating follows an earlier assessment by Australasian safety organisation ANCAP, supplemented by additional evaluations from Euro NCAP. Euro NCAP highlighted the Shark’s performance in several crash tests, including frontal-offset, full-width frontal and side-impact evaluations. The model also demonstrated effective protection for child occupants, with positive results for the 6- and 10-year-old child dummies in side-impact testing. Another notable feature is the child presence detection system, which can warn the driver if it detects that a child may have been left inside the vehicle. The Shark’s driver assistance technology also contributed to its five-star result. Its autonomous emergency braking system performed well when responding to cyclists and showed a good response to motorcyclists, helping the pick-up achieve its 74% score for Vulnerable Road User Protection. In the Safety Assist category, Euro NCAP recognised the effectiveness of the emergency braking system in responding to other vehicles, alongside the lane-departure support system and speed assistance technology. The latter can automatically adjust the speed limiter based on detected local speed limits. Beyond its safety credentials, the BYD Shark is designed to combine the practicality of a traditional work truck with the efficiency and comfort associated with electrified SUVs. Its Super Hybrid DMO powertrain combines two electric motors with a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine. The front electric motor produces 231PS and 310Nm of torque, while the rear motor delivers 204PS and 340Nm. Combined system output reaches 436PS and 650Nm of torque, allowing the Shark to accelerate from 0 to 62mph in 5.7 seconds. A 32.2kWh BYD Blade Battery supports electric driving, with the manufacturer quoting an electric-only range of up to 90km. With a fully charged battery and a full fuel tank, the plug-in hybrid pick-up offers a combined driving range of up to 419 miles. The battery is integrated into the vehicle’s ladder-frame platform using BYD’s Cell-to-Chassis technology, which incorporates the battery into the vehicle structure. The BYD Shark features a double-cab configuration with seating for five, targeting customers who need a versatile vehicle for work, family use and outdoor activities. Its cabin includes vegan-leather upholstery, heated and ventilated front seats, and a 12-speaker Dynaudio sound system. Technology highlights include a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster, a head-up display and a 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen with navigation, voice assistance, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Additional equipment includes a 50W wireless smartphone charger, remote cabin heating and cooling through the BYD app, keyless entry and start, and a 360-degree camera with front and rear parking sensors. The Shark also features Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) functionality, allowing external electrical devices to draw power from the vehicle through onboard power sockets. This capability adds versatility for work sites, camping trips and other outdoor activities. The Shark’s result marks the ninth five-star safety rating achieved by BYD since the brand entered the European passenger-car market in 2022, according to the company. Other BYD models recognised with five-star ratings include the Dolphin Surf, Dolphin, Seal, Seal U DM-i and Sealion 7. The latest result reinforces the brand’s emphasis on combining electrified powertrains with active safety technology and occupant protection. BYD Executive Vice President Stella Li said the result demonstrates how the company’s research and development capabilities can translate into practical benefits for customers. She also highlighted the Shark’s combination of work-ready capability, SUV-like comfort and electric driving efficiency. The BYD Shark DMO is available to order in the UK for £47,295, including VAT. With its five-star Euro NCAP rating, high-output hybrid powertrain and extensive standard equipment, the pick-up adds another electrified option to a segment traditionally dominated by diesel-powered models.

artigo.texto: Carbon market plan offers income opportunities — BBM Revenue from carbon credits could also help finance climate adaptation projects, including resilient infrastructure, water facilities and other essential services. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has issued Executive Order (eo) 127, which seeks to create income opportunities for Filipinos through environmental protection activities, including tree planting, forest conservation and pollution reduction. The order mandates the formulation of the Philippine Carbon Market Policy Framework to support the country’s climate commitments under the Paris Agreement, attract investments in green projects and establish rules for the trading of carbon credits. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said communities, farmers, businesses and other groups that help reduce pollution or absorb greenhouse gases could earn additional income through qualified environmental projects. Under the framework, eligible projects could generate carbon credits that may be sold to companies or other buyers seeking to meet their climate commitments. Recto cited communities that plant and protect trees as potential beneficiaries, since trees absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. “In other words, people can earn from planting and caring for trees, using clean energy, and engaging in other activities that help protect the environment. You will be given carbon credits for every activity proven to have reduced greenhouse gases, which can be sold,” Recto said. He stressed, however, that projects must meet government standards and undergo proper verification before qualifying for carbon credits. Registry Recto said the initiative could encourage investments in reforestation, sustainable agriculture, renewable energy and waste management while creating livelihood opportunities, particularly in rural communities. “We’re hitting two birds with one stone. The President wants to protect the environment while helping people earn more,” he said. Revenue from carbon credits could also help finance climate adaptation projects, including resilient infrastructure, water facilities and other essential services, Recto added. Under EO 127, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) will develop rules on project eligibility, carbon credit measurement and verification, and the sharing of revenues and other benefits. The DENR will also establish a Philippine National Carbon Registry to monitor carbon credits and prevent double counting and other irregularities. An interagency committee chaired by the Climate Change Commission, with the Department of Finance as vice chair, will oversee the development and implementation of the policy.

artigo.texto: A battery that costs about $3 million could end up being nearly fully offset by stacked state and federal incentives in Illinois. Larger batteries can store electricity for later use, keeping homes and businesses powered through hot summer nights, winter storms, and stretches when solar and wind output dips. Here's what to know Richardson Electronics said on October 14 that it is increasing commercial-scale battery production at its La Fox plant and plans to build a 5-megawatt storage battery there in summer 2027. The Chicago Tribune reported that company officials said no Illinois company has connected a larger battery to the grid. Richardson has global ambitions for its battery business, but executives say Illinois could become one of its biggest markets because the state aggressively subsidizes storage. Scott DuBois, who directs the company's storage operations, said stacking state incentives on top of federal tax credits leaves little of a battery's cost left to pay. Rising electricity demand, including from artificial intelligence, is adding to concerns about whether the grid will remain dependable. Matthew Tomc, Ameren's vice president for regulatory policy and energy supply, warned, "We are depending on out-of-state resources to essentially keep the lights on." He added that consumers could face seasonal price spikes, especially in summer, if the company doesn't add more power sources and storage in time. More background Commonwealth Edison customers in northern Illinois now pay about $141 a month on average, a 4% increase since 2021, according to Heatmap News and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Ameren's downstate customers pay more, averaging $224 a month, a 51% jump over five years. Storage can help because it allows utilities and communities to store electricity generated during the day and use it later, including after sunset or during weather-driven disruptions. Gil Quiniones, ComEd's chief executive, said, "If the majority of our residential, commercial, and industrial customers put in batteries, that's going to be a big win for the state." He added, "It could increase the capacity utilization for the grid we've already paid for, and have a chance to really put downward pressure on prices for everybody." The technology affects climate goals, monthly bills, and resilience during outages. Illinois is also starting far behind. Cleanview, a market research company in Henderson, Colorado, said Texas has 18 gigawatts of utility-scale battery storage, California has 16 gigawatts, and Illinois has just 102 megawatts. What's being done? Richardson describes its approach as specialized engineering work rather than mass production. Instead of chasing the biggest utility projects, the company plans to focus on customized microgrid systems, local energy networks that can power nearby users directly or trade electricity with the regional grid. An early battery order came from an Alaska microgrid that serves seven remote communities. The company also said its railroad locomotive battery packs helped shape its utility-scale storage technology. Richardson also struck a deal in May to handle engineering and marketing for the batteries Gotion builds at both the utility and neighborhood scale. Gotion runs a $2 billion factory in Manteno, Illinois. For its largest systems, the two companies start with roughly 4,500 battery cells, sealed together with cooling and control equipment inside a container about the size of a 20-foot shipping container. State planning is moving in parallel. Consultants to the Illinois Power Agency and other state agencies said that by 2045, the ComEd service area would need 12 gigawatts of battery storage capable of running four hours, while the Ameren region would need 8 gigawatts. The agencies are set to release a draft Integrated Resource Plan on November 16 that will address how Illinois can meet growing demand while staying on track with its clean-energy goals. Illinois' challenge is getting much bigger, not smaller. Nathan Miller, a consultant working with regulators on the Integrated Resource Plan, said, "For Illinois to meet its broader decarbonization goals across sectors, we need to be in a growth mode here. The system needs to get bigger." Where can I learn more? As utilities and homeowners weigh battery storage, the economics and reliability picture is changing fast. The articles below cover home-battery incentives, large solar-plus-storage projects, grid-scale build-outs, and financing that cuts upfront costs. • In Connecticut, home batteries gained a major edge as rooftop-solar incentives hit new caps. • In Nevada, the Gemini project pairs vast solar generation with batteries outside Las Vegas. • Across the United States, grid batteries are reshaping when wind and solar power reach customers. • In Idaho, utilities are building the state's largest battery to steady the grid. • With Palmetto financing, homeowners can now get backup batteries installed without upfront payments. artigo.texto: O desenvolvimento dos mercados de carbono e das regulamentações sobre a divulgação de informações climáticas está a impor exigências crescentes à medição, ao controlo e à verificação dos dados de emissões. Na União Europeia (UE), as entidades abrangidas pelo Sistema de Comércio de Emissões da UE (SCE) devem monitorizar e reportar as emissões anualmente e submeter-se a verificações regulamentares para cumprirem as suas obrigações de quotas. Entretanto, o Mecanismo de Ajustamento de Carbono na Fronteira (MBCF) exige a comunicação das emissões contidas em determinados bens importados, obrigando as empresas não só a realizar inventários de emissões a nível local, como também a identificar dados para cada produto individualmente. No Vietnã, o roteiro para o desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono está gradualmente concretizando os requisitos de gestão de emissões. A Decisão nº 232/QD-TTg, sobre o roteiro para o desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono nacional, fornece uma base para a implementação de mecanismos relacionados a cotas de emissão e negociação de carbono. Em particular, em 9 de fevereiro de 2026, o Primeiro-Ministro emitiu a Decisão nº 263/QD-TTg sobre as cotas piloto totais de emissão de gases de efeito estufa para 2025 e 2026 para 110 instalações nos setores de energia térmica, siderurgia e cimento. Esses desenvolvimentos significam que as emissões de gases de efeito estufa não são mais apenas uma questão de gestão ambiental, mas estão cada vez mais ligadas aos custos, obrigações e eficiência operacional das empresas. Nesse contexto, a contabilidade de carbono desempenha um papel crucial na conexão dos dados de emissões com os sistemas de informação contábil, auxiliando as empresas no controle de custos, na avaliação dos impactos financeiros e no aumento da transparência nos relatórios. Conectar os dados de emissão ao sistema de contabilização de carbono. O primeiro desafio da contabilização de carbono é garantir que os dados de emissões sejam completos, consistentes e verificáveis. Para atender a esse requisito, as empresas precisam identificar claramente a fonte das emissões, o escopo da medição, os métodos de cálculo e as responsabilidades de cada departamento no processo de coleta e agregação de dados. Se as informações entre produção, gestão ambiental e contabilidade forem inconsistentes ou carecerem de fundamento, as empresas enfrentarão dificuldades para determinar os custos de carbono, preparar relatórios e demonstrar a conformidade com as regulamentações pertinentes. No entanto, a contabilização de carbono vai além da simples medição e agregação de emissões. Os dados de carbono precisam ser comparados com informações sobre matérias-primas, consumo de energia, processos de produção e custos relacionados. Com base nisso, as empresas podem identificar processos que geram emissões significativas, avaliar a eficiência dos recursos e determinar estratégias adequadas de redução de emissões. Quando integradas a um sistema de contabilidade gerencial, as informações sobre carbono também auxiliam na análise de custos por produto, departamento ou processo, contribuindo para uma melhor tomada de decisão em relação a investimentos em tecnologia e organização da produção. Além da padronização de dados, o registro e a apresentação de transações relacionadas ao carbono também impõem novas exigências às práticas contábeis. Determinar como contabilizar cotas de emissão gratuitas, cotas de compra adicionais e obrigações de pagamento pode afetar o reflexo de ativos, despesas, passivos e resultados financeiros. Sem orientações adequadas ou com diferentes metodologias aplicadas pelas empresas, as informações financeiras podem apresentar inconsistências, reduzindo a comparabilidade entre empresas e entre períodos de reporte. Aprimorar a contabilização de carbono em conjunto com a transparência financeira. Para que a contabilização de carbono seja eficaz, as empresas precisam construir gradualmente um sistema de controle de dados de emissões integrado aos seus processos contábeis atuais. Isso inclui esclarecer as responsabilidades pela coleta, comparação e verificação de dados; estabelecer um mecanismo para armazenar registros rastreáveis; e fortalecer a coordenação entre os departamentos de produção, gestão ambiental, contabilidade e auditoria interna. Isso constitui a base para melhorar a confiabilidade das informações sobre emissões, minimizar discrepâncias na agregação de dados e facilitar a verificação quando necessário. Essencialmente, a contabilidade de carbono exige a integração de informações ambientais e financeiras. Enquanto os dados de emissões refletem o impacto ambiental das atividades de produção, as informações contábeis esclarecem os custos, as obrigações e as consequências econômicas associadas ao controle e à redução das emissões. Quando esses dois sistemas de informação são interligados com base em dados confiáveis e métodos de registro adequados, as empresas têm uma base sólida para melhorar a qualidade dos relatórios e desenvolver planos de produção sustentáveis.

artigo.texto: AI infrastructure plans are running into real world grid limits, as data centre projects face higher funding costs, local resistance, and questions over how much of the US build-out will actually happen. That uncertainty is shifting attention toward regulated utilities and grid-related companies that might still collect steady cash flows if power demand changes or slows. This article explains the trend and then examines 3 stocks tied to the same news shock, and why they may warrant a closer look. The companies below are only a small sample of what this grid build-out theme might mean for regulated utilities and power infrastructure, and the full screen surfaced 12 more businesses with equally compelling stories that are not covered here. Overview: Atkore manufactures electrical conduit, cable management and infrastructure products that feed into utility grid upgrades and data center build-outs worldwide. Operations: Atkore generates about US$2.1b from Electrical products and US$836 million from Safety & Infrastructure, with roughly US$2.5b of sales in the United States. Market Cap: US$3.2b Atkore matters for this theme because it supplies much of the hidden hardware that turns rising grid and data center ambition into actual powered facilities. "Robust investment in data centers, solar projects and wider nonresidential electrification continues to support demand for Atkore's metal framing, cable management and construction services. Ongoing operational improvements, including the completed closure of three United States plants and divestiture of several non core operations that are expected to provide US$10 million to US$12 million of annual cost savings, support Atkore's ability to stabilize net margins and earnings as volumes progress." artigo.texto: In recent years, one of the biggest challenges the American grid faces is maintaining reliability and stable power pricing amid massive forecasted load growth. Batteries don’t bring new generation to the grid but can store energy to reduce electricity curtailments, smooth pricing, and increase grid reliability while discharging. Utility-scale lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries have provided a great solution to gas plant ramp rates induced by the end-of-day solar reduction seen in the duck curve, as well as intra-day price smoothing. However, at only four hours of dispatch potential, these batteries are still largely incapable of providing a reliability improvement at times when power demand surges for multiple days at a time, like during a heat dome or prolonged cold front. This gap between market demands and grid infrastructure highlights the opportunity for new technology to be developed and implemented. In this Insight, we investigate the potential use and revenue of iron-air batteries within power markets by assuming a given project would have up to 100 hours of stored energy and roughly a 50% charge-discharge efficiency. Currently, all iron-air batteries planned in the United States are being developed by Form Energy, which has at least eight projects planned. Xcel Energy, a major natural gas and energy utility, has been a strong supporter of this battery technology. The company is currently set to install 32 GWh of the technology across Minnesota and Colorado, while another 11 GWh is planned for installation by other utilities across the eastern United States, including Virginia, Maine, New York, and Georgia. According to the April Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) published by Great River Energy, it expects its pilot project featuring the technology to reach commercial operations this year in Minnesota after breaking ground over two years ago. To investigate the use case of iron-air batteries, a model was developed to track the number of individual hours in which it would be profitable for an iron-air battery in a given region to charge for 100 hours followed by a consecutive 100-hour discharge given its 50% efficiency on the charge-dispatch cycle. This was done for both MISO and PJM, two ISOs with planned iron-air battery projects. Two subregions stick out as high-contrast pricing regions across the modeled charge-discharge cycles. MISO Zone 3 saw the most profitable hours under the model with 10% of all modeled hours producing revenue between January 2025 and August 2026. MISO Zone 3 is largely in Iowa, where wind can contribute to a large portion of the generation stack, making a long-duration battery useful in limiting curtailments and providing more price stability. PJM’s Dominion zone also saw higher time ranges with profits over 8%, as recent load growth in the region has resulted in higher pricing when surges in load cut deeper into the region’s reserve margins than in years past. Although the profitable trading cycles are an interesting metric, they do not cover the scale of the arbitrage opportunity, as larger pricing spreads across multiple days allow for more revenue generation. The figure below models the potential revenue for the single most profitable charge-discharge cycle each month in a given subregion within PJM and MISO and shows two interesting trends. The first trend is the seasonality of the profitability, which should come as no surprise since unpredictable spring weather patterns and high curtailments present ample opportunity to capitalize on long-duration battery storage. The other trend is the scale of the profitability in 2026 compared to the previous year, with both PJM and MISO having already doubled the maximum profitability of a given charge-discharge cycle in 2026 compared to 2025 under the model. It is worth highlighting that although the model gives some insight into a baseline charge-discharge scenario and captures the essence of long-duration energy storage, we have yet to see how these batteries function in terms of their charging habits, what levels of reserves they hold, how they rely on forecasts, and how capacity payments affect their profitability. But under the current energy market environment, these batteries stand to have their own market niche by bringing more reliability and price stability to the grid as well as making intermittent power generation a more reliable source of energy production. artigo.texto: Varroc Engineering to set up JV with French co Forsee Power to develop battery-pack solutions Synopsis Varroc Engineering has announced a joint venture with Forsee Power to develop battery-pack solutions for electric vehicles. The collaboration will begin with battery packs for three-wheelers, with plans to expand into other vehicle segments. Varroc will acquire a 45 percent stake in Forsee Power’s Indian subsidiary. This venture aims to combine expertise in battery technology and manufacturing for scalable solutions. Also Read: Gabriel India, Forvia form JV to tap Indiaâs fast-growing auto seating market Varroc will also subscribe to Optionally Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares (OCPRS) to support the joint venture, which is proposed to operate in India and is subject to applicable regulatory and corporate approvals, it added. The joint venture will initially focus on battery packs for three-wheelers, with a roadmap to address two-wheelers, light commercial vehicles, buses, trucks, off-highway and industrial vehicles, Varroc said. Also Read: Tariffs, supply risks push Indian auto parts makers to build beyond China Forsee Power India brings established expertise in battery-pack technology and systems, and Varroc contributes automotive engineering capabilities, established OEM relationships and cost-effective, world-class manufacturing expertise, the company said. Forsee Power specialises in battery systems for commercial and industrial electric vehicles (light vehicles, off-highway vehicles, buses, trucks, and trains). A major player in Europe, Asia and North America, the Group designs, assembles, and supplies energy management systems based on cells. Together, the two companies aim to combine these strengths to develop battery-pack solutions adaptable to different vehicle architectures and operating conditions, while building the capabilities required to support the continued evolution and scale of electric mobility, it added. As electric mobility gathers momentum across the world, the automotive industry is entering a new phase of transformation - one that calls for technology solutions that can evolve with changing vehicle architectures, customer requirements and the growing scale of electrification, the company said. In India, this transition presents a significant opportunity to build scalable, cost-effective and application-specific solutions that support OEMs across an expanding range of vehicle segments, it said. Electric mobility is evolving and growing rapidly, thus creating new opportunities and new requirements for the automotive industry. Through this evolution, OEMs will need partners who can anticipate changes and translate them into reliable, cost-effective solutions at scale, said Arjun Jain, Whole Time Director & CEO -- Business I at Varroc. artigo.texto: SHENZHEN, China, Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BYD Energy Storage has built a comprehensive after-sales service network in a multi‑tier framework: station O&M, project centers, regional centers and global headquarters. BYD Energy Storage operates nine O&M centers globally, each spanning 2,500 square meters. Its after-sales service network covers China, Chile, South Africa, the UK, the US, Australia, Japan, Poland, and the Middle East. New service centers will open in South Africa and Bulgaria in 2027 to further expand its global service footprint. The centers deliver core functions including spare parts storage and management, batteries repair and maintenance, regional spare parts allocation, batteries recycling, and training for locally hired engineers. BYD Energy Storage's regional centers fully comply with local regulatory requirements, deliver structured workforce training and enable rapid on-site response. The professional service team comprises over 200 field engineers and more than 100 R&D specialists. The company enforces standardized service SLAs: response within 24 hours, on-site arrival within 48 hours, and fault troubleshooting within 7 days. The company's global service network has achieved widespread coverage. It forms a multi-point supply network that ensures rapid spare parts delivery worldwide. Furthermore, leveraging localized production lines, its O&M teams integrate regional resources to deliver local battery repair services, providing global customers with fast, convenient, and localized after-sales support. "Our global service footprint is tailored to our fast‑growing BESS deployments. Trustworthy after‑sales support underpins the long‑term stable operation of energy storage assets," commented Mr. He Dehong, Head of Global After-sales Service at BYD Energy Storage. Guided by its vision, empower global energy storage industry with digital and intelligent service, BYD Energy Storage's mature global O&M system strongly supports its expanding battery energy storage footprint. The company topped global BESS shipments at over 60 GWh in 2025, and has delivered more than 650 energy storage projects in total, supported by standardized, localized after-sales services for reliable asset operation. artigo.texto: O evento, presidido pela Associação Vietnamita de Energia Limpa (VCEA) e organizado em colaboração com a GG Power Joint Stock Company, teve como foco a discussão de oportunidades, desafios e soluções para o desenvolvimento de energia solar em telhados combinada com sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) no Vietnã. Em seu discurso de abertura na conferência, o Sr. Mai Duy Thien, Presidente da Associação Vietnamita de Energia Limpa (VCEA), enfatizou o papel da energia solar em telhados, combinada com sistemas de armazenamento de energia, no aumento da autossuficiência energética, e também levantou a questão do desenvolvimento da capacidade de pesquisa e produção de soluções de armazenamento de energia no país. A meta de alcançar uma taxa média de crescimento do PIB superior a 10% durante o período de 2026-2030 impõe exigências significativas ao setor energético: garantir um fornecimento de eletricidade suficiente, estável e seguro, reduzir as emissões e aumentar a autossuficiência da economia . A Resolução nº 70-NQ/TW sobre a garantia da segurança energética nacional até 2030, com uma visão para 2045, define claramente os requisitos para assegurar uma segurança energética nacional robusta; desenvolver fontes de abastecimento internas; promover energias renováveis; construir um sistema energético moderno e inteligente; e melhorar gradualmente a capacidade de produção nacional de equipamentos críticos para o setor energético. De acordo com o Sr. Thien, o desenvolvimento de capacidades tecnológicas e de produção nacionais não só contribui para a gestão proativa da cadeia de abastecimento, como também forma gradualmente um ecossistema da indústria energética vietnamita, criando uma base para o desenvolvimento a longo prazo do mercado de energia limpa. Do ponto de vista profissional e prático na indústria de eletricidade, o Dr. Vo Quang Lam, ex-vice-diretor geral do Grupo de Eletricidade do Vietnã (EVN), enfatizou a necessidade de desenvolver energia solar fotovoltaica autossuficiente em telhados, combinada com a tecnologia BESS (Building, Energy, and Service - Edifício, Energia e Serviços), ao mesmo tempo em que se aprimora a capacidade nacional de dominar a tecnologia de armazenamento de energia. Em relação aos requisitos para empresas que desejam entrar no mercado, o Sr. Lam enfatizou: "É crucial que as empresas também desenvolvam capacidades substanciais, garantindo a qualidade do produto, a segurança operacional, o serviço pós-venda a preços adequados e a competitividade a longo prazo." Na conferência, o Sr. Bui Xuan Binh, Presidente e CEO da GG Power Joint Stock Company, compartilhou sua visão, enfatizando o objetivo de aprimorar as capacidades tecnológicas, desenvolver soluções de energia limpa e consolidar gradualmente a posição das empresas vietnamitas no setor de armazenamento de energia. O Sr. Nguyen Quoc Dat, Diretor Geral Adjunto responsável pela Cadeia de Suprimentos e P&D da GG Power, apresentou as soluções de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) da empresa e sua direção de pesquisa e desenvolvimento para aumentar a capacidade de produção nacional. Assim, a estratégia de desenvolvimento da GG Power para a solução BESS "Make in Vietnam" concentra-se não apenas na fabricação de equipamentos no país, mas também inclui pesquisa e desenvolvimento, controle de qualidade, integração de sistemas e serviços técnicos. Esses são elementos cruciais para agregar valor ao produto e atender aos requisitos operacionais práticos da rede elétrica do Vietnã, bem como às necessidades de eletricidade dos consumidores locais. O consenso na conferência foi que o desenvolvimento do mercado de energia solar em telhados, em conjunto com sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), requer mecanismos e políticas adequados, bem como capacidade real das empresas em pesquisa, produção, controle de qualidade, garantia de segurança e prestação de serviços técnicos. Os delegados concentraram suas discussões e soluções propostas em três grupos de questões: Em primeiro lugar, é necessário aprimorar os mecanismos e políticas sincronizados desde o nível central até o local, criando condições mais favoráveis para que pessoas e empresas invistam e implementem energia solar em telhados para autoprodução e autoconsumo, de acordo com as necessidades de uso de eletricidade e as condições reais. Em segundo lugar, é crucial promover o desenvolvimento de produtos de armazenamento de energia "Made in Vietnam" que atendam aos requisitos de qualidade, segurança operacional, estabilidade, fornecimento proativo e garantia de longo prazo e serviço pós-venda. O aprimoramento das capacidades tecnológicas nacionais é considerado um dos principais fatores para aumentar a competitividade das empresas vietnamitas. Em terceiro lugar, precisamos construir um ecossistema abrangente de soluções, desde energia solar e inversores até sistemas de armazenamento de energia balanceada (BESS), juntamente com políticas cooperativas e apoio ao desenvolvimento de mercado para a rede de distribuição. Isso fornecerá uma base para expandir o acesso a soluções de energia limpa, melhorar a eficiência dos investimentos e criar condições para que as empresas desenvolvam seus mercados de forma sustentável. Por meio das sessões de intercâmbio, a conferência "Desenvolvendo Energia Solar em Telhados - Autoprodução, Autoconsumo e Introdução de Novos Produtos" proporcionou aos participantes a oportunidade de compartilhar perspectivas práticas, identificar questões que necessitam de maior atenção e fortalecer as conexões entre agências, associações, empresas de tecnologia, distribuidores e organizações de investimento. As propostas apresentadas servem como base para o aprimoramento de soluções, a promoção da cooperação e o desenvolvimento do mercado de energia solar em telhados combinada com armazenamento de energia no Vietnã.

artigo.texto: Indonesia has introduced new rules for carbon credit projects in farming. The regulation requires businesses to work with farmer groups and agree on how to share the benefits from these projects. It covers rice farming, livestock and plantations. The new rule explains how agricultural projects can earn carbon credits, how emissions cuts must be checked, and how farmers should take part. The Indonesian Ministry of Agriculture issued Minister of Agriculture Regulation No. 18 of 2026 on October 6. It was published on October 12 and is set to take effect three months later. The rules come as Indonesia builds its wider carbon market. Its national carbon exchange had recorded more than 1.6 million tonnes of carbon credits traded by July 2025, with a total transaction value of about US$4.7 million. More than 100 organizations had registered to use the exchange. The new agricultural rules aim to give farming projects a clearer path into this market while setting conditions for farmer participation and benefit-sharing. Opening Carbon Trading for Rice, Livestock and Plantations The new regulation covers three main parts of agriculture: rice farming, livestock and plantations. Projects can earn carbon credits by cutting greenhouse gas emissions or storing more carbon in soil and plants. Possible activities include changing how rice fields are watered, using lower-emission crop varieties, applying the right amount of fertilizer and improving the handling of crop waste and animal waste. Other options include improving soil health, planting trees and other long-living crops, restoring damaged farmland and using farming methods that protect the soil. These activities can help reduce emissions or store more carbon. For example, changing how rice fields are watered can lower methane emissions. Better soil management can also help keep carbon in the ground. Businesses, government agencies and farmer groups may take part in these projects. The rules explain how they can work together to reduce emissions and support Indonesia’s climate goals. Businesses Must Agree to Share Benefits With Farmers One of the most important parts of the regulation is its requirement for businesses to work with farmer groups. Under Article 4, businesses involved in agricultural carbon trading must work with at least three farmer organizations near the project site. The number and choice of groups must consider factors such as the size of the business’s land area and its operations. The business and the farmer groups must sign a written agreement. It must explain what each side will do, how benefits will be shared and how long the agreement will last. Farmers must also give free, prior and informed consent. In simple terms, they must receive clear information and agree to take part without pressure. The regulation does not set one fixed percentage of carbon revenue for farmers. Instead, the share must consider several factors, including: - Cost of technology, - Size of the land or business, - Amount of emissions reduced, and - Number of carbon credits generated. This means the benefit-sharing arrangement can differ from one project to another. Farmer groups can also run carbon credit projects themselves through a cooperative or another business. They may also work with outside partners that provide funding, as long as the parties agree on how to share the benefits. The rules give farmer groups a formal role in carbon projects. They are not simply expected to provide land or help carry out farming activities. Projects Must Prove Their Emissions Cuts The regulation sets out steps that projects must follow before they can receive carbon credit approval. Businesses using Indonesia’s national certification system must first submit a project plan called a Climate Change Mitigation Action Design Document, or DRAM. This document explains what the project will do, how it will reduce emissions and how the results will be measured. The plan must go through an assessment and independent review. Once the project has carried out its activities, an independent verifier must check the reported results. The business can then apply for a recommendation for an Indonesian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Certificate, known as SPE GRK. These steps are designed to make sure that carbon credits are based on real, documented and verified results. Projects using other carbon credit standards may also qualify, subject to the relevant approval process. Projects must also follow rules on social and environmental protection, public participation and legal compliance. The regulation also seeks to prevent double counting. This happens when the same emissions reduction is claimed more than once by different parties or programs. Preventing this is important because buyers need to know that a credit represents a real emissions cut or carbon removal that has not already been counted elsewhere. National Carbon Registry Sets the Path for Tracking Farm Credits Agricultural carbon projects will use Indonesia’s national carbon registry, known as the Sistem Registri Unit Karbon, or SRUK. The registry records carbon units and helps track projects and transactions. It is part of the government’s wider effort to organize the country’s carbon market. Project developers must submit the required documents and follow the rules for project review, independent checks and approval. Moreover, projects that want to transfer carbon credits for use by another country or for international purposes may need additional approval from the environment minister. This follows a recommendation from the agriculture minister. - Approval to run a project does not automatically allow its credits to be transferred internationally. Projects must meet the separate requirements that apply to those transfers. artigo.texto: TRIESTE — Leaders of the 27 European Union countries reached a compromise overnight on the European Emissions Trading System (ETS), breaking the deadlock that had blocked the European Council’s conclusions. The compromise concerns ETS2, for which the Commission is being asked to update its assessment of all impacts, with particular attention to the system’s structure and related safeguards. The wording is contained in paragraph 8 of the official conclusions of the summit held on October 15 and 16, 2026. The text does not provide for a postponement of ETS2, nor does it directly alter the system’s implementation schedule; rather, it calls on the European Commission to conduct a new review of its effects and the way it is structured. ETS2 is the new carbon market designed to cover fuels used in buildings and road transportation, with a planned launch in 2028. Unlike the traditional ETS, which directly involves industrial and energy-production facilities subject to the regulations, the new system operates upstream in the supply chain, imposing obligations on fuel suppliers. Emissions costs may therefore be passed on to the prices of gasoline, diesel, and other fossil fuels, with potential consequences for households and businesses. For the trucking industry, the most sensitive issue is the impact on diesel prices, one of the main operating cost items for trucking companies. Any increase in fuel prices could result in higher expenses for carriers, especially those operating over long distances with tight profit margins. The extent of the impact will depend on trends in the price of emissions allowances, how suppliers pass on costs throughout the supply chain, and any compensatory measures that may be implemented. In general, the mechanism does not impose a direct obligation on individual trucking companies to purchase ETS2 allowances for every liter of diesel fuel consumed. The obligations to monitor and surrender allowances fall on regulated entities that place fuels on the market. For transporters, the economic impact is therefore primarily indirect, through the price at the pump and supply contracts. The repercussions could also extend to industrial and commercial customers. If rising fuel costs were passed on to transportation rates, logistics costs for goods transported by road could increase, with consequences for production and distribution chains. Carriers’ ability to pass on these increases to customers will depend on the structure of their contracts, the presence of fuel adjustment clauses, and the level of competition in the market. For the trucking industry, this issue also comes amid a transition toward lower-emission vehicles, charging infrastructure, and alternative fuels. The rising cost of fossil fuels could strengthen the incentive to renew fleets, but it also risks placing a burden on companies that lack the necessary resources to invest quickly in new technologies. The differences in financial capacity between large operators and small and medium-sized enterprises make the issue of safeguards particularly relevant. The review requested by the European Council will focus in particular on the structure of ETS2 and its safeguard measures. The decision does not, however, amount to a suspension of the mechanism, nor does it constitute an explicit mandate to change its launch date. Any changes will require further legislative action and the relevant European decision-making process. This issue is part of the broader debate on energy costs and the competitiveness of European industry. In paragraph 11 of the conclusions, the leaders call for a well-functioning, transparent, and predictable carbon market; for effective measures to combat the carbon leakage of CO₂ emissions; and for a reduction in carbon price volatility. The goal is also to mitigate the impact of carbon price volatility on electricity prices, without compromising the role of the ETS in the climate and energy transition. The text therefore has a twofold objective: on the one hand, to preserve the price signal on emissions, which is seen as a tool to stimulate investment and innovation; on the other hand, to limit the effects of market fluctuations and safeguard the competitiveness of European companies. The European Council also calls on the co-legislators to accelerate work on the market stability reserve, with the aim of mitigating excessive volatility in allowance prices. With regard to immediate measures to address high energy prices, the leaders are calling for a coordinated European response based on targeted and temporary measures, tailored to the circumstances of individual member states and consistent with the preservation of the single market. The conclusions welcome the Commission’s intention to extend the temporary state aid framework for the most vulnerable industrial sectors, develop a short-term framework to improve the capacity and efficiency of European refineries, and promote the voluntary aggregation of energy demand. The Commission is also invited to consider additional measures, if necessary, to address the surge in prices in the short term. However, no specific decision to postpone ETS2 is mentioned: the political agreement reached at the summit concerns updating the impact assessment, while the conclusions confirm the need to address volatility and the economic consequences of the carbon market. The compromise was reached after a day of discussions among the governments on energy policies and competitiveness. According to accounts of the negotiations,Italy, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, joined the Visegrád Group countries—Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia—in insisting on the need to reexamine the effects of ETS2. The official text confirms the inclusion of the request to update the assessment, but does not explicitly attribute the initiative to individual states. days
