artigo.texto: At an Oct. 13 meeting on a proposed data center, more than 200 residents crowded into Elizabeth Forward Middle School's auditorium in Elizabeth Township, Pa. Opposition emerged, petitions circulated, and Elizabeth Township officers escorted one attendee out after a disturbance. Here's what to know Commissioners were first approached in June about locating a possible data center at a power plant site, and the gathering at Elizabeth Forward Middle School was the township's first public move since then, according to the Mon Valley Independent. About 330 questions were submitted beforehand, and township resident Eric Piper condensed them into roughly four dozen for the discussion. According to the Mon Valley Independent, Bucks County developer Tim Hendricks, who said he has 35 years in real estate, is looking at a 550-acre Henderson Road site in the Buena Vista area next to the Youghiogheny River. Preliminary concepts presented at the meeting included 20 two-story buildings and stormwater basins. Hendricks said the development might generate $125 million in tax revenue for the township and school district and create 200 to 300 permanent jobs with salaries ranging from $60,000 to $100,000, according to the Mon Valley Independent. He also said residents' energy service would stay the same and that the facility would not emit pollutants. Key details were still unavailable. Asked by Commissioner Jim Benedek about expected electricity and water use, Hendricks said he did not want to offer figures until he had dependable information, according to the Mon Valley Independent. Residents also disputed the claim that nearby homes would be about 2,000 feet away, saying some properties across the river sit closer than that. More background To illustrate the site's scale, Piper said the property is about 2.5 times the size of Kennywood Park, while Hendricks said, according to the Mon Valley Independent, "There's hundreds of acres proposed that would not be built on out of the total. This is an evolving process. Things change as we get more information. As I start to get answers, we can update the plan to make it more usable and hopefully better for the community." Hendricks said he learned about the property from a colleague's brother, who had been exploring it for a possible solar project. He added that existing utility lines and earlier environmental cleanup made the site more appealing for redevelopment, according to the Mon Valley Independent. The debate arrives amid broader concerns about data centers, artificial intelligence, and pressure on the electric grid. Hendricks told the audience that people often view data centers only through the lens of AI, but said they also support ordinary online activity such as texting and streaming movies. Data centers can add computing capacity that helps optimize cleaner energy systems. Residents and local officials often focus on the tradeoffs, including heavy electricity demand, significant water use, security concerns, and the possibility that large new loads could strain local infrastructure and utility bills. Residents pressed environmental and quality-of-life concerns. Resident Candy Woy raised questions about wildlife at the site and possible environmental effects, while Mary Jane Carnahan, who identified herself as a Terrytown Drive neighbor, said underground mines and prolonged construction could disrupt daily life and reduce property values, according to the Mon Valley Independent. What's being done? For now, Hendricks said, the proposal is still at a very early stage. As of Oct. 13, nothing formal had been filed, and he said the concept would need many permits and approvals before it could move ahead, according to the Mon Valley Independent. He added that if construction ever happens, the eventual company behind the site would step into his role. According to the Mon Valley Independent, Hendricks said he is trying to place any data center as far from homes as possible and is still talking with gas providers while deciding whether the project fits the community. He told residents the plans would be revised further if the process continues. Residents are organizing their own response. Attendees signed anti-project petitions on the way in, and Megan McDonough, state director at Food and Water Watch, questioned whether public opposition would matter if commissioners were later asked to change zoning, according to the Mon Valley Independent. Protect Elizabeth Township has another town hall set for 6:30 p.m. Oct. 29 at Butler's Golf Course on Rock Run Road, featuring a speaker panel and opponents of data centers from other communities. Piper said, "This community is my home. My family has been in this township for nearly 100 years. I care about this community just as I know everyone in this room does. And whether you support this proposed development, oppose it or simply want to learn more, I believe we all have something in common. We want what's best for Elizabeth Township, and the people that call it home." Where can I learn more? What's happening in Elizabeth Township echoes fights in other communities over proposed data centers. artigo.texto: A homeowner who wanted to increase their home battery storage capacity was worried when their provider said they could only combine their existing system with another brand's technology. "Are there problems I should expect with that kind of setup?" they asked. Here's what to know In Reddit's r/FranklinWH, the homeowner explained that the provider that installed their existing battery storage was now only installing Tesla products, but they already had a Franklin system. "I was a bit confused, because they are still listed as a Franklin distributor/contractor, on their own website," they shared. That disconnect made them feel "extremely dubious." Complicating matters, they could only keep their warranties together if they agreed to let the provider incorporate a Tesla Powerwall into their current setup. Adding battery storage is one of the best ways to protect your home during outages, save money on energy, and gain more energy independence, but a mismatched configuration could undermine the system's reliability and simplicity. If you're considering your options, explore EnergySage to learn about home battery storage and obtain competitive installation estimates. EnergySage has teamed up with electrification brand Qmerit to help homeowners get the best price on home battery storage solutions. What can be done? Instead of taking their original provider's word at face value, commenters advised the OP to shop around. One warned that configuring two different types of tech could be like trying to mix oil and water. "Find another installer," they said. Others said to find a certified Franklin installer and read their installation contract closely. "Why would using someone else to add another Franklin to your system change your existing warranty?" one person wondered. Another said: "If you switch to another certified installer, their warranty usually stays intact. (Do verify with them first)." For people who aren't ready for a whole-home backup system, Pila's plug-and-play batteries cost a fraction of what a whole-home backup system would. Where can I learn more? artigo.texto: The training was attended by both representatives of enterprises and staff from the Environment Agency and the Environmental Protection Inspectorate. The former learnt about calculation and reporting rules, whilst the latter learnt methods for subsequently verifying the accuracy of the data submitted. The event was organised jointly with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Moldova as part of the project ‘Strengthening Capacity for Climate Action in the Republic of Moldova’, funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF). How businesses are to report on emissions During the seminar, participants were introduced to the main stages of preparing annual reports: collecting the necessary information, conducting an internal check at the enterprise, having the report reviewed by an accredited verifier, and submitting the document to the Environment Agency. Particular attention was paid to identifying emission sources and the corresponding source streams, as well as selecting measurement equipment and monitoring methodologies. This data is essential for developing greenhouse gas monitoring plans. Participants were also introduced to current regulations and national guidelines explaining how to complete the documents. The seminar thus covered not only the preparation of reports but also the creation of a system for collecting and verifying data, which will enable the comparison of companies’ performance indicators and the verification of the accuracy of calculations. ETS: the next stage of climate regulation Preparing businesses is seen as one of the steps towards the subsequent introduction of an emissions trading scheme (ETS). Such schemes involve regulating greenhouse gas emissions within set limits and establishing a mechanism for trading emissions allowances. For industry, this means establishing emissions accounting processes in advance, designating responsible staff and ensuring the reliability of source data. In future, monitoring and reporting requirements may become a key part of compliance with climate legislation and the planning of production costs. Such preparation is of particular importance for energy-intensive sectors, including the cement, glass and sugar industries, as well as energy sector enterprises, as mentioned by the seminar organisers. For Moldovan businesses, the key issues are the timeline for implementing the future mechanism, the specific requirements for regulated enterprises, and the potential impact of climate regulation on production costs and competitiveness. artigo.texto: The prime ministers of Sweden, Finland and Denmark oppose plans to relax EU carbon market requirements, warning that the move could put industrial investment at greater risk and slow emissions reductions. A letter from the three Nordic leaders was sent to the Council of the European Union on October 14. The recipients were Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen, Sweden’s Ulf Kristersson and Finland’s Petteri Orpo said the EU’s emissions trading system (ETS) must retain its ambition and credibility. The scheme requires the most polluting industries to pay for the carbon dioxide they emit. Diluting the rules, they warned, “would undermine the predictability on which investment decisions depend” and could hinder efforts to decarbonise industry. The three leaders also argued that easing requirements for heavy emitters would shift the burden to other sectors of the economy, forcing them to make steeper emissions cuts to ensure the EU meets its climate goals.

artigo.texto: (The Center Square) – Companies operating data centers should be the ones that pay for upgrades to the electric grid, most voters say according to a new poll. The Center Square Voters’ Voice Poll found that 66% of voters believe that data center companies should be paying for the increased power demand and infrastructure required to get that electricity to the data centers. Fourteen percent of those registered to vote say the costs of the upgrades should be shared by both data center companies and the public while 8% believe the upgrades are the responsibility of federal, state or local taxpayers and 6% believe that all electricity customers should pay for the upgrades. Another 6% said they were unsure who should pay. The results come from a survey conducted by Noble Predictive Insights from Oct. 5-7 that polled registered voters nationally via opt-in online panel and text-to-web cell phone messages. The sample included 2,527 respondents comprised of 1,011 Republicans, 1,011 Democrats, and 505 Independents. Among independent voters, 220 respondents were classified as true independents, which are individuals who do not lean toward either major party when given the choice. The margin of error is +/- 1.95%. The cost of electricity infrastructure to power data centers has been debated across the country as more energy sources are required as well as new transmission lines and power storage equipment. The U.S. House of Representatives nearly unanimously passed the Ratepayer Protection Act in September before it failed in the Senate on a 57-43 vote. The bill would have required state public utility commissioners “commence consideration” of implementing rules that would protect ordinary ratepayers within one year of the bill becoming law. President Donald Trump announced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge along with several hyper-scale data operators in 2025 with a goal of preventing Americans from paying for rising electricity costs associated with increased demand from data centers. The pledge states that companies including Amazon, xAI, Oracle, Microsoft, Meta, Google and OpenAI will pay for the new electricity generation and grid infrastructure needed to accommodate new data centers.

artigo.texto: Empreendimento no Porto Seco posiciona a região no mapa nacional da infraestrutura de dados O empresário Henrique Reis, de 29 anos e CEO da Wascer, lidera como sócio o primeiro data center do Sul de Minas, instalado no Porto Seco de Varginha. Inaugurado em setembro de 2025 com previsão de R$ 23 milhões em investimentos ao longo de dois anos, o projeto insere o município na rota nacional de processamento e conectividade. A iniciativa visa transformar cidades do interior em polos geradores e armazenadores de dados, superando o papel tradicional de meras consumidoras digitais. Receba notícias do BlogdoMadeira no seu celular Um centro de processamento de dados opera muito além do hardware básico de computadores e servidores. A unidade integra racks, equipamentos de rede, nobreaks, geradores, monitoramento contínuo e sistemas reforçados de refrigeração para suportar a dissipação de calor ininterrupta. A estabilidade operacional depende da redundância das fontes de energia e dos canais de fibra óptica. Como os serviços sustentam bancos, plataformas corporativas e lojas online, falhas em componentes individuais não podem interromper as operações locais. A escolha de Varginha considerou a localização estratégica do município, situado entre os eixos econômicos de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Belo Horizonte. O espaço foi preparado para fornecer serviços de colocation, servidores dedicados, armazenamento e cópias de segurança para clientes regionais e nacionais. Segundo Henrique Reis, a interiorização da tecnologia comprova que projetos de alta complexidade e profissionais qualificados não dependem exclusivamente das capitais. O avanço desses projetos no interior requer a combinação entre fornecimento elétrico estável, rotas de telecomunicações diversificadas e formação técnica qualificada. O Brasil concentra cerca de 200 data centers em operação, liderando o setor na América Latina e ocupando o 12º posto no ranking global. Projeções técnicas apontam que o setor movimentará entre R$ 60 bilhões e R$ 100 bilhões em novos aportes em infraestrutura no país até 2030. O consumo energético é o principal vetor para a viabilidade desses empreendimentos. Levantamentos apontam que a demanda por conexões eletrointensivas alcançará 54,2 GW até 2038, reforçando a importância de planejamento estrutural integrado para garantir sustentabilidade ao setor tecnológico. artigo.texto: North Huntingdon officials are considering passing an ordinance to govern the development of data centers that would be permitted in 20 sites in the 27-square mile township. The township commissioners Thursday decided the proposed 16-page ordinance needs revisions regarding the size of data centers. They plan to revisit the issue in November. The proposed ordinance would permit the data centers on a 10-acre parcel with setbacks of 500 feet from the property line, as a conditional use on land zoned for industrial purposes, as well as parcels designated as planned economic development districts 1 and 2. The ordinance was developed by the township solicitor in conjunction with the municipality’s engineers. Township Commissioner Ron Zona said he would want language in the ordinance that would address smaller data centers, possibly those less than 20,000 square feet, as well as larger ones. Board Chair Commissioner Zachary Haigis said he is comfortable with the draft ordinance as proposed. Township Solicitor Ashley Puchalski said the language in the ordinance must not exclude the development of data centers. Any data center also would have to be 1,500 feet from any school, daycare center, hospital, nursing facility and place of worship. The developer would need the township’s approval of a land development plan, as well as all applicable building permits, Department of Environmental Protection permits, as well as any other state and local permits. The ordinance addresses the issue of how much power a data center would use by requiring a qualified professional to document electricity demand. An expert also must document water demand on an average daily basis and identify the source for water to address an issue regarding water usage that data center opponents have raised. Like data center ordinances passed by other municipalities, North Huntingdon’s regulations would set requirements for decommissioning a data center, including removing buildings when it becomes inactive. A bond must be obtained to cover the estimated decommissioning costs and the cost to restore the site. By passing the ordinance in November, a public hearing could be held in 2027, Puchalski said. If approved by the township commissioners, North Huntingdon would join East Huntingdon, Hempfield, Ligonier, Rostraver, Sewickley and South Huntingdon townships in setting rules to govern data center development. Upper Burrell already has a data center at the former Alcoa Technology Center that’s operated by TECfusions. The Upper Burrell supervisors are scheduled to vote on a data center ordinance Thursday, Oct. 22, but that ordinance would pertain to future development, not the data center currently in operation. A Department of Environmental Protection website on data centers shows the TECfusions data center, where a 3-gigawatt power plant is planned, is the only data center in the county that is under review by environmental regulators. In South Huntingdon, a Sewickley developer, TriEnergy Inc., has applied for a land use permit for a $25 million project that would contain a data center within a 1 million square-foot warehouse to be built on a former farm along Route 31, east of the intersection with Interstate 70. DEP has yet to approval a sewage permit for the project, so the township has not reviewed a land development plan submitted in May.

artigo.texto: Setores de tecnologia, energia e indústria cobram decreto para colocar programa de incentivos em funcionamento. Divergências sobre fontes energéticas e equipamentos ainda dificultam a regulamentação. Uma coalizão de 32 entidades empresariais, com apoio de nove frentes parlamentares, cobra do governo federal a regulamentação imediata do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata). Segundo reportagem do Capital Digital, publicada em 15 de outubro de 2026, os representantes dos setores de energia, tecnologia, infraestrutura e indústria enviaram uma carta ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. O grupo defende a publicação do decreto mesmo diante de divergências técnicas sobre as condições do programa. Empresas querem acelerar incentivos para data centers no Brasil O Redata surgiu para estimular investimentos em infraestrutura digital, especialmente em instalações utilizadas para inteligência artificial, computação em nuvem e armazenamento de dados. - Desde 29 de setembro, órgãos do governo Trump são obrigados a trocar inteligência artificial por superinteligência em documentos oficiais, mas a ordem não vale para empresas e professor da UFPE vê estratégia de marketing - Mais de 34 mil satélites e detritos circulam na órbita baixa da Terra, enquanto previsão de novos lançamentos amplia preocupação com colisões entre objetos que viajam a 28 mil km/h - Átomos próximos do zero absoluto ajudam a testar Einstein no mundo quântico, e resultado confirma previsão sobre queda livre sem resolver o mistério da natureza da gravidade na física moderna - Interruptores iluminados, sensores e dimmers podem explicar por que seu LED continua aceso mesmo desligado, mas o brilho residual não permite diagnosticar sozinho a causa presente no circuito da iluminação O governo sancionou a Lei nº 15.504 em 15 de setembro de 2026, criando o regime especial de tributação. Entretanto, sua operacionalização depende de regras complementares. Por isso, as entidades defendem que o Executivo publique inicialmente as condições essenciais do programa. Depois, questões mais complexas poderiam passar por regulamentações específicas e consultas públicas. Segundo os representantes empresariais, a indefinição dificulta o planejamento financeiro de novos empreendimentos e reduz a previsibilidade para investidores. Além disso, os data centers exigem grandes quantidades de eletricidade para manter servidores, sistemas de refrigeração e equipamentos de processamento em funcionamento. Esse consumo já influencia decisões internacionais. Em reportagem do CPG, Roberta Souza mostrou como o Google contratou 396 MW de energia geotérmica para abastecer sua expansão de data centers nos Estados Unidos. Gás natural está no centro das divergências sobre energia Um dos principais pontos de discussão envolve as fontes energéticas aceitas para atender às exigências do Redata. As entidades defendem a chamada neutralidade tecnológica, permitindo que os empreendimentos utilizem diferentes alternativas de fornecimento. A lista apresentada pelo grupo inclui energia solar, eólica, hidrelétrica, biomassa, biogás, biometano, energia nuclear e gás natural. O argumento é que os data centers precisam de eletricidade contínua, inclusive durante períodos de baixa geração solar ou eólica. Entretanto, a inclusão do gás natural provoca discussões sobre os critérios de sustentabilidade. Embora possa oferecer geração firme, o combustível fóssil produz emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Segundo reportagem da CNN Brasil, publicada em setembro, representantes do setor de gás demonstraram preocupação com a possibilidade de exclusão dessa fonte dos incentivos. Além disso, a coalizão afirma que os custos adicionais de geração e transmissão associados aos novos data centers não devem ser transferidos aos demais consumidores. O debate ocorre enquanto o gás natural atrai investimentos no país. Em matéria do CPG, foi apresentado um projeto de quatro termelétricas na Bahia, com investimento estimado em R$ 900 milhões. Equipamentos e impostos também dificultam a regulamentação Além da energia, as entidades questionam possíveis restrições à relação de equipamentos beneficiados pelos incentivos tributários. Embora apoiem o desenvolvimento da indústria nacional, argumentam que uma lista excessivamente limitada pode dificultar a aquisição de componentes necessários aos projetos. Outro pedido envolve o Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (ICMS). O grupo quer que o governo federal discuta com os estados, no âmbito do Confaz, um tratamento tributário compatível com o Redata. Essas questões ganham importância porque grandes centros de processamento dependem de infraestrutura elétrica, sistemas de refrigeração e equipamentos especializados. Em outra reportagem do CPG, detalhou-se um projeto que combina energia solar e 380 MWh de baterias para atender à demanda energética de data centers. Por enquanto, a carta representa uma reivindicação dos setores empresariais, não uma decisão do governo. Também não há confirmação, na reportagem original, de uma data definitiva para a publicação do decreto. Assim, o impasse do Redata evidencia um desafio para o Brasil: atrair investimentos em inteligência artificial e infraestrutura digital sem deixar de considerar os custos da eletricidade, a segurança do abastecimento e as metas ambientais.

artigo.texto: Parcerias Colt DCS e RMZ iniciam a construção de data center de 64 MW em Mumbai, preparado para IA Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google A Colt Data Centre Services (Colt DCS), provedora global de data centers preparados para IA, hiperescaláveis e voltados a grandes empresas, e a RMZ, plataforma indiana de ativos reais de capital fechado, anunciaram em 15 de outubro de 2026 o início da construção do Mumbai 3, um data center de 64 MW preparado para IA no campus das parceiras em Navi Mumbai, na Índia. O primeiro cliente hiperescalável da instalação já foi contratado, e as empresas afirmaram que o data center está totalmente pré-alugado. A preparação do terreno começou em dezembro de 2025, e a construção está em andamento após a assinatura do contrato com o cliente. As empresas descreveram o início da construção como um marco que demonstra o ritmo de expansão da joint venture nos 18 meses desde sua assinatura. Investimento da joint venture e capacidade do campus O Mumbai 3 está sendo desenvolvido no âmbito da joint venture que a Colt DCS e a RMZ anunciaram em 2024 para investir US$ 1,7 bilhão no mercado indiano de data centers. Por meio da joint venture, as parceiras se comprometeram a desenvolver 250 MW de capacidade de data centers em Mumbai e Chennai. O Mumbai 3 será integrado às instalações existentes Mumbai 1 e Mumbai 2, no campus de Navi Mumbai, que atualmente atende a grandes empresas e cargas de trabalho em nuvem. O campus tem potencial para oferecer até 148 MW de capacidade quando estiver totalmente desenvolvido e, após a conclusão, o Mumbai 3 elevará a capacidade operacional do local para 86 MW, segundo as empresas. Projetado para cargas de trabalho de IA de alta densidade O Mumbai 3 foi projetado para atender a cargas de trabalho de IA e implantações de computação de alta densidade, com 64 MW de potência contratada garantida. A instalação usa uma arquitetura híbrida de refrigeração que combina o resfriamento a ar tradicional com o resfriamento líquido direto no chip. Uma subestação GIS de 220 kV localizada no campus oferece resiliência e escalabilidade, e o local dispõe de conectividade neutra em relação às operadoras, com acesso a rotas de fibra óptica de alta capacidade. Pratap Mane, responsável pela Colt DCS na Índia, afirmou que a demanda por data centers está evoluindo rapidamente, com clientes que precisam de implantações maiores, maior densidade de racks e infraestrutura capaz de atender a cargas de trabalho de IA cada vez mais intensivas. Ele disse que o Mumbai 3 foi concebido desde o início para estar preparado para IA, incorporando refrigeração líquida e infraestrutura elétrica reforçada para atender a implantações de alta densidade, e que isso permite aos clientes ampliar com eficiência as cargas de trabalho de IA de próxima geração e de computação de alto desempenho, mantendo a resiliência e a eficiência operacionais. Acrescentou que a instalação fortalece o campus de Navi Mumbai como uma plataforma escalável e preparada para o futuro de infraestrutura digital. Energia renovável e criação de empregos A instalação funcionará com 100% de energia renovável, afirmaram as empresas, e seu sistema de refrigeração em circuito fechado foi projetado para gerar quase nenhum efluente no processo de resfriamento. A expectativa é que o projeto crie mais de 700 empregos na construção e na operação, além de apoiar fornecedores, empreiteiros e prestadores de serviços locais. As empresas disseram que essas medidas refletem o compromisso conjunto de oferecer infraestrutura digital sustentável, que gere valor duradouro para as comunidades locais e a região como um todo. Deepak Chhabria, presidente da RMZ Infrastructure, afirmou que o campus foi projetado para permitir que provedores hiperescaláveis e de neocloud ampliem suas operações à medida que evoluem suas necessidades de capacidade e computação, reunindo escala, resiliência e rapidez de entrada no mercado. Ele disse que o investimento reforça o compromisso da RMZ com a construção de infraestrutura avançada de data centers e IA que atenda aos padrões globais e às demandas em rápida evolução da economia digital. A joint venture de 2024 A Colt DCS e a RMZ anunciaram a joint venture em 19 de novembro de 2024, como uma parceria em partes iguais voltada ao desenvolvimento de infraestrutura digital no mercado indiano. Na ocasião, as empresas disseram que o investimento se concentraria inicialmente em acelerar o desenvolvimento de locais existentes em Navi Mumbai e Ambattur, Chennai, com a inclusão de um terceiro local no futuro, e que os data centers teriam capacidade combinada de aproximadamente 250 MW após a conclusão de todas as fases. O anúncio de 2024 afirmou que a Colt DCS trazia 25 anos de experiência no desenvolvimento e na operação de data centers em mercados de primeira linha na Europa, no Japão e na Índia, e que a joint venture aceleraria a oferta de nova capacidade para clientes na Índia, aproveitando as relações de longo prazo da RMZ com parceiros da cadeia de suprimentos e seus clientes da lista Fortune India 500. Na assinatura, Niclas Sanfridsson, então diretor-executivo da Colt DCS, classificou a Índia como um país estratégico para os planos de crescimento da operadora, e Chhabria, então diretor-executivo da RMZ Infrastructure, descreveu a infraestrutura digital como um pilar do futuro econômico da Índia.

artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data Announces Plan for its askROI Subsidiary to Go Public in the Second or Third Quarter of 2027 askROI Offers an All-in-One Platform Featuring More Than 240 Productivity Tools, Generative AI, Business Automation and Advanced AI Research LAS VEGAS , Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that its subsidiary, askROI, Inc. ("askROI"), an AI technology company, is preparing to become a separate, publicly traded company, whether through a reverse takeover ("RTO"), an initial public offering of askROI's securities ("IPO"), or through the use of a special purpose acquisition company (a "SPAC" and collectively with the RTO and the IPO, a "Transaction"). artigo.texto: Premier Energies is advancing its planned 12 GWh BESS manufacturing agreement with RCT with a shareholders’ agreement The initial 6 GWh phase is expected to become operational in FY2027–28 RCT Nexor Energy can acquire a 15% stake in the JV in four tranches linked to project milestones, with an option to acquire an additional 5% India’s Premier Energies Limited has finalized a shareholders’ agreement for a joint venture (JV) to establish a 12 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS) manufacturing facility in Telangana. The agreement was signed between Premier Battery Technologies Private Limited (PBTPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Premier Energies; Premier Energies Storage Solutions Private Limited (PESSPL), the JV company; and RCT Nexor Energy Private Limited, part of Germany’s RCT Group. The facility is planned to come up in Seetharampur, Telangana, with an initial capacity of 6 GWh expected to be established in FY2027-28. The duo signed a binding term sheet for the facility in September 2026 (see India Solar PV News Snippets). The proposed facility will manufacture and assemble BESS for residential, small business, commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. Under the agreement, RCT Nexor Energy will have the right to acquire a 15% stake in the JV through four tranches linked to project milestones. It will also have the option to acquire an additional 5% equity stake for cash consideration at the end of the first phase, subject to the agreement’s terms. The JV’s board will comprise two nominees from PBTPL and one from RCT Nexor Energy. With this joint venture, solar cell and module manufacturer Premier Energies will enter BESS manufacturing, targeting both domestic and international markets. The company recently announced that it secured new orders worth INR 4,001 crore in Q2 FY2027 (July-September 2026). The orders cover 2,308 MW of solar cell and module supplies, along with EPC projects. It said the orders came from power producers, module manufacturers, EPC companies, and other customers, excluding the retail segment. Premier Energies’ module manufacturing capacity has nearly doubled to 11.1 GW, while its solar cell capacity has increased to 10.6 GW following the commissioning of a 7 GW TOPCon cell manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh (see Premier Energies Commissions India’s ‘Largest’ Solar Cell Fab).

artigo.texto: Na manhã de 18 de outubro, a Ucrânia lançou um ataque com drones em grande escala, visando uma instalação petrolífera, um centro de dados e uma ponte na cidade de São Petersburgo, localizada no noroeste da Rússia. A mídia russa noticiou que drones atacaram o porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo e o centro de dados do VKontakte, empresa que opera a maior rede social do país. O governador Aleksandr Beglov confirmou que um incêndio deflagrou na zona portuária do petróleo e em várias instalações civis em quatro distritos da cidade. As equipas de resgate atuaram imediatamente no combate às chamas e, até ao momento, não foram registadas vítimas. O incidente também afetou diversos voos no Aeroporto Internacional de Pulkovo. Na província de Leningrado, que circunda São Petersburgo, o governador Aleksandr Drozdenko anunciou que as defesas aéreas abateram 127 drones. Os destroços danificaram quatro carros em um estacionamento e causaram vários focos de incêndio. Fontes que monitoram o conflito disseram que o ataque começou por volta das 2h50 da manhã. Imagens registradas por moradores mostraram múltiplas explosões iluminando o céu noturno sobre São Petersburgo – uma cidade de 5,6 milhões de habitantes localizada a cerca de 856 km da fronteira com a Ucrânia. Alguns vídeos mostraram drones atingindo uma ponte de oito faixas e causando um grande incêndio na área portuária. O porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo tem capacidade para receber e transportar aproximadamente 12,5 milhões de toneladas por ano por via marítima, ferroviária e rodoviária, sendo um dos maiores centros de armazenamento e exportação de combustíveis da Rússia. A fabricante ucraniana Fire Point afirma ter utilizado seu avião de ataque FP-1 nessa operação. Diversos canais de notícias locais relataram que uma subestação de energia também foi danificada, causando cortes de energia localizados e redução da pressão da água em algumas áreas. Esses ataques fazem parte da operação de longo prazo da Ucrânia para pressionar intensamente o fornecimento de combustível e a infraestrutura digital da Rússia, em meio a uma complexa e contínua troca de ataques contra a infraestrutura energética entre os dois países. artigo.texto: O mercado global de infraestrutura física de data centers movimentou US$ 14 bilhões em receitas dos fabricantes no segundo trimestre de 2026, alta de 27% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. Segundo levantamento da consultoria Dell’Oro Group, a expansão foi impulsionada pela demanda por capacidade computacional para inteligência artificial (IA), que continua superando a oferta disponível. CONTEÚDO RELACIONADO – Vertiv compra empresa europeia para ampliar serviços de refrigeração líquida O resultado mantém o mercado em uma sequência de crescimento anual superior a 20%. A desaceleração moderada em relação ao primeiro trimestre não indica enfraquecimento da demanda, mas reflete uma base de comparação mais elevada, de acordo com a consultoria. Apesar do avanço dos investimentos, a implantação de novos data centers enfrenta obstáculos relacionados à disponibilidade de energia, ao prazo de entrega de equipamentos e à resistência de comunidades locais. Para Alex Cordovil, diretor de pesquisa da Dell’Oro Group, o licenciamento e a escolha dos locais para instalação passaram a representar os principais riscos de curto prazo para a expansão do setor. A avaliação considera que os planos de investimento das grandes empresas de tecnologia continuam indicando demanda robusta, mas a obtenção de licenças e as conexões à rede elétrica tornam mais difícil prever quando os projetos entrarão em operação. Refrigeração e energia concentram investimentos Entre os segmentos analisados, o de gerenciamento térmico registrou o crescimento mais acelerado, com expansão superior a 40% na comparação anual. A participação desse segmento na receita total da infraestrutura física de data centers também igualou seu recorde histórico. O desempenho foi puxado principalmente pelas soluções de refrigeração líquida direta (Direct Liquid Cooling, ou DLC) e pelos sistemas de rejeição de calor, responsáveis por transferir o calor para fora das instalações. Essas tecnologias ganham relevância diante da densidade de potência exigida pelos servidores e aceleradores utilizados em aplicações de IA. O segmento de sistemas de alimentação ininterrupta de energia (UPS) também avançou, com crescimento de aproximadamente 20% em um ano. Os ganhos se concentraram em sistemas trifásicos de grande porte, adequados aos blocos de potência na escala de megawatts utilizados nas instalações voltadas à IA. A consultoria também destaca a evolução para projetos de média tensão e a preparação dos fornecedores para arquiteturas de distribuição elétrica em corrente contínua de 800 volts (800 VDC). Já os sistemas busway, utilizados na distribuição de energia acima dos racks, seguem como a solução preferida para alimentar clusters de IA, embora a oferta limitada esteja restringindo o atendimento à demanda. Colocation lidera entre os segmentos de clientes A Dell’Oro Group passou a dividir os clientes do mercado em cinco categorias: provedores de colocation, grandes provedores de nuvem (hyperscalers), outros provedores de nuvem, empresas de telecomunicações e empresas de outros setores. Na nova classificação, os provedores de colocation responderam pela maior parcela do mercado, seguidos pelos hyperscalers. O grupo de outros provedores de nuvem, que inclui as chamadas neoclouds e empresas especializadas em modelos de IA, apresentou o crescimento mais acelerado. Dentro dessa categoria, os provedores de nuvem especializados em inteligência artificial aproximadamente dobraram de tamanho na comparação anual. As empresas tradicionais continuaram perdendo participação no mercado de infraestrutura física. Geograficamente, a América do Norte manteve a posição central, enquanto a região da Europa, Oriente Médio e África (EMEA) registrou seu ritmo de crescimento mais acelerado desde 2021, impulsionada por projetos de colocation e iniciativas de IA soberana. Licenciamento ganha peso no planejamento dos projetos As dificuldades para aprovar e conectar novos empreendimentos à infraestrutura elétrica também passaram a influenciar as perspectivas do setor. Segundo a Dell’Oro Group, movimentos de oposição local à construção de data centers começaram a se traduzir em medidas regulatórias em diferentes estados dos Estados Unidos. Em julho, Nova Iorque estabeleceu uma moratória estadual para data centers. Em agosto, a Pensilvânia retirou esses empreendimentos de seu programa de licenciamento acelerado. No Texas, uma auditoria determinada pelo governo estadual sobre projetos na fila de conexão à rede elétrica provocou atrasos nos primeiros estudos relacionados a grandes cargas de consumo. Paralelamente, o setor de energia e refrigeração vem passando por movimentos de consolidação. Entre os negócios citados pela consultoria estão a aquisição da CoolIT Systems, especializada em refrigeração líquida, pela Ecolab, concluída em julho; o acordo da Vertiv para adquirir a UtilityInnovation Group, voltada a energia atrás do medidor e microrredes; e o acordo da SLB para comprar a fabricante de trocadores de calor Kelvion.

(NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Ault Global Commodities, Inc. ("AGC"), has successfully completed the tokenization of 5,000 troy ounces of physical silver, representing a significant milestone in the Company's strategy to bring real-world assets ("RWAs") onto blockchain-based financial infrastructure. The tokenized silver, which represents exposure to physical spot silver, has now been listed on Ault Markets, a software platform which provides access to a decentralized exchange ("DEX") operating on the Ault Blockchain. Ault Markets, the software platform ("Ault Markets"), was developed by an indirectly held wholly owned subsidiary of the Company. Trading in the tokenized silver is expected to commence within weeks. Each token represents 1 troy ounce of silver and holders of the tokens have the right to redeem tokens for delivery of physical silver in 100-token increments. All of the physical silver represented by the tokens are held in secure vaults at The Wyoming Reserve. The announcement represents an important step in the Company's previously announced strategy to combine its holdings of physical commodities with blockchain technology, creating new opportunities for the development, distribution and trading of tokenized RWAs. The successful tokenization of 5,000 troy ounces of silver represents the next stage of that strategy, moving beyond physical commodity acquisitions and effectively converting them into blockchain-based digital assets. Unlike the Company's existing holdings of other digital assets, the new tokenized silver offering is associated with a tangible underlying commodity, with its economic exposure tied to the spot silver market. The Company believes this approach creates an opportunity to connect traditional precious metals markets with the emerging decentralized financial infrastructure. On October 8, 2026, Hyperscale Data announced the launch of live, invitation-only access to the DEX through Ault Markets, with plans to introduce tokenized silver, gold, platinum and potentially other precious metals. With the initial 5,000 troy ounces of silver now tokenized and listed, the Company has achieved its first announced silver tokenization milestone. Access to the DEX through Ault Markets remains in its invitation-only beta phase, with interested eligible participants able to request access through www.AultMarkets.com. "We believe this development represents an important milestone for both AGC and the Ault Blockchain ecosystem," stated Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Earlier this year, we told our stockholders that we intended to acquire physical silver and develop the infrastructure to tokenize RWAs. We purchased the silver, established relationships for precious metals procurement and custody, launched access to a DEX and have now completed the tokenization of our initial 5,000 troy ounces of silver." Following the model of other decentralized exchanges, listing decisions and trading on the DEX are not controlled by any centralized entity. The Company intends to continue evaluating opportunities to tokenize additional precious metals and other eligible RWAs, subject to applicable legal, regulatory, custody and operational requirements. Additionally, the Company believes that increased adoption of tokenized RWAs could generate additional economic activity throughout the Ault Blockchain ecosystem, though no assurance can be given regarding future trading volumes, adoption or financial results. Further details regarding the anticipated commencement of silver trading, access requirements and additional tokenized assets are expected to be announced as the initiatives progress. artigo.texto: By Vũ Hoa HƯNG YÊN — Combining rooftop solar power with battery energy storage systems (BESS) could help Việt Nam strengthen energy security, improve electricity efficiency and ease pressure on the national grid, but policy gaps, high costs and technical requirements remain barriers to wider adoption, experts said. Speaking at a conference on self-produced and self-consumed rooftop solar power in northern province of Hưng Yên on October 16, Mai Duy Thiện, chairman of the Việt Nam Clean Energy Association (VCEA), said the country’s target of average annual GDP growth of more than 10 per cent in 2026-30 would require sufficient, stable and safe electricity supplies. Resolution No 70-NQ/TW on national energy security and Government Directive No 10/CT-TTg, issued on March 30, 2026, identify renewable energy development, electricity savings and rooftop solar power as priorities. The Government has also called for research into preferential credit mechanisms to support investment in rooftop solar and BESS. However, market development remains constrained by high initial investment costs, limited access to finance, gaps in technical standards, fire safety requirements and complicated implementation procedures. Thiện called for closer coordination among regulators, local authorities, power companies and businesses to improve the legal framework, facilitate grid connections, enhance product quality and expand financing options. He also stressed the need to strengthen domestic research, manufacturing and technical capabilities to reduce reliance on imported equipment. Storage capacity set to expand Võ Quang Lâm, former deputy general director of Vietnam Electricity (EVN), said the country’s installed power capacity reached 87,616MW at the end of 2025, ranking second in Southeast Asia. As of August 2026, Việt Nam had 134,410 rooftop solar systems with a combined capacity of more than 11,450MWp, while the number of self-produced and self-consumed installations equipped with BESS remained very limited. On larger storage projects, Hà Nội Power Corporation (EVNHANOI) had completed 50MW of BESS capacity, while Northern Power Corporation (EVNNPC) had completed 155MW and aimed to reach 305MW in October 2026, Lâm said. Electricity Project Management Board No 2 and Power Generation Corporation 3 (EVNGENCO3) were pursuing investment procedures for centralised storage projects in northern Việt Nam, with planned capacities of 550MW and 300MW, respectively. Lâm said factories, commercial buildings and industrial parks could combine rooftop solar, battery storage and smart energy management systems to optimise electricity consumption and reduce dependence on grid power. He called for technical standards, grid-connection requirements, fire safety regulations, testing procedures and pricing mechanisms for BESS services. He also proposed publishing the PVout coefficient used to estimate rooftop solar generation at ward and commune level to improve calculation accuracy and support investment decisions. Bùi Xuân Bình, chairman and general director of GG Power, said Việt Nam should build its capacity to research, manufacture and export energy technologies rather than remain primarily a consumer market for products developed elsewhere. GG Power is developing energy storage manufacturing capacity, targeting an annual scale of 5GWh to serve residential, commercial, industrial and large-scale projects. Bình said a competitive domestic industry would require a complete value chain covering research, design, manufacturing, installation, maintenance and battery recycling. Cooperation among businesses, research institutions, distributors and financial institutions would also be needed to improve technology and access to finance. He stressed that product safety, quality, customer protection and effective battery collection and recycling systems were essential to sustainable market development. Representatives from Goldwind Group, Cornex Group, SRNE Group, Đan Khuê Solar, Ngọc Long Energy and Solar Kinh Bắc, among others, expressed interest in cooperation with GG Power. At the conference, the company introduced its “Made in Vietnam” energy storage products and signed cooperation agreements with several businesses to strengthen industry links and expand distribution networks. Participants said the market had significant growth potential but needed more consistent policies, affordable products and reliable warranty and maintenance services to improve the competitiveness of domestic technologies. — VNS

artigo.texto: Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) has pulled out of a planned AI data center in Loughton, Essex, that British cloud provider Nscale was building for it, Reuters reported on October 18, citing the Telegraph. Microsoft is one of Nscale's two largest customers. Reuters said the Telegraph did not specify why Microsoft withdrew, and Microsoft declined Reuters' request for comment. The site did have an obvious problem: power. The Telegraph reported that grid officials told Nscale they didn't expect to supply electricity until the 2030s. That matches a September report that UK Power Networks couldn't connect the site before the early to mid-2030s. Nscale says it remains committed to Loughton and is looking at other power sources. Loughton Was a Small Slice of Microsoft's Buildout Loughton was planned to house about 23,000 Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) chips for Azure, starting at 50 MW. Nscale agreed to supply Microsoft with about 200,000 Nvidia chips across the UK, Norway, Portugal and Texas, so Loughton was about 11.5% of the program. Microsoft added roughly a gigawatt of capacity in the June quarter alone, which makes Loughton's starting load about 5% of one quarter. The spending shows no sign of a pullback. Cash capital expenditure reached $35.80 billion in the June quarter, more than double the $17.08 billion a year earlier. Fiscal 2026 cash capex totaled $115.95 billion, up about 80%. On management's broader measure including finance leases, June-quarter capex was approximately $41 billion, with more than $50 billion expected in the September quarter. Demand is keeping pace. Intelligent Cloud revenue hit $39.31 billion in the June quarter, up about 32% from $29.88 billion, and CFO Amy Hood said customer demand still exceeds available supply. Microsoft has the customers and the cash. What it can't buy quickly is electricity. Power First, Then Chips Microsoft has been picky with Nscale before. It signed a letter of intent for up to 1.35 GW at Nscale's West Virginia campus in March, then walked away over the summer, and Anthropic took the capacity. Meanwhile, it is paying up for sites with a power date. On October 16, two days before the Loughton report, NiSource (NI) announced a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, with service expected to begin in 2028 and approximately 1,100 MW of generation resources to be added in Indiana. The other workaround is making power on-site, which is where Bloom Energy (BE:NYSE) comes in. Nscale reportedly held talks with Bloom about fuel cells for Loughton. Bloom's revenue reached a record $1.065 billion in the June quarter, up 166% from a year earlier. Its last four quarters brought in about $3.12 billion, nearly double the $1.63 billion of the four before. Grid delays are already showing up in someone's income statement.

artigo.texto: Epyr Raises $17 Million to Expand Industrial Thermal Energy Storage The funding will support new projects, including a 35-MWh thermal energy storage installation in France October 19, 2026 Follow Mercom India on WhatsApp for exclusive updates on clean energy news and insights France-based thermal energy storage provider Epyr has raised €15 million (~$17 million) in an oversubscribed Series A round led by SlateVC to expand its industrial thermal energy storage projects. Existing investors AENU and Daphni participated alongside WEPA Ventures, OVNI Capital, and Aurum Impact. Epyr develops thermal energy storage systems that use electricity during periods of low prices to generate and store heat for industrial applications. Its technology uses electric resistors to heat air, which transfers thermal energy to firebricks. The bricks store energy at high temperatures, allowing industrial facilities to use the heat when required. Sébastien Léger, co-founder and GP at SlateVC, said, “We were convinced by the quality of the entire Epyr team, their speed and their customer-centric approach. They deliver climate impact, energy cost savings and resilience to industrial sites. Epyr has the potential to become a European leader in electrifying the €100 billion (~$118 billion) industrial heat market. We are delighted to enable their growth in France and beyond.” The funding comes 18 months after Epyr’s pre-seed round, in which the company raised €3 million (~$3.1 million), co-led by AENU and Daphni. OVNI Capital, WEPA Ventures, and several other European angel investors also participated. Epyr has been selected to deploy a 35 MWh thermal energy storage unit at Papeco’s Orval-sur-Sienne facility in France. The company described the installation as France’s largest thermal energy storage project, replacing all natural gas consumption at the Papeco facility. The company said it is prioritizing industrial steam, mainly in paper, food and beverage, and chemicals. Epyr deployed an industrial thermal energy storage unit at WEPA Group, a hygiene paper manufacturer, in Troyes, which went into operation in early 2026. According to Mercom’s 1H 2026 Funding and M&A for Energy Storage report, VC funding for energy storage companies in 1H 2026 totaled $1.6 billion across 51 deals, representing a 6% YoY decline compared to the $1.7 billion raised across 36 deals in 1H 2025.

artigo.texto: CALAUAN, LAGUNA — The local government of Calauan is pushing for the implementation of a carbon credit initiative aimed at protecting the environment while potentially opening opportunities for additional funding for environmental and community development projects. Calauan Mayor Roseller Caratihan said the local government has been working on the initiative for four months, including conducting public hearings and deliberations at the Sangguniang Bayan. The proposed measure is now on its second reading, and the municipal council is expected to issue a corresponding resolution next week to advance the implementation of the carbon credit initiative in the municipality. Calauan’s initiative comes as the national government moves to establish a clearer policy framework for the development of carbon markets in the Philippines. On Oct. 13, 2026, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Executive Order 127, directing the formulation of the Philippine Carbon Market Policy Framework, creating the Inter-Agency Committee on Carbon Markets, and designating the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) as the national authority for carbon markets in the country. What is a carbon credit and how can it help? A carbon credit represents one metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) that has been verified as reduced or removed from the atmosphere through a qualified project. In a carbon market, carbon credits may be sold or traded to companies seeking to support or account for greenhouse gas emission reductions, subject to applicable standards and verification requirements. Projects that protect and restore forests, plant and maintain trees, improve waste management, or adopt technologies that reduce emissions may generate carbon credits, provided their environmental impact is properly measured, monitored, and verified. For local governments such as Calauan, this mechanism could provide an opportunity to attract additional funding for environmental programs. However, the potential benefits will depend on the type of project, compliance with applicable standards, verification of results, and the availability of buyers for the credits. Potential benefits for residents Beyond contributing to efforts to address climate change, the carbon credit initiative could create opportunities for projects that directly benefit local communities. These may include restoring green spaces, protecting natural resources, improving waste management, and generating livelihood opportunities for residents participating in environmental programs. Ensuring transparency in the management of potential carbon credit revenues will also be essential. The local government would need to establish how the proceeds will be managed, who will benefit, and how the rights and livelihoods of residents affected by the projects will be protected. The national policy framework envisioned under EO 127 is expected to help establish guidelines for project selection, monitoring, reporting, and the equitable sharing of benefits. In Calauan, attention is now focused on the Sangguniang Bayan’s next steps regarding the proposed resolution, which could pave the way for the initiative’s next phase. If properly implemented, the carbon credit initiative could become part of the municipality’s broader efforts to protect the environment while exploring innovative ways to support community needs and sustainable development.

artigo.texto: The 15-Minute Space TPU: Why Orbital Data Centers Are a Radiator Problem Google's prototype can only run for 15 minutes before it has to cool down. The radiator, not the chip, explains the entire economics of space compute. Google's first Project Suncatcher prototype satellite has reached orbit on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission. The spacecraft, built with Planet Labs and roughly the size of a refrigerator, carries four Google TPUs. Google says the ground team has made contact and that the satellite is operating as expected. The detail that traveled fastest was this: the TPUs can run for about 15 minutes, then must shut down while the radiator rejects the heat. That sounds like a thermal failure in orbit. It is not. The 15-minute window was written into the mission profile before launch. Google designed an intermittent operating cycle because, in vacuum, the radiator rather than the chip sets the long-run compute ceiling. That distinction matters. It moves the question from "can a TPU survive space?" to "what kind of system can run continuously in space?" A data center is judged by sustained average power, not by a 15-minute burst. On that measure, the radiator is the main character. Three problems, one still open Google's public test results divide the engineering risk into three buckets. Launch vibration: the TPU assembly passed three-axis vibration testing, with local loads of 50 to 100 g. Google's team described the result as better than expected. Radiation: at UC Davis, Google ran the Trillium TPU under a proton beam while it was executing workloads. The chip absorbed a total ionizing dose exceeding the cumulative dose of a five-year mission. That is a positive early signal for inference workloads. Training would face a higher risk profile. Heat rejection: Google tested the thermal path in a thermal vacuum chamber. The result was an intermittent operating mode. Vibration and radiation have fairly clear answers. Heat is being bypassed by duty cycle. Why the radiator sets average compute In space, there is no air convection and no atmospheric sink. Heat moves from the chip through heat pipes to a radiator, then leaves as infrared radiation. The radiator's continuous rejection rate is fixed by its area, its temperature, and its emissivity. The Stefan-Boltzmann relationship makes temperature the dominant term: rejection scales with the fourth power of absolute temperature. A rough estimate shows the scale. At a radiator surface temperature of 20°C (293 K) and emissivity 0.9, one square meter rejects about 376 W on one side. Two sides give roughly 750 W before accounting for Earth infrared and albedo inputs. The net figure is lower, around 600 W per square meter in a realistic low-Earth-orbit environment. A ground-based high-density AI rack now draws well over 100 kW. At 600 W per square meter net, one such rack maps to nearly 170 square meters of radiator area. That is one rack. This is why a space data center is a radiator-area project. The compute boards are a small part of the mass and volume. Most of the structure goes to radiators, heat pipes, and deployment mechanisms. Google's project lead has said the radiator is one of the heaviest components on the prototype. In an industry that charges by launch mass, the heaviest component also sets the compute ceiling. The economics follow the radiator. The design logic also flips. On the ground, cooling engineers push chip temperatures down: colder water, lower PUE, lower junction temperature, less leakage, longer life. In space, a hotter radiator is better. Raising the radiator surface from 20°C to 60°C (333 K) lifts single-side rejection from about 376 W per square meter to about 627 W per square meter, an increase of nearly 70%. A space-optimized compute chip should tolerate higher junction temperatures and accept a modest efficiency penalty in exchange for radiator mass reduction. Today's TPUs and GPUs are optimized for ground data-center temperature windows. Sending them up is a test under the wrong conditions. For a prototype, that is acceptable. For a scalable architecture, it is not. The long-run metric changes accordingly: from performance per watt to sustained performance per square meter of radiator area, or sustained performance per kilogram of launched mass. The duty cycle does not create extra compute The heat sink, heat pipes, and structure have thermal capacitance. During the 15-minute run, the chip's heat output exceeds the radiator's continuous rejection rate. The difference goes into thermal capacitance, and the temperature rises. When the chip shuts down, the radiator drains that stored heat. Averaged over a full run-and-cool cycle, the continuous heat rejection equals the radiator's capacity. The burst does not add a watt of long-run compute. It moves the radiator's capacity into a 15-minute window. For a single inference demo, one question and one answer, 15 minutes is enough. For a data center, the number that matters is the average. That number is set by radiator area and temperature. What the orbital test should measure Google says the satellite will run the Gemma open-weight model to observe how the chip behaves in space. The thermal chain matters more than the model output. Three measurements matter more than benchmark scores. First, whether thermal interface materials degrade under vacuum and repeated thermal cycling. Second, how far heat-pipe performance in microgravity diverges from ground measurements. Third, whether the 15-minute window shrinks over a year. A shrinking window would indicate thermal-path degradation. That is a more serious problem than radiation-induced bit flips, because it directly erodes average compute. Google plans to launch two more satellites in 2027 to test high-bandwidth laser inter-satellite links and formation flying. That work is as important as heat rejection. A single satellite has a fixed radiator area. Scaling means multiple satellites. The inter-satellite bandwidth

Kirill Dmitriev afirmou que as sanções impostas pelos Estados Unidos representam sérios obstáculos para a colaboração econômica entre os dois países. O enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin criticou a Lei Graham, aprovada recentemente, que tem como objetivo reduzir as receitas energéticas da Rússia por meio de sanções e tarifas. Apesar das dificuldades, Dmitriev mencionou que a Rússia e os EUA estão discutindo novas iniciativas em conjunto, como projetos de data centers energéticos movidos a energia nuclear. Ele enfatizou que a recente assinatura de um acordo sobre o diesel marca um passo importante nesse sentido. ✨ O Kremlin tem manifestado frustração com o fato de que os EUA vinculam acordos econômicos a um acordo de paz, mas Dmitriev demonstrou otimismo sobre a possibilidade de novas cooperações. Durante a conferência Russian Energy Week, em Moscou, o emissário russo destacou que o progresso nas negociações é desafiador, devido à resistência de diversos setores, mas que o exemplo recente do acordo sobre diesel indica um possível avanço em outras áreas. Ele também mencionou que o Tesouro dos EUA pediu auxílio ao fundo soberano russo para resolver questões de pagamento referentes ao acordo sobre o diesel. artigo.texto: Rising demand for energy storage systems driven by the spread of artificial intelligence data centers, coupled with expectations for the commercialization of next-generation batteries, has pushed a Shinhan Asset Management exchange-traded fund investing in solid-state battery companies to the top of three-month return rankings. The SOL Solid-State Battery & Silicon Anode ETF posted a 22.76% return over the three months through Oct. 16, according to the Korea Exchange on the 19th. That was the highest return among domestically listed equity ETFs, excluding leveraged and inverse products. It also exceeded the KOSPI's return of minus 16.90% over the same period by 39.66 percentage points. The fund's main holdings include next-generation battery companies such as Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution, EcoPro BM, Isu Specialty Chemical, Lotte Energy Materials and Daejoo Electronic Materials. The product focuses on competitiveness in next-generation technologies such as solid-state batteries and silicon anode materials, rather than short-term shifts in demand in the existing electric vehicle market. With the recent rally in domestic semiconductor shares losing momentum, secondary battery ETFs have moved into the top tier of returns. Analysts attribute the shift to improved investor sentiment as the battery industry, long weighed down by slowing EV demand, secures a new growth driver centered on ESS. Growing electricity demand from AI data centers and the expansion of renewable power generation are cited as the main drivers of ESS market growth. LG Energy Solution posted preliminary third-quarter operating profit of 756 billion won ($528 million), beating market expectations. The expansion of its North American ESS business and the conversion of production facilities are seen as supporting the earnings recovery. Expectations are also building for the commercialization of next-generation battery technology. Samsung SDI is pursuing technology development and cooperation with customers with the goal of mass-producing solid-state batteries in 2027. The government also plans to provide about 400 billion won for next-generation battery research and development over five years starting in 2027. Solid-state batteries replace conventional liquid electrolytes with solid ones to improve safety and energy density, and their applications are expected to expand beyond electric vehicles into areas such as humanoid robots and aerospace. "The secondary battery industry is securing a new demand base through ESS, and growth drivers are diversifying as the commercialization of next-generation technologies such as solid-state batteries and silicon anode materials comes into view," said Kim Jung-hyun, head of the ETF business group at Shinhan Asset Management. "Going forward, the earnings recovery through ESS and competitiveness in next-generation technologies such as solid-state batteries will be key factors determining corporate value."

artigo.texto: A China tem buscado avançar na transição energética sem dissociá-la da conservação dos ecossistemas. Essa orientação apareceu em duas iniciativas divulgadas pela agência estatal Xinhua em 16 de outubro: o avanço do armazenamento de energia, considerado importante para ampliar o aproveitamento das fontes renováveis, e a defesa do presidente Xi Jinping de que a conservação ecológica seja prioridade no desenvolvimento do país. Embora sejam ações distintas, as duas notícias refletem aspectos complementares da estratégia ambiental chinesa: transformar a infraestrutura energética e, ao mesmo tempo, fortalecer a proteção e a recuperação de áreas naturais. Armazenamento ganha importância na expansão das renováveis A Conferência Mundial de Armazenamento de Energia 2026, realizada de quarta a sexta-feira em Ningde, na província de Fujian, reuniu representantes do governo, da indústria e da comunidade internacional para discutir novas tecnologias, perspectivas de mercado e os desafios da integração energética. Segundo dados apresentados no evento, a expansão global anual do armazenamento de energia em baterias alcançou aproximadamente 307 gigawatts-hora (GWh) em 2025. A China respondeu por 56% desse volume, consolidando sua posição como um dos principais mercados do setor. Ilina Stefanova, chefe da Coalizão para Ação da Agência Internacional de Energia Renovável (IRENA), afirmou durante a abertura da conferência que a escala de implantação chinesa está ajudando a transformar a economia da eletricidade renovável. Para ela, a experiência do país em tecnologia, fabricação, instalação e integração dos sistemas à rede elétrica também pode contribuir para a transição energética internacional. O armazenamento é importante porque a geração solar e eólica varia conforme as condições naturais. Baterias podem guardar parte da eletricidade produzida quando há oferta abundante e disponibilizá-la posteriormente, contribuindo para equilibrar a oferta e a demanda. Sua integração à rede, porém, depende de fatores como custos, capacidade instalada, planejamento e características de cada sistema elétrico. Na China, a indústria continua ampliando sua capacidade de produção. De acordo com informações apresentadas pelo vice-ministro da Indústria e Informatização, Xiong Jijun, a produção nacional de baterias destinadas ao armazenamento de energia superou 420 GWh no primeiro semestre de 2026, alta de aproximadamente 110% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O setor também desenvolve diferentes soluções tecnológicas. As baterias de íons de lítio mantêm papel de destaque, enquanto alternativas como as baterias de íons de sódio e as baterias de fluxo avançam no mercado. Zeng Yuqun, fundador e presidente da fabricante chinesa CATL, destacou que o armazenamento deixou de ser apenas uma infraestrutura complementar e passou a ocupar uma posição cada vez mais importante nos sistemas de energia. Segundo ele, a expansão das fontes renováveis exige soluções capazes de atender às necessidades da rede e melhorar sua confiabilidade e estabilidade. A escala industrial, contudo, não elimina os desafios da transição. O armazenamento precisa ser economicamente viável, integrado de maneira eficiente às redes e acompanhado de planejamento para evitar desperdícios e assegurar o uso adequado dos recursos. Xi reforça prioridade à conservação ecológica No mesmo dia, o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, defendeu que o país mantenha o compromisso de priorizar a conservação ecológica e promover o desenvolvimento verde. A declaração foi feita durante uma visita de inspeção à cidade de Ulanqab, na Região Autônoma da Mongólia Interior, no norte da China. Um dos locais visitados foi a reserva natural do lago Huangqihai, cuja área alagada esteve próxima de secar em razão de impactos climáticos e de outros fatores. Segundo a Xinhua, após anos de esforços de conservação, o corpo d’água vem sendo recuperado e ampliado. Durante a visita, Xi conheceu as iniciativas regionais de proteção ambiental, percorreu áreas próximas à margem do lago e observou as aves que habitam o local. Ele pediu a aplicação integral da legislação chinesa de proteção de áreas úmidas, a preservação dos limites estabelecidos para a conservação ecológica e o fortalecimento da proteção da biodiversidade. Para ecossistemas de áreas úmidas degradados, Xi defendeu que a restauração natural seja priorizada, com intervenção humana complementar quando necessária. Também ressaltou a importância de conduzir esse trabalho de forma científica. As áreas úmidas desempenham funções ambientais relevantes, entre elas a manutenção de habitats, a regulação dos ciclos da água e o suporte à biodiversidade. Sua degradação pode afetar espécies, alterar o equilíbrio dos ecossistemas e reduzir a capacidade de resposta a mudanças ambientais. A recuperação do lago Huangqihai, conforme descrita pela agência chinesa, é um exemplo local dos esforços de conservação mencionados na visita. O caso, por si só, não permite medir a dimensão dos resultados ambientais alcançados em toda a China, mas ilustra a importância atribuída à restauração de ecossistemas específicos. Na mesma viagem, Xi visitou a Zona de Desenvolvimento de Alta Tecnologia de Chahar, onde recebeu informações sobre o projeto chinês “East Data, West Computing”, voltado à articulação da infraestrutura nacional de computação. Ele defendeu o desenvolvimento de uma indústria de capacidade computacional que seja eficiente, verde e segura. A agenda da visita, portanto, incluiu tanto a proteção direta da natureza quanto a busca por atividades econômicas e tecnológicas mais eficientes no uso de recursos. Conservação ecológica como diretriz de desenvolvimento A preocupação com a proteção ambiental também aparece no arcabouço legal chinês. Em 15 de agosto de 2026, entrou em vigor o Código Ecológico e Ambiental do país, aprovado pela Assembleia Popular Nacional em março. artigo.texto: I Drove Mercedes’ New EV With A Silicon Anode Battery. The Future Is Here The CLA Electric's flaws are overpowered by monster efficiency and charging speeds thanks to new silicon-containing cells. I couldn't help but roll my eyes when Mercedes-Benz first unveiled the all-electric CLA last year. What on Earth were those 142 illuminated stars doing on the grille? The automaker has admitted the industry had gone too far with giant screens and fewer buttons, so why did the new CLA still come with a humongous, pillar-to-pillar "Superscreen?" From the photos alone, I wasn't convinced that the CLA could be the electric hit Mercedes needs right now. The German automaker has been losing ground to increasingly competitive Chinese rivals, and its first wave of EQ-branded EVs with their computer-mouse-like designs didn't exactly take off. The CLA, then, is meant to be a fresh start, the first in a new generation of software-defined, higher-tech EVs. WHY LEMONADE? This story was published in partnership with Lemonade. But when Mercedes handed me the keys to a CLA 350 Electric for a week, the car proved me dead wrong. The CLA is lovely to drive and the all-wheel-drive 350 delivers serious performance. Its range comfortably blew past the EPA rating, and charging stops were astonishingly quick, thanks to the new silicon-containing battery. This compact luxury sedan has plenty of flaws, too. The software doesn't feel class leading, and I question some of its interior design choices. But the fundamentals are so strong that most of those drawbacks felt trivial to me. It's an excellent EV, but not necessarily a great Mercedes-Benz. And I'm perfectly fine with that. Let's dive right in. New-Generation Battery Cells At the heart of the CLA are Mercedes-Benz's new-generation battery cells that use a silicon-oxide and graphite blend in the anode, the electrode that stores lithium ions during charging. I found the CLA to be a strong performer in both range and charging performance, and Mercedes attributes that to the new batteries. Traditionally, graphite has been the go-to anode material in batteries, but automakers are increasingly incorporating silicon to boost energy density and charging speed. They're also trying to reduce their reliance on graphite; China dominates processing of the material, and it's dirty and expensive to mine. Mercedes said the new cells improve energy density by 20% while also reducing cobalt content. The rear-wheel-drive CLA 250's EPA-estimated 374 miles of range should be more than enough for most drivers. The all-wheel drive 350 is rated for 312 miles, but its real-world range is much higher. I didn't do a full-blown range test, but I did see an impressive 4.2 miles per kilowatt-hour across mostly highway driving in Sport mode in fall weather. With 85 kilowatt-hours of usable battery capacity, that works out to roughly 357 miles on a full charge, about 45 miles beyond its 312-mile EPA estimate. Plenty of electric sedans offer more range than the CLA, including the Lucid Air, Audi A6 e-tron, and new BMW i3. But those are all a bit bigger and not exactly apples-to-apples rivals. Charging performance is similarly impressive, even if it's nothing like the fastest-charging EVs in the U.S. I put it through a 16-80% and a 16-90% charging test at a 400-kilowatt Mercedes-Benz High Power Charging station in Livingston, New Jersey. The press car had Plug & Charge enabled, so the session started almost immediately after I connected the cable to its factory-fitted Tesla-style NACS charging port. Within seconds, the CLA was pulling a peak of 280 kW. It added 100 miles of indicated range in just five minutes. After 14 minutes, it had gained 200 miles, and it reached 80% state of charge in exactly 20 minutes, adding 254 miles of indicated range in that time. The really remarkable part came next. The CLA reached 90% in just 26 minutes, adding nearly 300 miles of indicated range over the session. With that kind of performance, the car may be ready to leave a charging stop before you've even finished grabbing a coffee or snack. Spend too long inside, and you may be paying for charging that you don't need. How It Feels To Drive Most EVs use a single-speed reduction gear, but the CLA is among a small group of electric cars—alongside the Porsche Taycan and Audi e-tron GT—to feature a two-speed transmission. Mercedes says the setup delivers the best of both worlds. First gear provides punchy acceleration from a standstill while also being suited to lower-speed driving. Second gear takes over at higher speeds, helping sustain power delivery and improve efficiency during highway cruising. In practice, I barely noticed the gear changes. According to our previous tests by my colleagues Andrei Nedelea and Editor-in-Chief Mack Hogan, the transmission shifts into second gear at around 60-65 miles per hour. My testing routes had speed limits of 60 mph or lower, so I suspect I spent much of my time in first gear. Either way, you never have to think about the gearbox. The CLA is buttery-smooth to drive, and that's what matters. The CLA 350's 349 horsepower and 380 pound-feet of torque get unleashed instantly and aggressively. The throttle response is sharp, and a firm squeeze of the pedal releases a forceful surge of acceleration. It loves the twisty back roads, too. It doesn't feel quite as light on its feet as its compact dimensions might suggest, and its heft is definitely noticeable in corners.
