artigo.texto: Green credit joins forces with the carbon market: A way to unlock capital for businesses. (Dan Tri Newspaper) - Reducing emissions is no longer a cost burden when carbon credits can generate real revenue, helping businesses have more cash flow to repay loans and unlock large-scale green credit packages. In many industrial zones, the challenge of investing in clean technology used to be a major concern for many business owners due to the high cost of machinery and the long payback period. Now, the mindset regarding green investment is fundamentally changing. Reducing emissions is no longer just about complying with environmental standards, but has become a concrete source of financial revenue through the sale of carbon quotas and credits. Businesses sell emissions reductions to repay loans. According to the Government Newspaper, at the workshop on Credit Policy and Carbon Market: Unlocking Green Capital Flows on October 14th, Deputy Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) Nguyen Ngoc Canh stated that achieving the goal of net-zero emissions by 2050 requires significant resources for technological innovation and energy transition. Decree No. 29/2026 on the domestic carbon exchange, along with the pilot phase in 2025-2026 with a scale of over 511 million tons of CO2 equivalent across three sectors—thermal power, iron and steel, and cement—has established a clear legal framework. Green credit and the carbon market thus form a natural synergistic link. Specifically, banks provide capital for businesses to install energy-saving equipment and low-emission technologies. In return, the carbon market helps convert the reduced emissions into cash. This revenue improves cash flow, enhances debt repayment capacity, and directly reduces the risk of bad debt for the banks. The Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system for emission reduction results will provide transparent data for credit institutions to monitor capital utilization and manage loan risks more effectively. You may also like The thirst for hundreds of billions of USD in capital and the legal challenges. Capital flows into sustainable sectors have shown significant progress. As of the end of June, outstanding green credit across the system reached over VND 856,000 billion, an increase of 9.87% compared to the end of 2025. The period from 2017 to 2025 recorded an average growth rate of over 20% per year. The largest concentration of capital flows is in agriculture , forestry, fisheries, and biodiversity conservation (accounting for over 31%), followed by green energy (accounting for nearly 28%). Nevertheless, the need for green transition capital in Vietnam remains very high. Mr. Bui Minh Giap, Chief Economist of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Vietnam, estimates that by 2040, Vietnam will need approximately US$368 billion for climate change adaptation and emission reduction, equivalent to 6.8% of GDP annually. Specifically for the electricity sector, the investment needs for power generation and transmission networks in the 2026-2030 period, according to the revised Power Development Plan VIII, are approximately US$136 billion. Mr. Giap noted that banks need to carefully assess the likelihood of credit approval, production volume, selling price, verification costs, and collection timing before calculating carbon revenue into the debt repayment plan. From the perspective of lending institutions, Dr. Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, Director of the Training School for Cadres and Deputy Head of the ESG Steering Committee of Agribank , stated that Agribank's green credit outstanding reached nearly 30,000 billion VND by the end of March 2026. Dr. Ha suggested clarifying ownership, disposal, and benefit-sharing rights from carbon credits, perfecting the legal framework for secured transactions, accounting, taxation, and foreign exchange, and reducing verification costs for cooperatives and small businesses. Adding channels for mobilizing international financial resources. You may also like Alongside domestic efforts, opportunities to expand access to foreign capital through carbon trading mechanisms are being promoted. According to Carbon Herald, the Climate Vulnerable Countries Forum and the V20 Finance Ministers Group (CVF-V20), along with the Voluntary Carbon Integrity Initiative (VCMI), recently published a guide on implementing Article 6 of the Paris Agreement in Bangkok, ahead of COP31. This document was developed for 77 countries facing an estimated $490 billion annual development finance shortfall, aiming to mobilize an additional $20 billion in carbon finance annually by 2030. Previously, developing countries' participation was quite limited, with the 45 least developed countries accounting for only 1.5% of projects under the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM). Several practical examples have emerged. For instance, Ghana and Switzerland implemented an agreement expected to generate 8 million tons of carbon credits, bringing in $300 million in carbon revenue and attracting $1.1 billion in investment. The Philippines entered into bilateral partnerships with Japan and Singapore, while Bhutan established its own climate fund. Ms. Usha Rao-Monari, Chair of VCMI, emphasized that the handbook helps policymakers make decisions based on accurate data, thereby obtaining higher economic value when undertaking international carbon projects. Simultaneously opening up bank credit channels and the carbon market promises to unlock a stable flow of funds for the energy transition in the coming period.

artigo.texto: Trontek to Unveil 5-MWh BESS, Targets 12 GWh Capacity by 2028 Trontek Electronics will unveil its 5-MWh EKOM battery energy storage system at The Battery Show India 2026 as it plans to scale manufacturing capacity from 3 GWh to 12 GWh by 2028. October 19, 2026. By News Bureau Trontek Electronics, an Indian battery and energy technology company advancing the future of energy storage, will unveil its 5-MWh EKOM containerised Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at The Battery Show India 2026, marking a step in its evolution from mobility batteries to large-scale energy storage. With active manufacturing capacity of 3 GWh and plans to scale to 12 GWh by 2028, the company is building capabilities to address India’s expanding energy storage needs. Trontek will showcase EKOM at Stall C16, Hall 18, from October 22–24, 2026, at India Expo Mart & Centre, Greater Noida. The launch expands Trontek’s presence into large-scale energy storage, bringing its battery expertise to applications beyond electric mobility. Designed for industrial and utility-scale requirements, the EKOM platform addresses the growing role of energy storage in renewable energy integration, power management and the evolving needs of India’s energy infrastructure. The unveiling comes as energy storage gains strategic importance in India’s energy transition. As renewable energy capacity expands and electricity demand evolves, BESS is emerging as a critical enabler of greater flexibility in how power is stored, managed and deployed. Trontek’s move into this segment reflects its ambition to participate in this expanding market through locally developed and manufactured solutions. Building on more than two decades of experience in battery technology and manufacturing, Trontek is extending its capabilities across a broader range of energy applications. The company is targeting 12 GWh of manufacturing capacity by 2028. Speaking ahead of the unveiling, Samrath S. Kochar, Founder & CEO, Trontek, said, “Energy storage is becoming central to how India powers its next phase of growth. With EKOM, we are taking Trontek’s two-decade battery expertise into large-scale energy storage, building capabilities in India for the country’s evolving industrial and energy needs. Our ambition is to contribute to a globally competitive Indian energy storage ecosystem.” The unveiling of Trontek’s 5-MWh EKOM containerised Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) marks the company’s expansion into large-scale energy storage, extending its battery technology expertise to industrial and utility-scale applications. At The Battery Show India 2026, Trontek will showcase its portfolio across electric mobility, energy storage, and power and critical infrastructure solutions. Its electric mobility segment includes battery solutions for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and other mobility applications. Under energy storage, the company offers POWERCUBE for residential applications, NOVARA for commercial facilities and EKOM for industrial and utility-scale storage, including the newly unveiled 5-MWh system. Its power and critical infrastructure portfolio includes inverters and solar solutions for distributed energy applications, along with battery systems for telecom infrastructure and backup power requirements. The portfolio reflects Trontek’s expansion from a mobility-focused battery business into a broader energy technology company, with Made-in-India solutions spanning mobility, distributed energy and large-scale energy storage. A key pillar of Trontek’s expansion is the development of energy storage solutions suited to Indian market requirements, supported by local engineering and manufacturing capabilities. As demand grows across residential, commercial, industrial and utility applications, the company sees an opportunity to build scale while contributing to the development of India’s domestic energy storage ecosystem. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr has ordered the creation of a national carbon market policy framework to attract climate investments and support domestic emissions cuts, the Presidential Communications Office announced on 17 October. To continue reading, subscribe to Eco‑Business. Access all our exclusive content and archive — with a 7-day free trial. Then just US$5/month. Cancel anytime. - Exclusive access to training across business and policy topics - Direct access to industry leaders at Eco-Business events - A seat among the decision makers shaping the region's sustainable development The executive order, signed on 13 October, directs the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to develop rules governing participation in domestic and international carbon markets, which enable trading in credits generated by projects that reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions. The framework will cover voluntary carbon credits, bought by choice rather than legal obligation, as well as credits under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which sets government approval and accounting rules for international carbon trading. The categories can overlap, but voluntary credits do not automatically meet Article 6 requirements. Under the order, the DENR will provide technical, policy and regulatory inputs for nature-based solutions, forestry and waste, while the Department of Energy will cover the energy sector. The Department of Agriculture and Philippine Statistics Authority will handle agriculture-related inputs, and the Department of Transportation will cover transport-related carbon credit projects. The Department of Finance will address fiscal policy, investment promotion, climate finance and the fiscal implications of carbon market transactions. “There is a need to formulate a national carbon market framework aligned with international standards, through a whole-of-government approach, to support the achievement of the country’s NDCs,” the order stated, referring to the Nationally Determined Contribution, a country’s climate action plan under the Paris Agreement. The Philippines submitted its updated pledge in September, seeking to strengthen its net sink status but without committing to a fossil fuel phase-out or net zero. John Leo Algo, national coordinator of the 40-member civil society network Aksyon Klima Pilipinas, said the order signals that the framework could be completed by COP31 or early 2027, potentially attracting investors awaiting clearer rules. But its contribution to stronger climate ambition remains uncertain, he told Eco-Business. “While the 2026 NDC has been finalised, it is missing a 1.5°C-aligned decarbonisation pathway and, subsequently, how much of its conditional target is planned to be achieved through carbon markets.” Algo urged meaningful consultations in the coming weeks, including with communities whose lands are being considered for carbon projects, rather than only prospective market participants. Jonathan Joson, Philippine operations head at Singapore-based carbon solutions firm Kennemer Eco Solutions, welcomed the order’s multi-agency approach. “I am more confident that this executive order resolves the fragmentation. There is higher regulatory certainty leading to investor confidence,” he told Eco-Business. Joson previously warned that carbon credit rules released last year, covering only clean energy projects, could divert investment from nature-based solutions, agriculture and blue carbon without an overarching framework. The order follows a Philippine-Singapore Article 6 agreement signed in May, establishing a legal framework for transferring emissions reductions between the countries. Observers cautioned that credible benefits would depend on robust rules for measuring and approving those reductions. Other Southeast Asian countries have also pursued such agreements before establishing comprehensive domestic carbon markets. Vietnam, which plans to make its carbon market fully operational around 2028, signed an agreement with Singapore last year allowing credits generated by Vietnamese projects to be transferred to the city-state. Thailand also signed an Article 6 agreement with Singapore last year. It operates voluntary crediting schemes and is exploring an emissions trading system, but has yet to introduce a nationwide compliance carbon market.

artigo.texto: A NiSource Inc. (NYSE:NI) firmou um contrato de fornecimento de energia de 20 anos com a Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) para fornecer aproximadamente 1.100 megawatts (MW) de recursos de geração para um complexo de data centers no noroeste de Indiana. A previsão é que o fornecimento de energia elétrica comece em 2028, com a Microsoft concordando em financiar a infraestrutura de geração e transmissão necessária para atender às necessidades de energia da instalação. O acordo será implementado por meio da NiSource Generation Company LLC (GenCo), uma subsidiária de geração da NiSource, e está estruturado para evitar que os custos adicionais de infraestrutura sejam repassados aos clientes de eletricidade da Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC (NIPSCO). A NiSource também aumentou a projeção de economia para seus clientes, associada aos contratos de data center, para aproximadamente US$ 1,75 bilhão ao longo da vigência dos contratos, em comparação com a estimativa anterior de US$ 1,4 bilhão. Microsoft financiará infraestrutura de geração e transmissão de energia Nos termos do acordo, a Microsoft será responsável pelo financiamento de toda a infraestrutura de geração e transmissão necessária para atender ao seu complexo de data centers. O objetivo do acordo é garantir que os custos associados ao fornecimento da demanda adicional de eletricidade sejam arcados pela Microsoft, e não pelos clientes atuais da NIPSCO. A infraestrutura será desenvolvida por meio da subsidiária GenCo da NiSource, que fornece recursos de geração para grandes clientes de eletricidade. O acordo abrange aproximadamente 1.100 MW de recursos de geração ao longo de um período de 20 anos. A dimensão do compromisso reflete as necessidades substanciais de eletricidade associadas às operações de grandes centros de dados, particularmente instalações que suportam computação em nuvem e cargas de trabalho de inteligência artificial. A NiSource ainda não divulgou o investimento total associado ao acordo nem a composição detalhada dos recursos de geração. Mais informações financeiras e operacionais são esperadas durante a teleconferência de resultados do terceiro trimestre da empresa. A estimativa de economia para os clientes da NIPSCO aumenta para US$ 1,75 bilhão A NiSource afirmou que o acordo com a Microsoft aumenta a economia projetada para os clientes de eletricidade da NIPSCO para aproximadamente US$ 1,75 bilhão ao longo da vigência de seus contratos de data center. O valor revisado compara-se com a estimativa anteriormente divulgada pela empresa, de US$ 1,4 bilhão. O aumento de aproximadamente 350 milhões de dólares reflete os benefícios adicionais que a NiSource espera obter com seus acordos com grandes consumidores de eletricidade. Segundo a empresa, a economia pode chegar a US$ 140 por ano para cada cliente de eletricidade atual. As projeções são baseadas nos efeitos financeiros previstos dos contratos de data center da empresa e não garantem reduções anuais para todos os clientes. O acordo foi concebido para dar suporte à demanda de eletricidade em larga escala, limitando o impacto financeiro sobre as famílias e empresas já atendidas pela NIPSCO. A GenCo contrata 600 MW de armazenamento em baterias Em relação ao acordo com a Microsoft, a NiSource Generation Company contratou 600 MW de capacidade de armazenamento de energia em baterias sob um contrato de prestação de serviços de longo prazo. A instalação de armazenamento de baterias será desenvolvida e construída por uma empresa afiliada ao Grupo AGP. Após entrar em operação, a instalação fará parte do portfólio de recursos de geração e armazenamento da GenCo, atendendo a diversos clientes de grande porte. Os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias podem armazenar eletricidade para uso posterior, proporcionando maior flexibilidade na gestão da oferta e da demanda de eletricidade. Os 600 MW contratados representam a capacidade de geração de energia da instalação. A NiSource não divulgou a duração do armazenamento de energia nem a capacidade total em megawatts-hora. A empresa também não especificou o cronograma de construção do projeto nem a data prevista para o seu lançamento. O sistema de armazenamento de baterias faz parte da estratégia mais ampla da NiSource para atender às necessidades de eletricidade de grandes clientes comerciais. NiSource mira na crescente demanda por eletricidade em data centers O acordo amplia a participação da NiSource no fornecimento de eletricidade para grandes empreendimentos de centros de dados. A demanda por eletricidade proveniente de centros de dados tornou-se uma consideração cada vez mais importante para as concessionárias de energia dos EUA, à medida que as empresas de tecnologia expandem sua infraestrutura de computação. Instalações de grande porte exigem capacidade de geração e conexões de transmissão substanciais, criando requisitos de investimento adicionais para os fornecedores de eletricidade. O acordo da NiSource com a Microsoft estabelece uma estrutura comercial de longo prazo para o fornecimento de infraestrutura ao campus de Indiana, alocando os custos associados à empresa de tecnologia. A duração de 20 anos estabelece um período contratual definido para os acordos de fornecimento de eletricidade planejados. No entanto, a contribuição financeira do acordo para os lucros e o fluxo de caixa da NiSource ainda não foi divulgada. A empresa deverá fornecer mais informações durante a apresentação de seus resultados trimestrais. NiSource e Microsoft enfatizam a proteção de custos para o cliente O presidente e diretor executivo da NiSource, Lloyd Yates, descreveu o acordo como parte de uma abordagem equilibrada para atrair investimentos e, ao mesmo tempo, proteger os clientes de eletricidade existentes. A empresa afirmou que o acordo foi concebido para apoiar o desenvolvimento econômico associado à construção de centros de dados, sem exigir que os atuais contribuintes financiem a infraestrutura adicional. artigo.texto: Russia’s Rosatom and Egypt’s Telecom and Technology Co. (Teletech) have signed an agreement to establish local battery energy storage system (BESS) assembly facilities in Egypt, with a potential annual production capacity of 500 megawatt-hours (MWh). The agreement, signed during the Egypt Energy 2026 Exhibition and Conference, covers personnel training and the gradual expansion of production capacity, according to a press release by Rosatom. “Teletech’s partnership with Rosatom represents a timely step toward strengthening Egypt’s energy infrastructure: we are combining advanced lithium-ion battery storage technology with local implementation capabilities,” said Ihab Saad, Chief Technology Officer of Teletech. The partnership aims to support the deployment of energy storage solutions across several sectors, including electricity, telecommunications, data centers, oil and gas, and other industries. “Egypt’s energy transition increasingly depends on the ability to combine a diversified energy mix with resilient infrastructure and stronger local industrial capabilities. Building local capacity for energy storage systems can support grid stability as renewable energy expands, reduce dependence on imported technologies and external supply chains, and develop domestic technical expertise,” said Murad Aslanov, Director of Rosatom’s Country Office in Egypt. Rosatom’s Energy Storage business unit develops lithium-ion energy storage systems for backup power supplies, renewable energy applications, and electric vehicles. Teletech is an Egyptian technology and telecommunications company specializing in technology design and implementation, procurement, logistics, and project execution. Egypt is rapidly expanding its battery energy storage systems (BESS) to stabilize its grid, shift daytime solar power to evening peaks, and achieve its updated target of 42% renewable energy generation by 2030. In August, Egypt laid the foundation stone for China’s Sungrow’s $50 million energy storage assembly plant in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), with a planned annual capacity of 10 gigawatt-hours (GWh) and operations expected to begin in April 2027. The project, which spans an area of 50,000 square meters (m²), is expected to have an annual production capacity of 10 gigawatt-hours (GWh) at full operation. In July, the Cabinet granted golden licenses for two BESS projects operated by Nefertiti Energy Storage Batteries Company and Horus Energy Storage Batteries in the Benban area in Aswan Governorate.

artigo.texto: Claro e Vivo questionam data centers como obrigação no leilão de 6 GHz Anatel defende vínculo com telecomunicações e prevê acesso aberto por 15 anos; Abrint pede proteção aos investimentos existentes. Vivo e Claro questionaram a inclusão de investimentos em data centers entre as obrigações das vencedoras do futuro leilão de 6 GHz e na audiência pública da Anatel realizada nesta sexta-feira, 16. As empresas defenderam que os compromissos associados à compra do espectro priorizem a expansão da conectividade. A agência sustentou que a infraestrutura de processamento de dados está ligada à prestação dos serviços de telecomunicações e à experiência dos usuários. A proposta em consulta prevê financiar núcleos regionais neutros e nós de borda, com prioridade para áreas menos atendidas por esse tipo de infraestrutura. Os recursos seriam aportados pelas vencedoras e administrados por uma entidade constituída por elas, sob a governança de um grupo presidido pela Anatel. Monique Barros, da Claro, afirmou que o questionamento da empresa está na vinculação do financiamento dos data centers à aquisição de frequências para redes móveis. “A questão que colocamos para reflexão não é sobre a importância do data center, e sim se a sua implementação deve constituir compromisso vinculado à aquisição de espectro”, declarou. A companhia apontou necessidades de investimento em cobertura de rodovias, áreas remotas e evolução tecnológica. “Essa evolução do serviço de telecomunicações devia ser o único foco dos compromissos dos editais de licitação do nosso setor”, acrescentou Monique. Rafael Andrade de Oliveira, representante da Vivo, argumentou que a implantação de data centers não está entre as modalidades de compromisso previstas no artigo 9º do Decreto nº 9.612/2018, que trata das políticas públicas de telecomunicações. A Vivo defendeu compromissos voltados à conectividade e executados diretamente pelas vencedoras, dispensando a entidade administradora. A GSMA, representada por Larissa Jales, também pediu aprofundamento da discussão sobre valoração, governança e relação dessas obrigações com as autorizações de radiofrequência. Demanda assegurada por cinco anos Na apresentação da proposta, a Anatel detalhou que as operadoras vencedoras deverão assegurar demanda mínima correspondente a 30% da capacidade energizada de cada núcleo nos primeiros 60 meses. O objetivo apresentado é dar condições iniciais de funcionamento aos projetos. Após 36 meses, nenhum grupo poderá ocupar mais de 40% da capacidade. A infraestrutura deverá oferecer acesso aberto por pelo menos 15 anos, mediante oferta pública de referência homologada pela agência. Também está previsto uso de, no mínimo, 80% de energia renovável. A entidade administradora ficará responsável pela gestão dos recursos, seleção, acompanhamento e auditoria dos projetos, mas não será executora dos projetos. A escolha das localidades incluirá critérios de priorização, teste de mercado para identificar investimentos privados existentes ou previstos e avaliação do déficit de viabilidade econômica. Recursos sem projetos elegíveis poderão ser direcionados a fibra e cobertura móvel. Abrint pede proteção aos investimentos A Abrint reconheceu o objetivo de aproximar processamento e interconexão dos usuários, mas pediu esclarecimentos sobre os critérios de localização e a verificação da neutralidade das instalações. “Os provedores regionais também vêm investindo em Edge Data Centers”, destacou Artur Coimbra, representante da associação. A entidade quer evitar que projetos financiados com recursos do leilão disputem os mesmos clientes em condições favorecidas, comprometendo investimentos já realizados. “A prioridade deve decorrer da necessidade demonstrada e da insuficiência da oferta disponível”, acrescentou Coimbra. A equipe da Anatel disse que evitar essa sobreposição é uma preocupação da proposta e solicitou contribuições para aperfeiçoar os mecanismos. Também defendeu que a inclusão de data centers acompanha a necessidade de considerar outras infraestruturas associadas às telecomunicações, além das redes de acesso e transporte.

artigo.texto: Crédito verde une forças com o mercado de carbono: uma forma de desbloquear capital para empresas. (Jornal Dan Tri) - Reduzir as emissões deixa de ser um fardo financeiro quando os créditos de carbono podem gerar receita real, ajudando as empresas a terem mais fluxo de caixa para pagar empréstimos e desbloquear pacotes de crédito verde em larga escala. Em muitas zonas industriais, o desafio de investir em tecnologia limpa costumava ser uma grande preocupação para muitos empresários devido ao alto custo das máquinas e ao longo período de retorno do investimento. Agora, a mentalidade em relação ao investimento verde está mudando fundamentalmente. Reduzir as emissões não se trata mais apenas de cumprir as normas ambientais, mas tornou-se uma fonte concreta de receita financeira por meio da venda de cotas e créditos de carbono. As empresas vendem reduções de emissões para pagar empréstimos. Segundo o jornal oficial do governo, durante o workshop sobre Política de Crédito e Mercado de Carbono: Desbloqueando Fluxos de Capital Verde, realizado em 14 de outubro, o vice-governador do Banco Central do Vietnã (SBV), Nguyen Ngoc Canh, afirmou que alcançar a meta de emissões líquidas zero até 2050 exige recursos significativos para inovação tecnológica e transição energética. O Decreto nº 29/2026 sobre o mercado interno de carbono, juntamente com a fase piloto em 2025-2026, abrangendo mais de 511 milhões de toneladas de CO2 equivalente em três setores — energia térmica, ferro e aço e cimento — estabeleceu um quadro legal claro. O crédito verde e o mercado de carbono formam, assim, uma ligação sinérgica natural. Especificamente, os bancos fornecem capital para que as empresas instalem equipamentos de economia de energia e tecnologias de baixa emissão. Em contrapartida, o mercado de carbono ajuda a converter a redução das emissões em dinheiro. Essa receita melhora o fluxo de caixa, aumenta a capacidade de pagamento da dívida e reduz diretamente o risco de inadimplência para os bancos. O sistema de Medição, Relato e Verificação (MRV) dos resultados de redução de emissões fornecerá dados transparentes para que as instituições de crédito monitorem a utilização de capital e gerenciem os riscos de empréstimo de forma mais eficaz. Você também pode gostar A sede por centenas de bilhões de dólares em capital e os desafios legais. Os fluxos de capital para setores sustentáveis têm apresentado progressos significativos. No final de junho, o crédito verde em circulação em todo o sistema atingiu mais de 856 trilhões de VND, um aumento de 9,87% em comparação com o final de 2025. O período de 2017 a 2025 registrou uma taxa média de crescimento superior a 20% ao ano. A maior concentração de fluxos de capital está na agricultura , silvicultura, pesca e conservação da biodiversidade (representando mais de 31%), seguida pela energia verde (representando quase 28%). Contudo, a necessidade de capital para a transição verde no Vietname permanece muito elevada. O Sr. Bui Minh Giap, Economista- Chefe do Banco Asiático de Desenvolvimento (BAD) no Vietname, estima que, até 2040, o Vietname necessitará de aproximadamente 368 mil milhões de dólares para a adaptação às alterações climáticas e a redução das emissões, o equivalente a 6,8% do PIB anualmente. Especificamente para o setor elétrico, as necessidades de investimento para a geração e transmissão de energia no período de 2026-2030, de acordo com o Plano de Desenvolvimento Energético VIII revisto, são de aproximadamente 136 mil milhões de dólares. O Sr. Giap observou que os bancos precisam avaliar cuidadosamente a probabilidade de aprovação do crédito, o volume de produção, o preço de venda, os custos de verificação e o cronograma de cobrança antes de incluir a receita de carbono no plano de pagamento da dívida. Do ponto de vista das instituições de crédito, a Dra. Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, Diretora da Escola de Formação de Quadros e Vice-Chefe do Comitê Diretivo de ESG do Agribank , afirmou que o saldo de crédito verde do Agribank atingiu quase 30 trilhões de VND no final de março de 2026. A Dra. Ha sugeriu esclarecer os direitos de propriedade, alienação e compartilhamento de benefícios dos créditos de carbono, aperfeiçoar o arcabouço legal para transações garantidas, contabilidade, tributação e câmbio, e reduzir os custos de verificação para cooperativas e pequenas empresas. Criar canais para mobilizar recursos financeiros internacionais. Você também pode gostar Paralelamente aos esforços nacionais, estão sendo promovidas oportunidades para ampliar o acesso ao capital estrangeiro por meio de mecanismos de negociação de carbono. De acordo com o Carbon Herald, o Fórum de Países Vulneráveis às Mudanças Climáticas e o Grupo de Ministros das Finanças do V20 (CVF-V20), juntamente com a Iniciativa Voluntária para a Integridade do Carbono (VCMI), publicaram recentemente um guia sobre a implementação do Artigo 6 do Acordo de Paris em Bangkok, antes da COP31. Este documento foi desenvolvido para 77 países que enfrentam um déficit estimado de US$ 490 bilhões em financiamento para o desenvolvimento, com o objetivo de mobilizar US$ 20 bilhões adicionais em financiamento de carbono anualmente até 2030. Anteriormente, a participação dos países em desenvolvimento era bastante limitada, com os 45 países menos desenvolvidos representando apenas 1,5% dos projetos no âmbito do Mecanismo de Desenvolvimento Limpo (MDL). Surgiram diversos exemplos práticos. Por exemplo, Gana e Suíça implementaram um acordo que deverá gerar 8 milhões de toneladas de créditos de carbono, arrecadando US$ 300 milhões em receitas de carbono e atraindo US$ 1,1 bilhão em investimentos. As Filipinas firmaram parcerias bilaterais com o Japão e Singapura, enquanto o Butão criou seu próprio fundo climático. A Sra. Usha Rao-Monari, Presidente da VCMI, enfatizou que o manual ajuda os formuladores de políticas a tomarem decisões com base em dados precisos, obtendo assim maior valor econômico ao empreenderem projetos internacionais

artigo.texto: BYD’s next-generation Han sedan has appeared in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) homologation records with three battery-electric vehicle (BEV) configurations and one plug-in hybrid (PHEV). The electric lineup comprises two rear-wheel-drive versions rated at 245 kW and 300 kW, plus an all-wheel-drive version with 520 kW of combined motor output and a top speed of 270 km/h. The PHEV pairs a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine with a 200 kW electric motor. The sedan was spotted undergoing road tests in China in September, with spy shots showing camouflage and a roof-mounted LiDAR unit. Earlier reports speculated that it could sit below the Han L, but the homologated dimensions place the new model above the Han L in length and wheelbase. Dimensions place the Han between Han L and Da Han The new Han measures 5,156 mm long and 1,969 mm wide, with a 3,030 mm wheelbase. Height varies by configuration: 1,492 mm or 1,507 mm. The new Han is 106 mm longer than the Han L and has a 60 mm longer wheelbase. The Da Han is 100 mm longer and has a 100 mm longer wheelbase than the new model. Three battery-electric powertrains The rear-wheel-drive BYD7000CEBEV2 uses a 245 kW permanent-magnet synchronous motor, equivalent to approximately 329 hp. It weighs 2,005 kg and reaches 240 km/h. Roof-mounted LiDAR is optional. The BYD7000CEBEV3 raises motor output to 300 kW (about 402 hp). It weighs 2,125 kg and reaches 240 km/h. Its listed heights are 1,492 mm and 1,507 mm. No LiDAR-delete option is listed. The all-wheel-drive BYD7000CEBEV1 combines a 200 kW front AC asynchronous motor with a 320 kW rear permanent-magnet synchronous motor. Together, they produce a rated output of 520 kW, equivalent to about 697 hp. The vehicle weighs 2,351 kg and reaches 270 km/h. All three BEVs use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) Blade batteries supplied by BYD subsidiary FinDreams Battery. PHEV pairs a 1.5-litre engine with a 200 kW motor The BYD7150CE6HEV1 PHEV uses a 1,498 cc turbocharged petrol engine coded BYD472ZQB. The engine produces 115 kW of maximum power and 110 kW of net power, equivalent to about 148 hp. Its electric motor is rated at 200 kW (about 268 hp). The PHEV weighs 2,115 kg and reaches 200 km/h. A version without roof-mounted LiDAR is available. The engine and motor figures are separate component ratings; the records do not specify combined system power. Braking, EDR and production details All four configurations list Bosch Integrated Power Brake (IPB) equipment and event data recorders (EDRs). The records identify BYD assembly locations in Xi’an, Shaanxi province, and Changzhou, Jiangsu province, but do not assign each configuration to a specific plant. The filling records do not list battery capacity, CLTC driving range, retail pricing or showroom launch dates.

artigo.texto: For once, I have to agree with Cooper Freeman regarding putting a data center in the middle of Cook Inlet. One has to wonder why Louis Wolfson, representing Deep Green, would come to Alaska from Massachusetts and think building a massive data center in Cook Inlet was a good idea. The 32-foot tide alone would be a serious engineering concern! Why would one want to try and permit such a beast? One would have to do a huge number of studies in a very inhospitable environment to be able to convince scientists, permitting experts and the public that your submarine heat pump wouldn’t harm the environment. This will likely be a long process, cost millions of dollars and may or may not be successful in the end (assuming the engineers could design such a thing). Why build at the bottom of Cook Inlet when we have so much land in Alaska? Wolfson should have looked out the window while flying into the Anchorage International Airport and seen all that open land. Here’s a suggestion — why not build a data center on land, far enough away from neighborhoods (since many people aren’t that thrilled about having a data center nearby), but close enough to use the waste heat from the data center to either heat homes or, better yet, grow fresh, hydroponically grown produce? Having a large land-based anchor customer should lower everyone’s power bill if structured properly (much like the Kinross Fort Knox mine’s large baseload power consumption lowers everyone’s monthly electric bill in Fairbanks). If approached this way, a data center would bring real benefits to the general public — Alaskans would certainly welcome lower energy bills and more farm-to-table fresh produce! — Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse, GeoMetallica Inc., Fairbanks Have something on your mind? artigo.texto: The AI Cooling Inflection Point This launches our article series on practical approaches for building scalable, AI-ready environments. AI and high-performance workloads are forcing operators to rethink how data centers are powered, cooled, and scaled. Infrastructure designed for predictable enterprise demand is being pushed beyond its original thermal assumptions. At the center of this shift is cooling. Modern AI workloads create heat densities that traditional air cooling alone can struggle to support efficiently at scale, driving adoption of hybrid architectures that combine air and liquid cooling. This article series examines the technologies, design strategies, and operational realities shaping AI-ready infrastructure, including Trane’s role in helping operators integrate air, chilled-water, and liquid cooling strategies in practical, scalable ways. In the AI era, cooling is no longer just supporting infrastructure. It is becoming a defining factor in whether infrastructure can scale. Introduction The data center industry has reached a major inflection point. Artificial intelligence and high-performance computing are reshaping how infrastructure is designed, powered, cooled, and operated, creating denser and more dynamic workloads. For years, infrastructure evolved gradually. That model has changed. Rack densities have pushed beyond 25 kW and continue climbing, while cooling systems now consume roughly half of total facility power. Modern AI workloads generate concentrated heat that is difficult to manage with traditional approaches alone. Air cooling remains foundational, but as densities rise, many operators are supplementing air-cooled environments with liquid cooling as part of a broader hybrid strategy. This transition introduces new considerations around integration, water management, deployment planning, operational readiness, and lifecycle service, especially in existing facilities. This article series outlines practical approaches for building scalable, AI-ready environments. For Trane, that practical middle ground is central to its value proposition: combining global thermal management expertise, intelligent controls, lifecycle services, and a network of more than 6,000 technicians with LiquidStack’s liquid cooling portfolio. The Physical Limits of Air in the AI Era Airflow is not going away. It remains a critical part of data center design. But AI is changing the equation as heat loads grow more concentrated, which is where hybrid cooling strategies begin to take shape. Modern AI environments generate heat levels that traditional rack designs were never intended to support at scale. As GPU density rises, airflow becomes more difficult to manage, hotspots develop faster, and even small inefficiencies can affect performance, efficiency, and hardware longevity. Operators are already adapting by improving containment, environmental visibility, airflow refinement, and controls while introducing liquid cooling into targeted high-density areas. This is why hybrid cooling architecture is becoming increasingly important. Air still plays a foundational role, but it now works alongside liquid cooling in a more coordinated and workload-aware way. That includes: - Better visibility into airflow behavior at the rack and row level. - Hybrid designs that deploy liquid cooling where it delivers the most value. - Operational models built around continuous monitoring and adjustment. - Intelligent controls that optimize system performance, anticipate maintenance needs, and improve reliability. The takeaway: AI-era cooling is not just about moving more air. It is about building a balanced thermal strategy that supports density, reliability, and long-term scalability. The AI Cooling Inflection Point Today, AI workloads are reshaping the operational profile of the data center, introducing new thermal, power, and infrastructure demands that many legacy environments were never designed to support. AI training, inference, and high-density compute deployments are increasing thermal intensity across enterprise and colocation facilities alike. As a result, airflow management is becoming increasingly important in supporting higher-density AI and HPC workloads. artigo.texto: Optical PCIe Extends the Reach of AI Rack Design Lumentum, Astera Labs, and Corning demoed optical PCIe, which extends reach beyond copper and enables more flexible, disaggregated AI rack designs, though it’s still an early-stage proof of concept. As AI racks become denser and PCIe data rates continue to rise, traditional electrical interconnects face familiar constraints in reach, signal integrity, power, thermal management, and cable density. Optical PCIe is emerging as one possible way to ease some of those pressures. PCIe, or Peripheral Component Interconnect Express, is a widely used architecture that links accelerators, switches, memory, storage, and other devices. Optical PCIe preserves that architecture but carries the signals as light over fiber rather than as electrical signals over copper. At the 2026 OCP Global Summit in San Jose, Lumentum, Astera Labs, and Corning used a rack-level demonstration to show how that approach could work in practice. The setup combined Astera Labs’ Scorpio Smart Fabric Switch, Lumentum’s optical interconnect, and Corning multimode fiber. The links used VCSELs (vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers), which are semiconductor lasers that emit light from the chip surface. Lumentum described the system as a proof of concept, not a product announcement. “Optical PCIe does not eliminate every system constraint, but it can relax several of them by moving data over lightweight, low-loss optical links across longer distances,” Christian Urricariet, senior director of product and strategic marketing at Lumentum, told Data Center Knowledge. Copper’s Limits Become More Apparent as AI Systems Scale One of the clearest pressure points for electrical interconnects is distance. “Given today’s high data rates as well as future even higher data rates, optical connections can span tens to hundreds of meters within a data center,” Joshua Fennimore, commercial technology manager at Corning Optical Communications, told Data Center Knowledge. “Passive copper connections are generally limited to only a few meters, while active copper can extend somewhat farther.” Those constraints become harder to manage as PCIe speeds increase. Urricariet said that higher PCIe data rates make electrical links more sensitive to loss, crosstalk, and equalization requirements over the distances that operators want to support. “Designers may need to add retimers or place connected devices closer together, while high-speed copper cables can become bulky and difficult to route and manage,” Urricariet noted. More Reach Could Reshape Rack and Row Design The practical appeal of optical PCIe is not simply replacing copper with fiber. It is the ability to change where infrastructure can be placed within a rack, or even across multiple racks. Fennimore said copper’s limited reach tends to keep switches and compute hardware physically close together. Fiber, by contrast, gives designers more room to separate those systems while still maintaining high-speed connectivity. “Fiber allows those systems to be separated across racks or rows inside a data center, giving operators greater flexibility to optimize rack layouts around compute density, power, cooling, serviceability, and cable management,” Fennimore said. That added reach could support broader architectural changes as well. Jignesh Shah, senior director of product marketing for the Signal Connectivity Group at Astera Labs, said optical PCIe could enable scale-up designs that span multiple racks rather than being confined to a single enclosure or a short electrical path. “With optical PCIe, reach can be tens of meters, which allows for large scale-up architectures across multiple racks and disaggregated scale-up architectures, with dedicated racks for GPUs, switches, and memory,” Shah told Data Center Knowledge. “Optical PCIe also enables high-density solutions, which are needed for high-radix switches and GPU applications.” In practical terms, the promise of optical PCIe is greater flexibility for system architects. By easing the constraints imposed by the electrical channel budget, Urricariet said, optical PCIe could make it easier to build more modular and composable rack-scale designs, particularly in AI environments where power delivery, thermal limits, and serviceability are becoming just as important as raw performance. Copper Still Has a Strong Role Even as vendors push optical PCIe forward, copper is not going away. For short distances, copper remains the more established and cost-effective choice. According to Shah, once designs move beyond about 3 meters of reach, operators are at a point where it makes sense to evaluate both copper and optical options. “Ultimately, the variables that customers care about come down to power, density, and latency requirements, which can influence a decision between copper and optical,” Shah said. “Optical can support higher density and lower latency, but given copper’s maturity, copper currently offers the best TCO for anything within a few meters.” A Working Demo, Not Yet a Broad Deployment Story For now, the technology remains in its early stages. Urricariet said the OCP demonstration showed fully operational optical links using multiple 32 GB/s channels and an error-free PCIe 5 link in a rack-representative system. But moving from a controlled demonstration to broad deployment will require more than a successful show-floor proof of concept. “Moving from a demonstration to broad deployment requires further work across system integration, reliability, manufacturing, and customer qualification,” Urricariet said. Copper still has a place, and that’s not going to change, but as the demands of AI data centers grow, optical PCIe provides another option. “The goal is not to suggest that every PCIe connection will become optical, but to expand the set of practical system architectures as AI racks grow in scale and complexity,” Urricariet said.

artigo.texto: XBM and SiCAM Technologies join forces to develop a sustainable, ultra-high-density battery technology using locally sourced materials for drones and electric aircraft. Lithium-sulfur cathode developer Xponential Battery Materials (XBM) and silicon-carbon anode specialist SiCAM Technologies have entered into a technology partnership to create a new silicon-sulfur battery materials platform tailored for US battery original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). The collaborative platform will combine SiCAM’s silicon-carbon (Si-C) anode material with XBM’s lithium-sulfur (Li-S) cathode technology and cell architecture. According to the two companies, silicon-sulfur batteries offer significantly higher theoretical energy density compared to conventional lithium-ion cells. The primary components are widely available within the region: silicon is the second most abundant element in the Earth’s crust, while sulfur is produced as a byproduct of US petroleum refining. Whereas most Si-C anode developers rely on silane via a chemical vapour deposition (CVD) process, SiCAM employs trichlorosilane within a fluidized-bed CVD setup. This fluidized-bed method is engineered to form a bonded silicon-composite primary structure, helping to mitigate the 300% swelling typically experienced by silicon during charge and discharge cycles. SiCAM holds the exclusive licence for this patented anode material and is currently working towards commercialising the technology and establishing manufacturing facilities in the US. XBM’s CarbonX cathode material is derived from lignin, a byproduct of the US paper pulping industry. The cathode utilises porous carbon created through a proprietary sol-gel process and infused with sulfur and catalysts, a design intended to enhance sulfur utilisation, extend cycle life, and boost cell-level energy density. Phillip Roberts, co-founder of both SiCAM Technologies and XBM, noted that the collaboration represents a natural step in advancing a sustainable battery vision that bypasses traditional chemistries reliant on mined, costly, and foreign-controlled supply chains. Jon Shan, Chief Technology Officer at XBM, stated that the immediate objective is to refine the high-capacity Li-S cathode and Si-C anode integration. The resulting silicon-sulfur platform will initially target lightweight, high-energy-density eMobility applications, including electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and drones.

artigo.texto: EverWind, a Nova Scotia-based energy infrastructure company, has announced plans for over CA$ 10 billion (US$ 7.09 billion) in private investment for a data center campus at its Point Tupper industrial site while Anthropic has confirmed it has entered into a lease agreement at the campus. As outlined in a press release, the planned investment includes more than CA$ 8 billion (US$ 5.68 billion) to develop, construct, own, and finance the campus. The remaining CA$ 2 billion (US$ 1.42 billion) will be used to expand EverWind’s onshore wind portfolio in Nova Scotia. “Point Tupper has supported industry in the Strait Region for more than 50 years. Today’s announcement represents major new investment in Nova Scotia’s digital and energy infrastructure and highlights the role Nova Scotians can play in driving Canada’s renewed economic ambitions, marking a new chapter for the site and creating opportunities for rural Nova Scotia,” said Trent Vichie, EverWind founder and Chief Executive Officer. The campus plans to have an initial capacity of 95 MW in late 2027 but by 2028, total capacity will balloon to 420 MW. The company also said that the CA$ 2 billion will support its four renewable energy generation projects in Bear Lake, Windy Ridge, Kmtnuk, and Upper Afton. The data center is said to complement EverWind’s plans for green hydrogen and ammonia at Point Tupper. Following EverWind’s announcement, Jacob Glick, Anthropic Head of Public Policy, Canada, announced on LinkedIn that the Claude developer had signed its first data center lease in Canada with EverWind. “Canada and Nova Scotia have both set a high bar for how data centres get built. We’ve signed the federal Responsible Data Centre Development Principles, and we’re committed to meeting Premier Houston’s conditions: protecting ratepayers, safeguarding water and making sure Nova Scotians benefit,” wrote Glick. While not its first lease agreement, the deal is part of a growing trend for the company as it pushes to meet demand for its AI products. As w.media reported in July, Anthropic signed a 20-year lease agreement with US digital infrastructure company TeraWulf. That lease covers 401 MW of critical IT load at a facility in Kentucky and is expected to generate US$ 19 billion in contracted revenue over the initial term. The company also entered into its first data center lease in Australia in September. The AI company has made a long-term commitment at the Western Downs Digital Park in Queensland which is expected to have a peak capacity of 2.16 GW.

artigo.texto: The BYD Atto 3 recently enjoyed a monopoly in Pakistan’s premium EV market. However, that uncontested run is officially over. Lucky Motor Corporation (LMC) just launched the GAC AION V Premium. The company priced it at Rs. 8,899,000. Consequently, this new electric SUV undercuts the Atto 3 by exactly Rs. 91,000. This price difference seems small. Yet, the AION V targets the exact needs of the Pakistani consumer. Furthermore, this launch is part of a massive ecosystem expansion. As we previously reported, LMC officially launched GAC Aion and Hyptec EVs in Pakistan. This strategic partnership brings multiple models, including the affordable Aion UT and the premium Hyptec HT series, directly to the local market. So, why might the GAC AION V dethrone the BYD Atto 3? Let’s break down the facts. A Proper SUV Built for Families Pakistani buyers love large, imposing vehicles. Therefore, they want cars that comfortably seat big families. The BYD Atto 3 acts more like a crossover. It blurs the line of a compact SUV. Meanwhile, the GAC AION V provides a traditional SUV footprint. It stands taller, wider, and longer than its rival. As a result, the AION V delivers superior headroom and excellent rear passenger comfort. Buyers simply get a bigger, more practical vehicle for their money. GAC AION V vs BYD Atto 3: Range Over Powertrain Performance Range anxiety remains a major problem in Pakistan. Public EV chargers are still scarce on the motorways. Therefore, buyers prioritize battery life above all else. GAC understood this assignment perfectly. The AION V features a massive 64.5 kWh LFP “Magazine Battery.” It boasts a claimed NEDC range of 520 km. On the other hand, the BYD Atto 3 uses a smaller 49.92 kWh battery. It offers only 410 km of NEDC range. Consequently, the AION V gives drivers an extra 110 kilometers of peace of mind during inter-city trips. Here is a factual comparison of the two vehicles: The Smart Compromise for Pakistan You might wonder how GAC offers a bigger battery for less money. LMC and GAC made a calculated compromise. They deliberately sacrificed raw motor performance to maximize the vehicle’s range. The BYD Atto 3 produces an aggressive 201 hp and 310 Nm of torque. Conversely, the AION V delivers a modest 134 hp and 240 Nm of torque. However, this power deficit hardly matters in Pakistan. Local drivers rarely take family SUVs to the racetrack. Instead, they care about low running costs, cabin space, and highway stability. A 134 hp motor easily handles daily city traffic. Furthermore, LMC backs this new SUV with official warranties and guaranteed spare parts through its established nationwide network. Previously, imported EV buyers struggled with maintenance. Now, LMC provides essential institutional trust. Ultimately, the BYD Atto 3 remains the top choice for driving enthusiasts. It offers unmatched acceleration in this price bracket. But everyday buyers value space and range much more. Therefore, the GAC AION V perfectly aligns with local market demands. If it performs as advertised, it will easily become Pakistan’s new default electric SUV.

artigo.texto: A Microsoft vai-se retirar do projeto de desenvolvimento de um data center de inteligência artificial (IA) no Reino Unido por preocupações com o fornecimento de energia, segundo avança o jornal “The Guardian”. O empreendimento, que é liderado pela britânica Nscale, previa a criação do maior data center de IA do país, com inauguração prevista para o próximo ano em Essex. Já tinham surgido dúvidas sobre o local escolhido para o projeto, mas a Microsoft, um dos maiores clientes previstos para o projeto, informou à empresa que vai sair do acordo. A decisão ocorreu um mês depois de serem conhecidos problemas no fornecimento de energia, o que iria afetar o início das operações deste projeto. O governo de Keir Starmer destacou este projeto como o “maior data center soberano de IA do Reino Unido”. Com a saída da Microsoft a Nscale perdeu o único cliente anunciado publicamente para o data center. Contudo, um porta-voz da empresa britânica revelou que continuam comprometidos com o projeto e com o Reino Unido e estão a explorar novas fontes de energia para o projeto. artigo.texto: A Microsoft desistiu de um acordo para a utilização de um centro de dados da fornecedora britânica de infraestruturas Nscale. A decisão afeta as instalações planeadas para Loughton, em Essex, e surge na sequência de atrasos significativos na garantia de fornecimento de energia elétrica. Segundo a Reuters, que cita um relatório original do jornal Telegraph, os responsáveis pela rede elétrica nacional britânica alertaram a Nscale de que não existiria capacidade de fornecimento para o centro de dados antes da década de 2030. A gigante norte-americana era considerada um dos dois maiores clientes desta empresa de serviços na nuvem. Impacto e resposta da Nscale Apesar do revés no projeto de Essex, um porta-voz da Nscale desvalorizou a quebra do contrato e garantiu que a relação com a Microsoft se mantém forte e com perspetivas de longo prazo. A fornecedora sublinha que o problema elétrico em redor da região de Londres não afeta os restantes compromissos estabelecidos. A empresa reafirmou ainda a sua dedicação ao mercado do Reino Unido e explicou que está a explorar fontes de energia alternativas para o local, além de procurar outras áreas de expansão no país. A Microsoft recusou comentar o caso de forma oficial. Crescimento e entrada na bolsa A Nscale, que conta com o apoio financeiro da Nvidia, fornece infraestruturas de computação, energia e software para o treino e execução de modelos de inteligência artificial. A empresa concorre no mesmo segmento que a CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe e Lambda, e registou um crescimento acentuado desde o seu lançamento. Num período de apenas dois anos e meio, o valor total dos seus contratos saltou de 100 milhões de dólares para mais de 103 mil milhões de dólares (cerca de 94 mil milhões de euros). No mês passado, a Nscale formalizou o pedido para uma oferta pública inicial nos Estados Unidos. O prospeto da operação apontava precisamente a Microsoft e a Anthropic como os seus principais clientes futuros.

artigo.texto: EXCLUSIVE: As massive data centers rise across the country to power America's artificial intelligence boom, one of the industry's biggest builders is making the case that the benefits extend far beyond the technology inside. During an exclusive tour of Compass Datacenters' sprawling campus in Red Oak, Texas, Fox News Digital got a rare look inside the infrastructure behind the nation's growing appetite for computing. Getting inside took roughly three months' of approvals. Once on site, Fox News Digital passed through six layers of security and suited up in personal protective equipment before entering the facility, where photos and recording devices were prohibited. Beyond the checkpoints, the interior was remarkably clean and surprisingly quiet, with little of the industrial noise one might expect from an operation running around the clock. Inside, rows of towering server racks stretched across the spotless floor, surrounded by the electrical and cooling systems needed to keep the equipment operating. At Red Oak, Compass uses a closed-loop cooling system that recirculates coolant rather than continuously drawing water to cool the equipment. DATA CENTER CEO SHARES THE POWERFUL WAY AMERICAN COMMUNITIES CAN BENEFIT FROM THE NEW TECH BOOM Compass CEO Chris Crosby, a North Texas native, said the Red Oak campus has not used water for cooling since it began operating. "We haven't used water since inception," Crosby said, noting the importance of conserving the region's resources. "Water is precious in North Texas." Beyond cooling, security is another major consideration for facilities housing vast amounts of computing infrastructure. Crosby the extensive security is not about keeping the facilities secret, but rather protecting the sensitive information and critical infrastructure housed inside. "Hacking is real, attacks on infrastructure are real," Crosby said. "If people knew that a bank or a government was operating at a particular facility, they could infiltrate that facility. So that's why the levels of security are so high at our campuses." The campus, roughly 20 miles south of Dallas, will eventually include 10 data center buildings spanning roughly 2.6 million square feet. A Schneider Electric manufacturing facility and a workforce training center operated in partnership with Texas State Technical College are also located on the campus. AMERICA’S NEW BLUE-COLLAR JOB BOOM IS ONE NOBODY SAW COMING — AND IT’S JUST GETTING STARTED Crosby says the development offers a glimpse at an often-overlooked side of America's data center boom: blue-collar jobs. "Data centers are where the economic engine is going to be going forward," Crosby told Fox News Digital, pointing to the jobs, economic activity and tax revenue generated by the industry. Roughly 600 people work for Compass at the campus, while Schneider Electric employs about 300 more, according to Crosby. Thousands of construction workers have also cycled through the development since work began in 2019. And the company says it needs more. "We can't get enough people into this career," Crosby said. That demand helped spur the creation of MEI Pathways, a workforce development program built in partnership with Texas State Technical College. The $12.6 million training facility offers a 12-week program aimed at preparing electricians, mechanics and technicians for jobs in the industry. Building data centers also requires an array of skilled trades, including carpenters, welders and concrete workers. A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES "There was a war on blue-collar jobs for a long time — everybody had to get a four-year degree," Crosby said. "I'm so glad that's over with." Compass has worked with local officials on roads, sewer and other infrastructure and donated $15 million toward a new animal shelter after Ellis County's previous shelter arrangement ended. The investments come as Texas grapples with how to accommodate the enormous electricity demands accompanying the industry's growth while protecting the reliability of its power grid. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Crosby, however, the debate should also account for what is happening outside the server rooms. "I am tired of the elitism that this doesn't create jobs," he said.

artigo.texto: Burgess emphasizes transparency, data center oversight ahead of election Georgia House District 164 candidate discusses priorities if elected You can view Burgess’ full interview with WTOC above. SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - Voters in Georgia’s 164th State House District will decide next month who will represent them. Stephanie Burgess will represent the Democratic party on November’s ticket. “When I thought about what we’re facing right now in the state and even in the nation, I’m like, why not me?” Burgess said. Burgess works as an attorney and said her law experience would be helpful when it comes to public safety policy. She said when looking at current public safety issues, like Flock cameras, she thinks voters are looking at them as larger transparency issues. “I can say that transparency and accountability may not be listed on the ballot, but that’s what’s on the ballot this year,” Burgess said. Data center transparency Burgess said one of her main focuses would be bringing transparency to development, specifically data centers. “If I’m elected, the voters of 164 would have voted me in. And so I would need to promote what their issues are. And if they don’t want a data center, then I’m not voting for a data center,” Burgess said. Balancing growth and cost of living Burgess said balancing development with quality of life and rising costs of living is another priority. “Growth should not harm the people. It should help the people,” Burgess said. If elected, Burgess would be the first Democrat to represent the district in the 29 years Republican Ron Stephens has held it. “We have big issues. I’m a big fighter, and we need big change,” Burgess said. Early voting is underway. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Copyright 2026 WTOC. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: A Ucrânia lançou um ataque massivo contra um porto petrolífero e um centro de dados em São Petersburgo, na Rússia. Um ataque em larga escala com drones, realizado pela Ucrânia nas primeiras horas de 18 de outubro, teve como alvo um porto petrolífero, um centro de dados e uma ponte em São Petersburgo. A Rússia informou que um grande incêndio deflagrou no porto petrolífero e que as forças locais abateram 127 drones. Segundo o Kyiv Independent, num ataque em grande escala ocorrido na noite de 17 de outubro e na madrugada de 18 de outubro, as forças ucranianas alvejaram uma instalação petrolífera, um centro de dados e uma ponte na cidade de São Petersburgo, no noroeste da Rússia. Segundo a mídia estatal russa, drones ucranianos atacaram o porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo e um centro de dados pertencente ao VKontakte (VK), uma das principais redes sociais da Rússia. Segundo o governador de São Petersburgo, Aleksandr Beglov, incêndios deflagraram no porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo e em diversas instalações de infraestrutura civil em outros quatro distritos da cidade. Equipes de resgate foram mobilizadas para combater os incêndios; não há relatos de vítimas. O tráfego aéreo no Aeroporto Internacional de Pulkovo também foi afetado pelo ataque. Entretanto, o governador da região de Leningrado (que circunda São Petersburgo), Aleksandr Drozdenko, anunciou que as defesas aéreas abateram 127 drones ucranianos na área. Detritos de drones danificaram quatro carros em um estacionamento. Também foram relatados incêndios, mas as autoridades ainda não divulgaram a extensão total dos danos. Os canais que monitoram a situação na Ucrânia e na Rússia, Exilenova+ e Supernova+, informaram que o ataque começou por volta das 2h50 da manhã, horário local. Vídeos gravados por moradores de São Petersburgo parecem mostrar drones sobrevoando a cidade, juntamente com sistemas de defesa aérea em operação. Outras imagens mostram explosões iluminando o céu noturno sobre a cidade de cerca de 5,6 milhões de habitantes, localizada a aproximadamente 856 km ao norte da fronteira com a Ucrânia. Alguns vídeos parecem mostrar um drone ucraniano atingindo uma ponte de oito faixas. Outras imagens mostram chamas irrompendo no porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo. Localizado na zona portuária da cidade, o porto petrolífero de São Petersburgo é uma das principais instalações de armazenamento e exportação de combustíveis da Rússia. A instalação movimenta e transporta produtos petrolíferos por via marítima, ferroviária e rodoviária, com uma capacidade de produção estimada em cerca de 12,5 milhões de toneladas por ano. A fabricante ucraniana de drones Fire Point afirma ter usado drones de ataque FP-1 no ataque que teve como alvo o porto petrolífero. O ataque ocorreu depois que o acordo de cessar-fogo sobre instalações de energia entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia, que o presidente dos EUA , Donald Trump, havia anunciado que promoveria, não produziu os resultados esperados. A agência de notícias russa Astra informou que uma subestação elétrica também foi atingida. Houve relatos de falta de energia e baixa pressão da água em algumas áreas, além de danos a um prédio residencial. Essas informações não foram verificadas de forma independente. O jornal Kyiv Independent observou que ainda não era possível verificar de forma independente os alvos atingidos ou a extensão dos danos causados pelo ataque. O ataque em São Petersburgo fez parte da campanha da Ucrânia que utiliza drones de longo alcance para atingir instalações petrolíferas, logística militar e infraestrutura tecnológica em território russo. Nas últimas semanas, Kiev expandiu seus alvos para incluir centros de dados, após dois centros pertencentes à empresa russa de tecnologia Yandex terem sido atacados por drones nos dias 8 e 9 de outubro, interrompendo diversos serviços. Os ataques também ocorreram em um momento em que a Rússia continuava a intensificar seus ataques à infraestrutura energética e tecnológica da Ucrânia, às vésperas do inverno. Em 12 de outubro, Kiev acusou a Rússia de continuar atacando alvos do setor energético, apesar do anúncio do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, de um acordo de cessar-fogo no setor. De acordo com a Ucrânia, atacar instalações petrolíferas poderia pressionar a capacidade de fornecimento de combustível da Rússia, enquanto ataques a centros de dados correm o risco de interromper o funcionamento dos serviços digitais.

artigo.texto: BMW inicia produção em massa de baterias de 6ª geração na China Para promover a industrialização em larga escala, a empresa trabalha em colaboração com fabricantes chineses de baterias O BMW Group deu início oficial à produção em massa de suas baterias de alta voltagem de 6ª geração na 5ª feira (15.out.2026) em Shenyang, capital da Província de Liaoning, no nordeste da China, estabelecendo um marco que destaca um passo fundamental em sua estratégia de eletrificação e localização no país. “O início da produção de baterias é um passo fundamental para trazer os modelos Neue Klasse (Nova Classe) para a China, aproveitando as capacidades sistêmicas da BMW em pesquisa e desenvolvimento, engenharia, compras e produção em Shenyang”, disse Birgit Boehm, presidente e CEO da BMW Brilliance Automotive Ltd. Com um investimento de 10 bilhões de yuans (US$ 1,49 bilhão), o projeto de baterias apresenta um design avançado de células cilíndricas de grande porte. Para promover a industrialização em larga escala dessas células, a BMW tem trabalhado em estreita colaboração com fabricantes chineses de baterias, incluindo a CATL e a EVE Energy. Shenyang é a maior base de produção do BMW Group em todo o mundo. Desde 2010, a BMW investiu mais de 120 bilhões de yuans na cidade, e o veículo de número 7 milhões saiu da linha de produção em maio deste ano. Milan Nedeljković, presidente do conselho de administração da BMW AG, afirmou que as fortes vantagens geográficas de Shenyang, as sólidas bases industriais e o ambiente de negócios favorável incentivaram a BMW a continuar aumentando os investimentos e transformar a base de Shenyang em uma referência para a cooperação industrial mutuamente benéfica entre a China e parceiros estrangeiros. A BMW também anunciou na 5ª feira (15.out) que seu novo BMW i3, desenvolvido especificamente para o mercado chinês, conseguiu fazer um percurso de 1.213 km sem recarga. De acordo com os planos da empresa, cerca de 20 modelos novos e atualizados, equipados com a tecnologia Neue Klasse, chegarão ao mercado chinês até 2027. Até 2030, a BMW pretende elevar a participação dos veículos produzidos localmente e vendidos na China para mais de 95%. A empresa também está avaliando a expansão das exportações de modelos produzidos na China, em Shenyang, para mercados internacionais, incluindo o Sudeste Asiático. Nedeljković disse que a China é o mercado mais dinâmico e competitivo do mundo e que a BMW está comprometida em aprofundar a cooperação mutuamente benéfica e abrir um futuro para a eletrificação junto com a China. Este texto foi publicado originalmente pela Agência Xinhua, em 16 de outubro de 2026. O conteúdo é livre para republicação, citada a fonte, e foi adaptado para o padrão do Poder360.

artigo.texto: AI, Data Centers to Boost Demand for Field Services: ISG Study Infrastructure and connected devices will increase the need for specialized support even as self-healing resolves more incidents, new ISG research finds STAMFORD, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 16, 2026-- A majority of large enterprises expect AI to increase demand for field services until at least the end of 2028, according to a new research report from Information Services Group (ISG) (Nasdaq: III), a global AI-focused technology research and advisory firm. The ISG Market Lens™ 2026 Field Services Report, published today, covers the delivery of onsite and physical technology support across enterprise locations. Between now and the end of 2028, 56 percent of companies responding to a global survey expect AI infrastructure or AI-enabled devices to be significant drivers of additional field services demand. However, AI is also likely to help organizations deliver field services more efficiently: Companies expect one-quarter of field service incidents to be resolved with no human intervention by year-end 2028, up from 14 percent today. ISG AI maturity data indicates that AI is a key enabler of that trend. “AI is changing the game for field services,” said Michael Dornan, ISG principal analyst and co-author of the report. “Enterprises are expanding AI data centers and injecting AI into operations so quickly that the need for field support is escalating. Competing in this new age will require more field service capacity, broader coverage and effective fulfillment models.” The global survey of 200 field services decision-makers at large, mostly multinational enterprises in the Americas and Europe finds that these organizations spend an average of $21 million annually, or approximately $100,000 per supported site. As operations expand across more locations, enterprises report a growing need for improved responsiveness, resilience and customer experience. Amid the growth of AI, data centers are expected to be a hotspot for field services. Data center, network or connectivity expansion was cited by 39 percent of companies as a significant driver of additional need. Legacy system retirement and new security, regulatory or access requirements were also cited by more than one-third of respondents. The mean forecast of demand growth for data centers and technical infrastructure sites is 3 percent, the highest of all operating environments. New technologies are helping to meet increasing demand. Field service technicians remain important, but other interventions such as remote diagnostics and predictive maintenance are reducing avoidable dispatches, the study finds. By the end of 2028, automation or self-healing is expected to be the fastest-growing method of resolving incidents, followed by self-service or digitally guided resolution on site. The percentage of incidents requiring onsite intervention by a technician is expected to fall from nearly 29 percent to just 17 percent and will often involve specialized, time-sensitive work on mission-critical systems. Enterprise satisfaction with field services is generally high in core enterprise environments, such as corporate offices, logistics facilities and data centers, but lower in less central locations. More than one-third of survey respondents said services at remote, low-density or unmanned fixed sites fell short of their expectations, and more than one-quarter were dissatisfied with field services at mobile, fleet and temporary operating locations. While standardized delivery models may serve core locations well, supporting remote sites often requires additional flexibility, ISG says. Expectations for field services differ among organizations, the study finds. The largest group of survey respondents (46 percent) aim for a cost-optimized field service capability that is only differentiated where business-critical needs require it. Another 13 percent want a standardized utility that reliably meets defined requirements. But 36 percent of enterprises seek, above all, high-performing services that minimize downtime and protect user or customer experience in all operations. “As large companies build out increasingly complex environments, cost of support is no longer the only criterion for evaluating field services,” said Angela Kreiter, ISG principal analyst and co-author of the report. “Organizations want partners to help them establish an enterprise-wide operating model that combines internal, outsourced and on-demand resources to meet the requirements at each type of site.” Additional information on the ISG Market Lens Field Services report is available here. About ISG ISG (Nasdaq: III) is a global AI-centered technology research and advisory firm. A trusted partner to more than 900 clients, including 75 of the world’s top 100 enterprises, ISG is a long-time leader in technology and business services that is now at the forefront of leveraging AI to help organizations achieve operational excellence and faster growth. The firm, founded in 2006, is known for its proprietary market data and research, in-depth knowledge and governance of provider ecosystems, and the expertise of its 1,500 professionals worldwide working together to help clients maximize the value of their technology investments. artigo.texto: North Elba approves one-year moratorium on battery energy storage systems NORTH ELBA, N.Y. (WCAX) - North Elba is joining a growing list of Adirondack communities holding off on battery energy storage systems. Town officials voted Tuesday to approve a one-year moratorium. It comes after the town received two solar farm applications that would use around 25 megawatts of power in Ray Brook and include a battery unit. Town Supervisor Rick Preston says they hit pause after realizing their zoning had gaps when it comes to energy projects. However, he says he doesn’t believe the town will consider individual battery applications going forward. “We don’t see a battery energy storage system being suited for North Elba or the village of Lake Placid. We just don’t have the acreage for it,” he said. North Elba’s moratorium now follows similar ones in towns like Champlain and Ticonderoga. Copyright 2026 WCAX. All rights reserved.
