artigo.texto: BYD Racco price in Sri Lanka vs Japan: trims, batteries and range The 3.4-metre BYD Racco electric car costs 11.45 million Sri Lankan rupees, or about $34,600, in Sri Lanka. Claims that its Japanese price is 2.5 times lower are misleading: they compare the export offer with the cheapest Japanese version, although the trims may differ. The Racco went on sale in Sri Lanka on October 9, the model’s first export market after Japan. Official distributor John Keells CG Auto unveiled it in Colombo, Kandy and Galle. The introductory price runs until November 9, 2026; the subsequent price has not been announced. In Japan, the entry-level Racco 200 lists for 2,145,000 yen, the 300 Plus for 2,398,000 yen and the 300 Premium for 2,497,000 yen. Local publication MotorGuide identifies the 11.45-million-rupee offer as the 300 Premium, but the exact export specification still needs confirmation from the distributor. Compared provisionally with Japan’s 300 Premium, the Sri Lankan price is about 2.2 times higher. An accurate comparison requires confirmation of equipment and exchange rates. Import taxes, transport and local pricing also matter; the entire difference cannot be attributed to a manufacturer markup. The four-seat Racco has sliding rear doors and a 47-kW electric motor, equivalent to around 64 metric horsepower. In Japan, the 300 Premium has a 35.84-kWh LFP battery and a claimed 320-km WLTC range; the Racco 200 has a 22.4-kWh battery and a rated 210 km under the same cycle. Export specifications need local confirmation. The Racco was developed to meet Japan’s kei-car size rules. It measures 3,395 mm long and 1,475 mm wide. It competes with small local city cars in Japan, while its Sri Lankan launch signals BYD’s interest in exporting vehicles in this class. Despite the high local price, distributor John Keells CG Auto aims to sell 3,000 Raccos over the next 12 months, according to EconomyNext. November 9 will be the next price milestone, when the introductory offer expires and a new price may be announced. This English edition was prepared using AI translation under editorial oversight by SpeedMe. The original reporting is by Polina Kotikova

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- Batteries are the heart of the new-energy vehicle industry, making monthly battery data a vital barometer of the sector's health. The latest September 2026 data from the China Automotive Power Battery Innovation Alliance (the "Battery Alliance") shows that China's power and energy storage battery production and sales remain elevated, exports show continued resilience, and the installation mix keeps tilting toward lithium iron phosphate (LFP). Behind the surging numbers lies more than arithmetic — it’s the simultaneous evolution of demand dynamics, technology pathways, and the broader market landscape. Production and Sales Hit Highs, Energy Storage Opens a Second Growth Curve Battery Alliance data shows combined production of power and energy storage batteries hit 237.8 GWh in September — edging up 0.3% from August and jumping 57.3% from a year earlier. Output for the first nine months totaled 1,833.1 GWh, a 63.4% annual gain. Source: China Automotive Power Battery Innovation Alliance (same below) By operational rhythm, monthly output has settled onto a high plateau, with the first three quarters' production and sales already surpassing last year's full-year totals. Rather than easing as the base effect climbs, the industry is maintaining strong utilization rates, propelled by unleashed demand and overseas orders. The structural shifts on the sales side warrant a closer look. Combined sales reached 222.7 GWh in September — slipping 0.2% from August but surging 52% year-on-year. Power battery sales stood at 149.2 GWh, making up 67% of the total, a 1.7% monthly gain and a 35% annual jump. Energy storage battery sales hit 73.5 GWh, claiming a 33% share and more than doubling with a 104.4% annual increase. For the first nine months, energy storage sales totaled 595.4 GWh — a 111.8% year-on-year surge — claiming 35.4% of overall sales, up 9.1 percentage points from a year earlier. If power batteries anchor the baseline through the EV market, energy storage is emerging as the industry’s second growth curve. As storage use cases multiply, battery makers are unlocking new shipment channels beyond passenger cars. Within the LFP chemistry, storage has become a critical growth driver: LFP claimed a full 100% of energy storage sales in September, and nearly 99.97% across the first nine months. The divergence in technology pathways is equally stark. LFP output reached 202.4 GWh in September, capturing an 85.1% share and climbing 69.4% year-on-year; ternary output stood at 35.0 GWh, taking 14.7%. This isn't a simple substitution — it's the combined outcome of cost, safety, cycle life, and supply chain maturity. Corporate performance is diverging, too. While overall power and storage sales jumped 52% in September, EVE Energy, Gotion High-Tech, and Sunwoda outpaced the industry average. On the power battery side, where sales climbed 35%, the same trio beat the mean. Top players are defending share through customer ties and scale, while second-tier rivals chase growth elasticity via storage contracts and overseas orders. Exports, meanwhile, have opened another growth avenue. Combined exports reached 44.0 GWh in September, edging up 3.7% from August and surging 64.5% year-on-year to account for 19.7% of the month’s sales. Power battery exports totaled 28.4 GWh — a 60.9% annual jump — while storage shipments hit 15.6 GWh, climbing 71.4%. For the first nine months, cumulative exports stood at 302.9 GWh, up 51.6% from a year earlier. Driven by rising vehicle exports and the ramp-up of overseas plants, Chinese battery makers are evolving from simply shipping products abroad to building out global footprints and industrial synergies. Installations Gain Momentum, LFP Solidifies as the Dominant Chemistry Surging production, sales, and exports ultimately face their proving ground at the installation stage. Domestic power battery installations reached 87.2 GWh in September, advancing 10.4% from August and 14.7% year-on-year. First-nine-month installations totaled 576.3 GWh, a 16.7% annual gain. While far milder than the 50%-plus growth on the production and sales side, the installation pace more closely mirrors the real consumption rhythm of China’s EV market. By chemistry, LFP’s dominance only deepened. September installations hit 74.5 GWh — an 85.5% share and a 19.9% annual gain — while ternary slipped to 12.3 GWh, claiming 14.1% and dropping 10.9% year-on-year. Over the first nine months, LFP installations totaled 477.2 GWh for an 82.8% share, climbing 18.5%; ternary managed 97.9 GWh, or 17%. LFP’s grip on the market is backed by authoritative voices. Citing academician Ouyang Minggao, Zhang Yongwei, president of the China EV 100 Research Institute, recently noted that LFP will remain dominant among liquid batteries, with shipments already surpassing 1 TWh. Looking ahead, hybrid solid-liquid and sodium-ion batteries are expected to scale up faster over the next two years. Sodium-ion, in particular, is already gaining commercial traction in energy storage, low-speed vehicles, and start-stop applications. All-solid-state batteries, meanwhile, remain in the engineering validation phase and are unlikely to reach scale until around 2030. That doesn’t render the ternary route obsolete. For premium long-range, high-performance, or cold-climate applications, ternary cells retain a clear edge in energy density. Among battery-electric passenger cars in September, those packing 140 to 160 Wh/kg accounted for 50% of the mix, while those at 160 Wh/kg or above claimed 8.1%. These high-density segments still leave room for diverse chemistries. September’s installation rankings confirm that top players still call the shots. CATL led with 35.49 GWh and a 40.92% share, trailed by BYD at 18.29 GWh and 21.09%. CALB, EVE Energy, and Gotion High-Tech followed, installing 6.04 GWh, 5.03 GWh, and 4.87 GWh, respectively. artigo.texto: [Liruiwei Unveils High-Performance RISC-V Everest 200 Chip for Intelligent Computing Centers] During the sixth RISC-V China Summit, ZTE Microelectronics' subsidiary Liruiwei unveiled the Everest 200, a high-performance RISC-V CPU chip built for intelligent computing centers, marking its first public appearance. The Everest 200 is the industry's first RISC-V CPU chip designed for intelligent computing center scenarios, focusing on three key use cases: Agent clusters, inference supernode hosts, and enterprise-grade hybrid intelligent computing inference. It natively features RISC-V AI instruction acceleration and is deeply optimized for KV Cache and long-context large model inference. The chip integrates multiple acceleration engines for Matrix, Vector, compression, and encryption, and supports high-speed interconnect interfaces including DDR5, PCIe, and CXL. It is compatible with MoE large model hybrid inference solutions using native RISC-V AI plus GPU accelerator cards. Detailed product specifications for the Everest 200 will be officially released at the end of this year.

A cantora Iza, que deixou o posto, foi responsável pela coroação. Ela entregou a faixa à atriz e as duas deram um beijo. Para a ocasião, a atriz apostou em um figurino com pedrarias verdes, em referência às cores da escola. “Voltar não estava nos meus planos. Mas foi olhando o carnaval de um pouco mais longe que percebi o tamanho do meu amor por ele. O carnaval tá no meu corpo, nas minhas lembranças, no jeito que eu sinto alegria. Como é que a gente se despede completamente de uma coisa que faz parte da gente?”, escreveu a atriz no Instagram. continua após a publicidade Antes de assumir o posto na Imperatriz, Paolla foi rainha de bateria da Grande Rio até 2025, escola pela qual desfilou por cinco anos. Na ocasião, Paolla Oliveira afirmou que precisava se dedicar às gravações de Vale Tudo, novela da TV Globo em que interpretou Heleninha Roitman, e aos cuidados com o pai, diagnosticado com demência frontotemporal. continua após a publicidade Ela foi substituída por Virginia Fonseca, que permaneceu apenas um ano no posto. Atualmente, Anitta é a rainha de bateria da Grande Rio. artigo.texto: BYD India Introduces Limited-Edition Sealion 7 Premium with New Interior The BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition continues to deliver 308.4 bhp and a claimed 567km NEDC range, alongside a 15.6-inch touchscreen and 11 airbags. BYD India has launched the Sealion 7 Festive Edition at Rs 50.60 lakh (ex-showroom), adding a new interior colour combination to its electric SUV range for the festive season. The limited-edition model is based on the Sealion 7 Premium and will be available in only 150 units. Its main change is the Tan and Black cabin, which distinguishes it from the standard version. The new edition retains the Premium variant’s battery, performance figures, equipment, and safety features, meaning the update focuses on the cabin rather than mechanical changes. Also Read: BYD Denza India Entry Confirmed; Here's What to Expect BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition: What's New? Apart from the Tan and Black interior, the rest of the cabin equipment remains unchanged, including quilted Nappa leather seats, a 15.6-inch rotating touchscreen, a panoramic glass roof with an electric sunshade, and a head-up display. BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition: Battery, Range and Performance The BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition uses the same 82.56kWh Blade Battery as the Premium variant. The battery incorporates BYD's Cell-to-Body (CTB) technology, which integrates the battery structure with the vehicle's body, while Intelligent Torque Adaptation Control (iTAC) manages torque distribution. The electric SUV produces 308.4bhp and 380Nm of torque. BYD claims a 0-100km/h acceleration time of 6.7 seconds and a range of 567km under the NEDC test cycle. BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition: Safety and Features Safety equipment includes 11 airbags, and the Sealion 7 has received a five-star safety rating from Euro NCAP. The SUV also offers a range of technology and comfort features, including the rotating infotainment display and head-up display. Also Read: BYD Sealion 7 Dynamic Launched at Rs 41.90 Lakh in India; Claims 520km Range The BYD Sealion 7 Festive Edition will only be available exclusively in the Premium configuration.

artigo.texto: Paolla Oliveira será coroada rainha de bateria da Imperatriz neste sábado O evento acontece na quadra da agremiação de Ramos com feijoada e shows de Iza, Jorge Aragão e Xande de Pilares, com transmissão ao vivo a partir das 16h A atriz Paolla Oliveira, 44, será coroada rainha de bateria da escola de samba Imperatriz Leopoldinense, no Rio de Janeiro, neste sábado (17), durante a feijoada da agremiação de Ramos, a partir das 13h. Os ingressos para o evento estão esgotados. Nas redes sociais, a nova majestade abriu o coração e falou sobre a ansiedade para a coroação. "Estou animada, um pouquinho nervosa", confessou na sexta-feira (16), em um story compartilhado pelo Mestre Lolo, responsável por comandar os ritmistas. "Mas, passando isso aí, é só alegria", emendou. Mais tarde, Paolla também publicou um vídeo com uma série de registros dos ensaios e comentou a expectativa para voltar à Marquês de Sapucaí em 2027. "Fiquei pensando, acho que não vou conseguir cruzar a avenida de novo. É muita coisa! A rainha está de volta, real. A gente nunca sabe o jeito de fazer, o jeito que vai dar certo, o jeito que é bom. A gente só sabe depois que é, né?", refletiu. Para animar o público, a festa contará com apresentação de Jorge Aragão, Xande de Pilares e Iza, que ocupava o cargo até o último ano. Ver esse post no Instagram Relembre o anúncio de Paolla Oliveira na Imperatriz A atriz foi anunciada publicamente como nova rainha de bateria no dia 23 de setembro. Em comunicado divulgado à imprensa, Catia Drumond, presidente da Imperatriz, afirmou ter certeza de que Paolla chega para somar ao time e, principalmente, à comunidade de Ramos e toda a Zona da Leopoldina. "Que ela seja muito bem-vinda e, claro, muito feliz conosco." Em 2025, Oliveira fez seu último desfile à frente da bateria da Grande Rio. Ao anunciar a decisão, ela disse que a escolha estava sendo difícil, mas que precisava "pensar em redistribuir sua atenção" em outras áreas da vida, como, por exemplo, a parte pessoal. Após um ano longe da folia, Paolla volta para reinar diante dos ritmistas comandados pelo mestre Lolo. "O Carnaval vive em mim, vocês sabem. E a vida tem essa beleza do inesperado, em que a gente percebe que pode ainda ter muita coisa bonita para viver, sem nunca perder de vista tudo o que já foi vivido", disse ela à imprensa. "Estou muito feliz de estar aqui, de coração aberto e para começar mais uma história no carnaval. Chego com muito respeito, vontade de estar perto, conhecer, aprender e viver mais uma vez essa experiência rica e coletiva. Tem frio na barriga, claro, mas tem também uma alegria enorme por tudo que está começando", acrescentou. Com o enredo “A Memória do Rei e o Sumiço de Dona Júlia”, idealizado pelo carnavalesco Leandro Vieira, a Imperatriz Leopoldinense será a quarta escola a desfilar na Marquês de Sapucaí, fechando a segunda-feira de Carnaval, 8 de fevereiro, em busca do 10º título de sua história.

artigo.texto: Global clean energy brand BLUETTI showcased its portable power stations, residential energy storage systems, and commercial and industrial (C&I) energy solutions at the 140th Canton Fair, held from October 15 to 19, 2026. The exhibition highlighted the company’s products for personal, household, and business use while opening opportunities for partnerships with distributors and energy providers worldwide. The showcase covered solutions ranging from portable backup power to integrated solar, battery storage, and electric vehicle (EV) charging systems. BLUETTI also highlighted a pay-as-you-go financing model intended to make energy solutions more accessible to households and small businesses. Why it matters: Portable power and energy storage can help households and businesses manage power interruptions, while solar-powered systems offer another way to meet electricity needs. BLUETTI’s range of products also reflects the different requirements of individual users, residential customers, and commercial operations. The details: For portable power, BLUETTI presented its PREMIUM series, designed for outdoor activities, recreational vehicle travel, and home backup. It also showcased the Pioneer 5000, a professional portable power station rated for 5,000W of continuous output. The company said the Pioneer 5000 is designed for applications such as construction sites, equipment rental businesses, and agricultural operations. BLUETTI’s portable power solutions use lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery technology and support features such as fast charging, solar input, and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) protection. These features are intended to provide flexibility for users who need power in outdoor, residential, and professional settings. The bigger picture: BLUETTI also highlighted its HomeStar residential energy storage series, which supports AC and solar charging alongside app-based smart energy management. The company said these systems can serve households, clinics, and small businesses that need backup power. Another focus was BLUETTI’s integrated pay-as-you-go (PAYGO) solution, which uses flexible installment payments to make energy products more affordable. The BLUETTI GO platform supports digital operations management for the system. The company is inviting global partners to join its PAYGO solar network. Through platform integration, product deployment, and local distribution partnerships, BLUETTI aims to reach underserved households and micro-businesses, particularly in emerging markets. Between the lines: The PAYGO model is a key part of BLUETTI’s effort to expand beyond customers who can pay the full cost of an energy system upfront. Flexible payments may lower the initial financial barrier for eligible customers, while local distribution partners can help bring products to specific markets. However, the announcement does not provide detailed financing terms, eligibility requirements, or confirmed deployment plans for the Philippines. For businesses: BLUETTI’s commercial and industrial portfolio includes energy storage systems ranging from 64kWh to 240kWh, alongside integrated solar, storage, and EV charging solutions. The company said these systems can support peak shaving, energy arbitrage, backup power for critical loads, and flexible capacity expansion. By coordinating solar generation, battery storage, and EV charging demand, businesses may be able to manage peak electricity use, reduce reliance on the grid, and maintain operations during power disruptions. The potential benefits will depend on each installation’s energy demand, system configuration, local electricity rates, and operating conditions. What’s next: BLUETTI plans to strengthen its partnerships with distributors, energy developers, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractors, and other industry participants worldwide. The company aims to expand the deployment of its energy solutions across markets with different power requirements and business opportunities. BLUETTI reports serving more than 3.5 million customers worldwide and says it will continue developing products for personal, residential, and commercial applications. The Bottom Line: BLUETTI used the 140th Canton Fair to present its broader energy portfolio, from portable power stations and residential storage to large-scale commercial systems and PAYGO solar solutions. Its next steps focus on building global partnerships and expanding access to energy products for households and businesses. Get the latest from WALASTECH directly on your Google feed. artigo.texto: DCF Global: The Nordics' AI Boom Meets the Power Test Key Highlights - Finland's grid operator reports nearly 5 GW of eventual data center capacity associated with signed connection agreements, underscoring the scale of the country's AI infrastructure ambitions. - JLL, CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield and datacenterHawk research points to growing Nordic investment appeal, alongside significant questions about power availability, preleasing and project execution. - The region's experience offers an increasingly relevant comparison with North America, where power delivery, infrastructure costs and community acceptance are similarly reshaping data center development. The Nordic countries have long occupied a distinctive position in the global data center industry. Their appeal rests on a familiar combination of cool climates, comparatively abundant low-carbon electricity, political stability, and sophisticated energy and communications infrastructure. Now, the accelerating demand for AI computing is transforming that established proposition into something considerably larger. Across Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Iceland, hyperscalers, AI cloud providers, infrastructure developers and institutional investors are advancing a new generation of high-density data center projects. Their ambitions increasingly extend beyond conventional cloud regions and enterprise colocation into multihundred-megawatt AI campuses and integrated energy infrastructure. The scale of that transformation is particularly evident in Finland, where the country's transmission system operator, Fingrid, reported in August that data center projects with signed grid-connection agreements represented nearly 5 gigawatts of planned eventual capacity. That figure encompasses projects connected to transmission and distribution networks. It does not represent operating data center capacity, nor does a connection agreement guarantee that a project will be completed at its proposed size. Nevertheless, it illustrates the extraordinary volume of investment now being directed toward a country that, until recently, occupied a secondary position behind Sweden and Norway in the Nordic data center market. The acceleration comes with a paradox. The electricity resources, industrial sites and favorable environmental conditions attracting AI developers are also becoming subjects of increasingly consequential public-policy decisions. Finland has raised electricity taxes on data centers and is considering changes to grid-connection priorities. Denmark has already introduced a system that places most large data center projects in a lower-priority category for constrained grid capacity. Meanwhile, investment continues to accelerate. For the Nordics, the central question is no longer whether the region can attract AI infrastructure development. It is how much of the announced capacity can be financed, permitted, connected and ultimately brought into production without compromising the energy-system advantages and sustainability commitments on which the market's appeal depends. Finland Moves to the Center of Europe's AI Infrastructure Map The strongest evidence of Finland's changing position came in September, when Google announced plans to invest €13 billion in Finnish digital infrastructure and related projects over 2027 and 2028. The investment encompasses operations and planned development in Hamina, Muhos, Vaala and Kajaani, extending Google's presence beyond its established Hamina campus. At the same time, Google and Finnish energy company Fortum announced a 22-year nuclear power purchase agreement covering up to 50% of the generating capacity at the Loviisa nuclear power plant. The arrangement provides financial support for extending the plant's operating life through 2050, while the companies have also agreed to explore additional nuclear generation, renewable energy and grid-flexibility solutions. The agreement underscores the growing relationship between AI infrastructure development and long-term commitments to power generation, illustrating how large technology customers are becoming increasingly influential participants in regional electricity markets. Google is far from alone. In early September, Cerebras Systems and Compute Nordic Finland announced a 165 MW AI data center development in Mikkeli, with construction already underway on an initial 50 MW phase. Unlike many early-stage development announcements, the Mikkeli project is supported by a series of seven-year contracted capacity agreements. The distinction matters: committed customer demand provides a stronger indication of potential project delivery than land acquisition or preliminary power arrangements alone. More recently, French AI infrastructure developer Sesterce announced a proposed $10 billion, 600 MW campus in Jämsä, beginning with a planned 200 MW first phase. The project would redevelop the former Kaipola paper mill, illustrating a recurring Nordic development strategy: converting established industrial properties into locations for computational infrastructure. Sesterce says it has secured an anchor customer and plans to pair the campus with commitments concerning additional renewable generation, closed-loop cooling and recycled-water use. Those commitments remain to be demonstrated as the project advances. Another emerging participant, Applied Digital, has secured an agreement providing access to as much as 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland. However, the company has not announced a customer for the site and is continuing to market the development, with initial power availability anticipated in 2028. Nordic operator atNorth has also announced plans for a 75 MW initial phase at its FIN05 campus in Salo, with a potential expansion pathway to 230 MW. The company says power for the first phase has been secured, with initial operations targeted for 2028. Taken together, these developments establish Finland as a major destination for AI infrastructure investment.

artigo.texto: Data center fervor is sweeping Central Florida, as voters pressure political leaders to keep the massive hubs of network infrastructure out of their cities and counties for fear they’ll gobble up local water resources and lead to higher electricity prices. And whether it’s in Florida’s governor race or local contests, candidates are being pinned down in forums and interviews for their positions on so-called hyper-scale data centers that polling shows voters loathe. A July University of North Florida poll found 68% of Florida voters disapprove of data centers being built in their area, including 84% of Democrats surveyed and 52% of Republicans. But perhaps most important in numerous races thought to be closely contested, 76% of voters with no party affiliation also don’t support them. Few people surveyed like data centers, the sprawling facilities that power artificial intelligence, among other things, said Sean Freeder, the director of the UNF Public Opinion Research Lab. “It’s the only question in the last several years in our polling where majorities dislike it across the board,” he said. “Democrats and independents are similar: They utterly hate them.” There are no hyper-scale centers in Central Florida, though a developer is marketing land in a rural section of Osceola County as a good site for one of the 5,000+ server facilities that are the focus of public ire. That’s prompted a petition urging county officials to turn down any such request should a data center developer try to buy the land. At least two other counties are considering moratoriums on data centers, even without any proposals in the pipeline. Data centers also have become one of the defining issues in the race to be Florida’s governor between Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly, who have staked out significantly different positions on the issue. Donalds has offered some conditional support while Jolly, labeling his opponent “Data Center Donalds,” says he doesn’t want them in Florida. Complaints about the facilities range from how much water and electricity they consume to the constant noise of loud cooling fans measuring 100 decibels or more. Donalds has said he supports existing state law that allows cities and counties to determine for themselves whether or not to build data centers in their jurisdictions and says that utility rates cannot increase because of a hyperscale data center. He also has said he wants Florida to regulate how close such a facility can be to homes. After New York passed a one-year moratorium on large-scale centers, Donalds said that’s not the right approach for Florida. “But you also have to understand that when you start doing stuff like what New York just did, that’s a signal to the business community that this is not a place to invest capital,” he said. “This is not a place to invest in businesses, and so we have to be balanced and be mindful about that.” But the tech industry and data center developers have also been a major support of Donalds — with $6 million in direct donations and advertising support from donors such as utilities like Next Era and Duke Energy, as well as firms like Google and Meta, according to the state government watchdog website Seeking Rents. Jolly and Florida Democrats have tried to use the issue as they work to win the governor’s mansion for the first time in 30 years. After dubbing the Republican with the data center nickname, they use it frequently in online campaign ads. Jolly has said he would implement a one year moratorium on new data centers if elected. In an interview last month with the Orlando Sentinel, Jolly made his strategy clear: “Every time I open my mouth it’s ‘Housing, health care, education and no data centers,’” he said. “That’s it.” Florida Democrats this week hosted what they called the Data Center Donalds tour, stopping in downtown Orlando for a news conference. “Ultimately, data centers are not here to create new jobs; they’re here to exploit our resources, to impact our quality of life in a negative way and do it so that a handful of oligarchs can continue to be rich and wealthy while the rest of us struggle,” Rep. Anna Eskamani, D-Orlando, said. This comes as local governments across the state, including those dominated by Republicans, grapple with how to handle data center proposals. For instance, in conservative Lake County, last month the Board of County Commissioners enacted a 90-day pause on any new data centers. But the board this week asked its staff to draw up an ordinance that would allow them under a conditional use permit, which would mean any proposed center would require a vote by the commission. In Democrat-controlled Orange County, commissioners signaled last month they were likely to impose a moratorium on any new hyperscale data centers, though they haven’t yet voted to do so. Both candidates on the ballot next month for mayor, Tiffany Moore Russell, a Democrat, and Chris Messina, a Republican, have said they support a moratorium. Last month, several dozen speakers addressed commissioners urging them to support such restrictions. Toward the end of public comment, one resident, Angie Hatfield, made it plain. “As elected officials, if you don’t vote yes on a data moratorium, who are you representing?” she said. In Osceola, the commercial real estate firm CBRE is marketing 2,232 acres off Canoe Creek Road in Kenansville as “Florida’s premier hyperscale data center development site.” The listing notes it includes 1,066 buildable acres, with electrical service by Duke Energy and “significant water resources permitted.” The listing has drawn opposition in the form of a petition with more than 600 signatures. It urges Osceola County’s Board of County Commissioners to reject the project, if it comes forward. “They should reject the data center, and no vote should happen without public hearings and full disclosure of its water use, energy demands and environmental impact,” it reads. artigo.texto: Maharashtra State Power Generation Co. Ltd., Mumbai, India (MAHAGENCO) has issued a 500 MW/1,600 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) tender with two-hour and four-hour storage across Maharashtra. It envisions developing the project under a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model, including Operation & Maintenance (O&M) for 15 years. It has sought online bids until November 5, 2026. It plans to develop six battery energy storage systems (BESS) totaling 500 MW/1,600 MWh. It includes developing 100 MW/400 MWh units each in Uran (Raigad district), Koradi, Nashik, and Khaperkheda. The tender also includes developing a 50 MW/100 MWh BESS project each at Chandrapur (Lakhmapur) and Parli, connected to MSETCL STU substations (33 kV and above). Each bidder must submit the bid processing fee of Rs. 10 lakh plus 18% GST for the total project capacity quoted via NEFT/RTGS to MAHAGENCO's account. The EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) or bid security for the project is Rs. 5 lakh/MW. Previous BESS Projects in Maharashtra Previously, companies such as Oriana Power Limited and GK Energy Limited won a combined Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity of 1,050 MW / 2,100 MWh from MSEDCL. They secured this capacity under MSEDCL’s 2,000 MW / 4,000 MWh BESS tender, which was awarded within a month of its issuance. Oriana Power received two Letters of Award (LoAs) from MSEDCL to establish 900 MW / 1,800 MWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in Maharashtra. Under these two LoAs, Oriana Power’s capacity is divided into 500 MW / 1,000 MWh and 400 MW / 800 MWh, respectively. GK Energy Limited also secured a BESS project after receiving a Letter of Award (LoA) from MSEDCL to set up a 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS project with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support. Under this tender, the company was awarded the project at a tariff of Rs. 2,38,000/MW/month, resulting in an annual revenue of Rs. 42.84 crore (excluding GST) for 15 years from the commercial operation date (COD).

artigo.texto: With the Nov. 3 general election coming up, NHPR is sitting down with the candidates for governor to discuss top issues in the race and ask questions submitted by listeners and readers. Cinde Warmington, an attorney and former executive councilor from Concord, is the Democratic nominee. Here are some takeaways from her interview with NHPR. A full transcript of this conversation with All Things Considered host Julia Barnett follows below. On housing - Warmington said she would create a new state position of “housing czar” to focus on housing inventory and affordability. - She also promised investments in the Affordable Housing Fund, a state-administered loan program managed by New Hampshire Housing, to leverage federal funds. On data centers - Warmington is calling for an immediate moratorium on AI data centers in New Hampshire. She said the state needs to protect itself from skyrocketing electric rates and begin environmental impact studies as needed. On local or state agreements with ICE - “At the state level I do not believe that we should be cooperating with an organization that has been shown to be lawless, to be putting masked thugs on the street, terrorizing communities around our state.” On her past work as an opioid company lobbyist - Warmington said her representation of Purdue Pharma was 25 years ago. She said the pharmaceutical company lied to doctors and the FDA. - “I've been very, very clear that if I had known at the time what we all learned later, I would have had nothing, nothing to do with this work. And I certainly regret having anything to do with this work, knowing what we all know now.” What questions do you have about this year's elections? Let us know at voices@nhpr.org, and we could help you get the answers. Find all of our 2026 election coverage here. This transcript has been lightly edited for clarity. Rising housing costs continue to be a major issue for Granite Staters. As governor, what new ideas would you bring to address the housing crisis here? Well, as you said, housing costs are through the roof here. We've hit record highs under Kelly Ayotte's administration. I'm hearing about it everywhere I go across the state. Young people who can't afford to buy a home. Young people who can barely afford to pay rent. I'm hearing from seniors who are having trouble staying in their homes because of the skyrocketing property taxes, yet there's no place for them to downsize to. There's just no place for them to go. Small businesses, large businesses can't hire people because of the housing crisis in our state. This really needs to be taken head on. You may know that in our state, we actually have nobody accountable for knowing how many housing units we have, how many we need, and how we're going to get there. So first thing is, we're going to put in a housing czar who is going to be accountable for making sure we have a plan going forward. We're going to invest in the Affordable Housing Fund, because that's a fund where for every dollar we invest, we can leverage three federal dollars for that. We have been leaving millions of dollars on the table that should be invested in the Affordable Housing Fund, and we're going to fund that Housing Champions program, which was working so well. Almost half of our housing starts came from Housing Champions communities last year, and Kelly Ayotte defunded that program. There's so many more. We need to have all stakeholders at the table, but this is an all hands on deck problem that we need to tackle head on. And the state has struggled with a tight budget historically. Where would this money come from to support these efforts? This money was in the budget. And Kelly Ayotte decided to defund, for instance, the Housing Champions program. This is a matter of priorities and where you're going to put the priorities. Housing is a number one issue in the state, and it is going to affect not only the ability of people to stay here and raise their families here, but it affects the viability of our economy going forward. We absolutely have to be invested in this. As winter approaches, many folks are facing soaring fuel and electricity costs on top of other affordability concerns they may already have. What will you do as governor to help mitigate energy costs for Granite Staters, both in the short and long term? Well, I mean, first thing, we have to stand up and speak out about why energy costs are through the roof right now. As you mentioned, gas prices, heating oil prices are through the roof. That is largely because of Donald Trump's reckless war and his tariffs, both of things that Kelly Ayotte has simply refused to stand up and speak out about and defend Granite Staters. Also skyrocketing electric prices, up 15% since Kelly Ayotte came into office, due largely because of her failed energy policies that just are simply hostile towards energy efficiency and renewable energy. That's where we need to be putting the emphasis so that we have an energy policy for the future that will make sure we are bringing down electric rates and not also appointing people to our public utilities commission, who will continue to cater to the utilities. We need people on that commission that are looking out for our ratepayers. And when it comes to renewables, you've proposed getting to net-zero emissions by 2040. That's 14 years away. How realistic is that? Well, I proposed 2040 in the last election, and that is when we had sort of record investments by the federal government in helping communities to do that. Under the Trump administration, of course, that money has gone away. So they've made the 2040 date impossible. But there needs to be a date out there somewhere where we are decreasing our dependence on fossil fuels. I do want to clear up a misunderstanding or a misrepresentation of my position. I am not against all emissions. I'm not against gas-powered cars. I am not against gas stoves. I cook with a gas stove myself. And net zero does not mean zero.

She adds that many incentives that go towards data centers are actually from local governments instead of the state.

artigo.texto: Pro-Russian accounts targeting Ukrainians on Facebook and Telegram sharply declined after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers, according to a new report from a Ukrainian government agency. It’s the most direct evidence so far behind a claim that went viral last week, but it falls well short of proving it. The report comes from Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), which operates under the country’s National Security and Defense Council. It was published Oct. 15, and United24 Media covered it on Oct. 17. The CCD used software from the Ukrainian security firm Osavul to track accounts it flagged as showing "signs of inauthentic behavior." According to Osavul's website, the firm "builds AI-powered risk intelligence for hybrid threats." According to United24, the CCD analyzed 22,664 messages from 5,201 accounts posted between Oct. 6 and 12, across 26 topics in Ukraine’s information space. The report found two sharp drops in activity, each following a strike that fully shut down a Yandex facility. On Oct. 8, the day a fire took Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, offline, messages fell 83.6 percent, from 4,032 to 660. The number of active accounts fell by a similar share. Activity rebounded past pre-strike levels by Oct. 10, but on Oct. 12, a day after a strike fully halted operations at a Yandex data center in Vladimir, messages fell by 42.6 percent and active accounts dropped by 41 percent. A smaller group of 98 accounts that posted pro-war propaganda, conspiracy theories, or calls for violence followed the same pattern. The CCD concluded that strikes on data centers can significantly disrupt Russian influence networks, but the effect appears to be short-lived. Mashable was unable to verify the CCD’s findings independently. Before publication, we emailed Osavul to request the underlying dataset, the criteria it uses to flag inauthentic behavior, and any information about where the accounts were hosted. Osavul did not respond by publication time. The report never defines "inauthentic behavior." While the term is quite broad, some general signals that researchers typically attribute to bot accounts include newly created profiles, unusually high posting volume, blank or AI-generated profile photos, and activity across many unrelated political narratives. Without Osavul’s criteria, it’s unclear whether these accounts are automated, run by coordinated humans, or a mix of both. Still, if the numbers hold up, they point to something real. The CCD argues that the drops show strikes on data centers can significantly constrain Russia’s information operations by disrupting the automated networks behind them. However, the agency also acknowledges how quickly the accounts came back, suggesting the disruptions were "substantial but short-lived." Why it matters The findings arrive after a week of overheated claims. Last week, Mashable looked at viral claims that Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers had knocked Russia’s bot army offline. The conclusion we and other outlets reached was that the data behind those claims couldn’t support them. That claim spread like wildfire on social media, amplified by European officials and even backed up by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, President Zelenskyy said "everyone noticed" a drop in Russian bot activity. Social media users echoed similar observations about the seemingly stark decline in pro-GOP and pro-AfD posts after the strikes. It was an easy idea to believe, given how platforms like Facebook and X incentivize and reward polarizing political ragebait, and Russia’s online influence operations are well-documented. The claim also seemed to have supporting data. United24 Media, the Ukrainian government-run outlet whose reporting drove much of the conversation, cited an analysis by The Deep Dive of Cloudflare Radar data. That data showed automated traffic from Yandex’s network had nearly vanished by Oct. 11. As Mashable reported at the time, that data couldn’t support the claim. "Automated traffic" means any request that software, rather than a person, sends to a website, and most of it is mundane. Yandex, often called "Russia's Google," runs the Federation's biggest search engine, so its network constantly sends out crawlers to index the web. Knocking its data centers offline would stop that traffic, whether or not a single troll account went quiet. We found no published evidence tying influence campaigns on social media to Yandex servers, and United24 acknowledged the same limitation. Cloudflare has since published its own analysis. It said its data doesn’t appear to support claims that the strikes crippled social media manipulation, though it couldn’t rule out a connection. Zelenskyy’s office has also narrowed his remarks. According to BBC Verify, his office said the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media" rather than a fall in bot activity.

artigo.texto: Conciliar a produção agrícola com a conservação das florestas, ampliar a restauração de áreas degradadas e transformar a preservação ambiental em oportunidades econômicas estão entre os desafios e as possibilidades para o Pará. Em entrevista ao Grupo Liberal, Leonardo Sobral, diretor de Florestas e Restauração do Imaflora (Instituto de Manejo e Certificação Florestal e Agrícola), destaca o potencial do estado para avançar nessa agenda por meio de incentivos econômicos, do mercado de carbono, da bioeconomia e das concessões florestais para restauração. O especialista também ressalta a importância de valorizar os produtos da floresta em pé e de fortalecer iniciativas que conciliem conservação ambiental, produção sustentável e geração de renda. 1.Quais são hoje os maiores desafios para conciliar a produção agrícola com a conservação das florestas no estado do Pará? A primeira grande notícia é que a conciliação da produção agrícola com a área florestal é totalmente possível. Hoje não só no estado do Pará, mas em toda a Amazônia, existem áreas produtivas, áreas com aptidão de produção agrícola e que elas devem cada vez mais implementar as boas práticas produtivas. Nesse caso, eu me refiro a boas práticas tanto do ponto de vista ambiental como do ponto de vista social. E, ao mesmo tempo, mantendo a sua reserva florestal, mantendo a floresta em pé, sem que haja essa concorrência, vamos dizer, entre as atividades. 2. Como o Imaflora avalia o ritmo atual das iniciativas de reflorestamento e restauração na Amazônia? Estamos avançando no tempo necessário ou ainda não? O tema da restauração florestal no ambiente de pesquisa já é muito consolidado, e nos últimos anos, a gente viu um grande interesse do setor privado, principalmente dada a questão do carbono florestal. A gente tem que entender que a restauração florestal é uma forma de, ao mesmo tempo que você planta as árvores, está restaurando a floresta original, e, ao crescer as árvores, ela faz o sequestro do carbono, a remoção do carbono. Você consegue dessa forma estabelecer um projeto de carbono e ter uma remuneração por esse carbono que está sendo retirado da atmosfera. Nos últimos anos, essa atividade vem crescendo bastante, vem ganhando muita importância no Brasil, no estado do Pará, mas como você pergunta do ritmo, tem muito ainda o que se fazer. O que a gente vem discutindo é que cada vez mais deva ter incentivos econômicos. Além do carbono, outros produtos, seja madeira, seja produtos não madeireiros, possam vir atrelados a essa atividade, para que ela seja viável cada vez mais do ponto de vista econômico mesmo. Ainda tem um longo caminho a ser percorrido, mas o que a gente vem vendo atualmente são muitas ações de fortalecimento desse setor. A gente entende que o estado do Pará tem aptidão para isso. Ele tem muitas áreas degradadas que poderiam estar sendo restauradas e já tem um programa de governo instituído, então digo que hoje temos um ambiente favorável para avançar na agenda de restauração. 3.O Imaflora tem algum projeto que avalia como destaque, com importância nessa questão do carbono no Pará ou na Amazônia? A gente tem uma plataforma de monitoramento chamada “Carbon Track”. Essa plataforma de monitoramento da restauração florestal avalia a qualidade da restauração e ao mesmo tempo faz uma avaliação da quantidade de carbono que está sendo sequestrado. Hoje existem diversas tecnologias nesse mundo de avanço tecnológico. Tem muita informação. Tem muita novidade. Por exemplo, a gente fez o monitoramento de uma área utilizando tecnologia de LiDAR (sigla para Light Detection and Ranging, ou Detecção e Alcance de Luz), que são lasers, embarcados num drone. Isso reduz o tempo de monitoramento em campo, otimizando essa atividade e trazendo maior precisão para a quantificação de carbono. Esse é só um exemplo. Tem outras tecnologias existentes e a gente vem cada vez mais também avançando nessa atividade. 4.Belém e o Pará estão no centro das atenções globais devido à agenda climática, principalmente depois da Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas (COP 30) que ocorreu em novembro de 2025 aqui. Como a população local pode se beneficiar diretamente da chamada bioeconomia? Belém de fato está no centro da atenção climática, depois da COP 30. A cidade conseguiu de fato fazer uma COP muito bem feita, no meu ponto de vista, e eu acho que a partir daí muitos benefícios podem advir disso. A bioeconomia é um exemplo. Quando a gente fala de bioeconomia, a gente está falando de produtos da floresta, produtos da sociobioeconomia, que vão desde frutos, óleos, sementes. É uma gama enorme de produtos. A COP trouxe um legado importante: um olhar também internacional. As pessoas de vários países tiveram em Belém, podendo ver a riqueza e valorizar esses produtos. Nem o próprio Brasil também conhece essa riqueza e valoriza esses produtos. Acho que nessa perspectiva de valorização do produto, que é um produto que vai para a culinária, por exemplo, é super importante que eles sejam valorizados e reconhecidos. Por quê? Porque quanto mais a gente valoriza produtos da floresta, mais incentivo a gente está dando para que a floresta permaneça em pé. Então, conectando um pouco os produtos da sociobioeconomia com a questão climática, a questão de contenção do desmatamento, a premissa é essa - a gente precisa valorizar a floresta em pé através de seus produtos e de seus serviços que são prestados não só localmente, no estado do Pará, em Belém, mas para todo mundo. É a regulação do clima que a gente está falando. 5. Na prática, de que forma a certificação florestal ajuda a combater o desmatamento ilegal na Amazônia? artigo.texto: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has finalized the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Battery Energy Storage System) Regulations, 2026, establishing a regulatory framework for integrating Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) into Gujarat’s electricity grid. The regulations aim to improve grid stability, enhance operational flexibility, and support the growing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly solar and wind power, whose generation depends on weather conditions. The new framework aligns with guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, which recognize energy storage as an important component of electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and ancillary services. Battery energy storage systems can help balance electricity supply and demand by storing surplus power and releasing it when required, thereby supporting reliable grid operations. GERC initiated the regulatory process by publishing the draft regulations on May 12, 2026. The Commission subsequently conducted a public consultation process to gather feedback from stakeholders. Written comments and objections were received from 20 stakeholders, followed by a public hearing on June 15, 2026. The finalized regulations incorporate the Commission’s decisions on key aspects of BESS procurement, project registration, operating models, charging arrangements, and grid control. Under the finalized framework, electricity distribution licensees and other applicable licensees are primarily required to procure BESS capacity through competitive bidding under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003. This approach is intended to promote transparent procurement and cost-effective tariff discovery. Procurement under Section 62 will be permitted only in exceptional circumstances, subject to prior approval from the Commission and the submission of adequate techno-commercial justification. The regulations also establish registration and minimum project-size requirements for grid-connected battery storage installations in Gujarat. All grid-connected BESS projects must register with the Gujarat Energy Development Agency (GEDA). For standalone installations, the minimum individual project size has been specified as above 1 MW in power capacity, with an energy storage duration of at least two hours. Such projects must connect to the electricity network at 11 kV or higher. The framework allows battery storage systems to operate under different business models, including co-located projects alongside renewable energy plants, standalone installations, systems embedded within transmission or distribution networks, and consumer or prosumer arrangements. These provisions are intended to accommodate different applications of energy storage across the power sector. For co-located BESS installations, the Commission has specified that charging must take place exclusively from the associated renewable energy plant. This restriction is designed to avoid complications in energy accounting and Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) compliance. Grid charging without the appropriate contract demand will attract temporary supply tariffs, discouraging unauthorized electricity consumption through the grid. The regulations also clarify the role of the State Load Despatch Centre (SLDC) in maintaining grid security. The SLDC will retain overriding authority to issue dispatch instructions to all grid-connected BESS during grid disturbances, helping safeguard system reliability. With these regulations, Gujarat has established a framework for the controlled deployment and operation of battery energy storage systems. The measures are expected to support renewable energy integration, improve grid flexibility, and strengthen the state’s ability to manage changing electricity demand and generation patterns. artigo.texto: A Pahlavan Ventures One, empresa controlada pela Cloud HQ, pediu à Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) o reconhecimento do direito de contratar mais 11,53 MW de capacidade de transmissão em 2029 sem se submeter às regras do novo processo competitivo de acesso à rede. A empresa busca garantir a contratação da capacidade prevista para seus data centers em São Paulo sem comprometer os resultados da primeira temporada de acesso da Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão (Pnast), na qual foi uma das vencedoras. Caso o prêmio do certame seja pago sobre a totalidade da capacidade conquistada, a companhia também pede a devolução do valor proporcional ao volume adicional. O novo requerimento foi apresentado em 15 de outubro, após uma disputa que chegou à Justiça Federal. Em 6 de outubro, o Tribunal Regional Federal da 1ª Região (TRF1) determinou que a Aneel analisasse, em até 48 horas, um pedido de medida cautelar apresentado pelas empresas do Complexo Pahlavan. A decisão também estabeleceu a adoção de providências para evitar que eventual capacidade remanescente no barramento de 440 kV da subestação Replan, em São Paulo, fosse definitivamente destinada a terceiros antes da análise da agência. A decisão judicial, contudo, não garantiu a contratação da capacidade adicional. O novo documento busca justamente o reconhecimento, pela Aneel, de que parte do aumento de carga previsto para 2029 pode ser atendida pelas regras de transição aprovadas pela agência. Inicialmente, o pedido de enquadramento abrangia as três empresas do grupo, a Pahlavan Ventures One, Two e Three. Após reunião com representantes da Aneel em 14 de outubro, o requerimento foi reformulado para contemplar exclusivamente a Pahlavan One, com um aumento de 11,53 MW no Montante de Uso do Sistema de Transmissão (Must). O Must corresponde à capacidade de uso da rede de transmissão contratada pelo consumidor. Segundo a empresa, o aumento solicitado para 2029 já estava previsto no parecer de acesso original elaborado pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), que considerou a expansão gradual da demanda do empreendimento. A Pahlavan One afirma cumprir os requisitos para receber o tratamento de transição, incluindo a existência de portaria do Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME), contrato de uso do sistema de transmissão e estudos técnicos que contemplavam a implantação escalonada do projeto. A companhia também informa que solicitou o incremento ao ONS em 1º de janeiro de 2026, antes do prazo-limite de 22 de janeiro estabelecido para o enquadramento. Pedido depende da capacidade disponível A empresa apresentou duas alternativas para que o aumento de capacidade seja viabilizado. A primeira é que os 11,53 MW sejam atendidos prioritariamente com eventual capacidade remanescente no barramento de 440 kV da subestação Replan, em São Paulo, desde que esse espaço não tenha sido destinado no processo competitivo nem contratado ou reservado por terceiros. Caso não exista capacidade remanescente, a Pahlavan One solicita que o regime de transição seja aplicado a uma parcela dos aproximadamente 101 MW que conquistou no mesmo ponto de conexão durante a primeira temporada de acesso à rede. Nesse cenário, os 11,53 MW seriam enquadrados no regime anterior, enquanto o restante da capacidade permaneceria submetido às regras da Pnast e às condições do processo competitivo. A companhia argumenta que essa alternativa permitiria conciliar a proteção das situações constituídas sob as regras anteriores com a manutenção dos resultados do certame. De acordo com a manifestação, a medida não alteraria o volume total de capacidade destinado aos vencedores, não modificaria a classificação dos participantes e não afetaria direitos de terceiros. Pahlavan também pede devolução de prêmio A manifestação inclui, ainda, um pedido financeiro condicionado à situação da contratação. Se a Aneel determinar a aplicação do regime de transição aos 11,53 MW, mas a Pahlavan One já tiver pago o prêmio referente à totalidade dos aproximadamente 101 MW obtidos no processo competitivo, a empresa solicita a restituição da parcela correspondente à capacidade que passar a ser atendida pelo regime de transição. Na prática, a companhia quer evitar que os 11,53 MW sejam submetidos às condições do novo modelo de acesso e ao pagamento do prêmio previsto no certame, caso a agência reconheça que esse montante deve receber o tratamento regulatório anterior. A Pahlavan One pediu que a Aneel analise a solicitação com brevidade, considerando os prazos para pagamento do prêmio e para as etapas seguintes da contratação.

artigo.texto: As Diwali approaches and Delhi braces for its annual smog season, conversations about air quality usually turn to firecrackers and stubble burning. These conversations seem to miss out on pollution caused by factories, power plants and furnaces that run all year and are a steadier source of pollution. This is a fitting moment to ask what India’s biggest industrial emitters have been doing, and how the 2026 UN Climate Change COP31 will bring about an environmental change for the better. Starting November, for the first time, Indian factories will be able to buy and sell carbon credit certificates on power exchanges, finally turning a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified by the government in 2023, into a working market reality. The legal foundation for the concept is the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022, which empowered the government to create an Indian carbon market and a carbon credit trading scheme which was notified in 2023. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency has issued emission targets to around 490 industrial units across seven sectors and credits are expected to be issued this month, with trading between November and January. To understand this better how the carbon credit market works, think back to school. Imagine a school where every student gets a fixed number of late passes each term. The punctual kids end up with spares and the chronic latecomers run short. Now let them trade. The early birds sell their extras, the sleepyheads buy them, and the school still meets its overall punctuality target. Replace late passes with tonnes of carbon dioxide and students with factories, and what you have is carbon credit trading. The idea is simple. A government sets emission targets for polluting industries. A company that beats its target earns certain credits, one for every tonne of carbon dioxide it avoided. A company that misses must buy credits from the one who met its targets. Therefore, pollution gets a price tag, and environment friendly industry practices becomes a way of earning money instead of a cost. While the efficacy of the scheme, and the volume of trade it inspires, remains to be seen, there are interesting aspects of the scheme which deserve to be highlighted. Firstly, the credit trading scheme operates differently from other types of environment policies. For instance a green tax, such as a carbon tax or India’s former coal cess, puts a fixed price on pollution. Every company pays for every tonne it emits, and the money goes to the government. As opposed to this, the carbon credit trading scheme would target the emissions more directly leading to actual reduction while letting the market set the price for per unit emission. Secondly, the scheme has a dual benefit: it cuts pollution while putting money in motion, since companies that clean up earn credits to sell their certificates. One market research firm valued India’s carbon credit market at about 34 billion dollars in 2025 and expects it to grow more than tenfold by 2034. The scheme also helps India keep its promises under the Paris Agreement, where it has pledged to cut the emissions intensity of its economy by 47 percent by 2035. Lastly, the scheme sets targets as emissions per unit of output rather than as a cap on total emissions per industry. That choice matters for a developing country like India, where industry must keep expanding to support growth and jobs. An intensity-based approach lets factories grow while still rewarding them for producing more cleanly. It does, however, raise two concerns. The first is a practical one: since industries would expand and output would rise even if per unit emissions becomes cleaner, India’s total emissions may still continue to climb in the long run. The second concern is more fundamental: the scheme risks becoming a permission slip to pollute, letting heavy emitters buy their way out of their obligations instead of changing how they operate. So is this a climate tool or an accounting trick? The answer would depend upon its enforcement. A carbon market with tough targets, honest verification and real penalties would ultimately make clean factories richer. While lasting positive impact on climate would require cleaner technology, stronger enforcement and steady shifts in how industry operates, the carbon credit scheme is a meaningful first step in that direction because it would incentivise industries to invest in developing cleaner technologies with the aim of long term monetary gains. Nakul Dewan is a Senior Advocate and King’s Counsel.

artigo.texto: A preservação de florestas e a recuperação de áreas degradadas podem gerar créditos de carbono e abrir oportunidades econômicas na Amazônia. Em entrevista ao Grupo Liberal, Leonardo Sobral, diretor de Florestas e Restauração do Imaflora (Instituto de Manejo e Certificação Florestal e Agrícola), explica como funciona esse mecanismo, que busca valorizar a manutenção da floresta em pé e incentivar a restauração florestal. Segundo o especialista, as árvores armazenam carbono em sua estrutura, e a quantidade presente em uma área pode ser calculada a partir da medição da vegetação. Como exemplo, ele cita que um hectare de floresta pode armazenar cerca de 300 toneladas de carbono. “À medida que você evita que essa floresta seja derrubada, seja desmatada, eu posso, através de um projeto, vender esse carbono”, explica Sobral. VEJA MAIS Nesse caso, a quantidade de carbono cuja emissão foi evitada pode gerar créditos comercializados no mercado. O mecanismo também pode ser aplicado à recuperação de áreas degradadas. Quando árvores são plantadas durante um projeto de restauração florestal, elas absorvem carbono da atmosfera, permitindo calcular a quantidade de créditos gerados. “Essa restauração, quando planta as árvores, sequestra carbono. Com essa quantidade de carbono que é sequestrado é feito todo esse cálculo para ver quantos créditos de carbono estão sendo gerados”, afirma o diretor do Imaflora.

artigo.texto: Trontek Electronics will unveil its 5 MWh EKOM containerised Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at The Battery Show India 2026, marking the company’s entry into large-scale energy storage for industrial and utility applications. The company will showcase the system at Stall C16, Hall 18, at India Expo Mart & Centre in Greater Noida from October 22 to 24, 2026. The launch extends Trontek’s battery technology and manufacturing experience into applications beyond electric mobility. The EKOM platform is designed to address larger energy storage requirements as India expands its renewable energy capacity and seeks greater flexibility in power management. Battery energy storage systems can help manage variations in electricity supply and demand, support renewable energy integration and improve the use of stored power across industrial and utility operations. Trontek has more than two decades of experience in battery technology and manufacturing. The company currently has an active manufacturing capacity of 3 GWh and plans to increase this to 12 GWh by 2028. The proposed expansion is intended to support its growing presence across mobility, distributed energy and large-scale storage markets. Samrath S Kochar, Founder and CEO of Trontek, said energy storage would play an important role in meeting India’s future power requirements. He said the EKOM launch would extend the company’s battery expertise into large-scale applications while supporting the development of domestic energy storage capabilities. At the exhibition, Trontek will present its products across three business areas: electric mobility, energy storage, and power and critical infrastructure solutions. Its electric mobility portfolio includes battery solutions for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and other mobility applications. Under energy storage, the company offers POWERCUBE for residential applications, NOVARA for commercial facilities and EKOM for industrial and utility-scale requirements. The newly unveiled 5 MWh system will form part of the EKOM range. The company will also display inverter and solar solutions for distributed energy applications, along with battery systems for telecom infrastructure and backup power requirements. Trontek’s expanded portfolio reflects its move towards a broader energy technology business, supported by Indian engineering and manufacturing capabilities. The company aims to develop products for residential, commercial, industrial and utility customers as demand for energy storage increases. The EKOM unveiling marks a new phase in Trontek’s business development as it seeks to build manufacturing scale and expand its participation in India’s changing energy landscape. Its planned capacity increase to 12 GWh by 2028 forms a key part of this strategy.

artigo.texto: Rússia e EUA debatem parcerias, incluindo data centres, diz enviado Kirill Dmitriev afirmou que as sanções dos EUA representam sérios obstáculos e criticou como “equivocada” a Lei Graham Rússia e EUA estão discutindo uma série de novos projetos conjuntos, incluindo data centres movidos a energia nuclear, na esteira do acordo sobre diesel firmado na semana passada, disse nesta sexta-feira (16) o enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin. Kirill Dmitriev afirmou que as sanções dos EUA representam sérios obstáculos e criticou como “equivocada” a Lei Graham, assinada pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, no mês passado, que visa reduzir as receitas energéticas da Rússia por meio de sanções e tarifas. No entanto, ele disse que os dois países estão considerando outras formas de cooperação econômica na esteira do acordo sobre o diesel. “Também estamos discutindo projetos conjuntos na área de data centres russos e norte-americanos, inclusive com o uso de usinas nucleares de pequena escala”, acrescentou ele, sem dar detalhes. Neste mês, a Ucrânia atacou centros de dados do grupo de tecnologia russo Yandex e do grupo bancário e tecnológico Sberbank, no que classificou como uma resposta a ataques russos contra instalações ucranianas. Dmitriev, figura-chave nas negociações entre a Rússia e os EUA para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia, vem há muito tempo pressionando por uma série de acordos potenciais ambiciosos, inclusive sobre minerais e energia. O Kremlin tem manifestado frustração pelo fato de os EUA, até agora, terem vinculado tais acordos a um acordo de paz, que continua indefinido. Mas Dmitriev demonstrou otimismo de que isso está mudando. “Naturalmente, o progresso é bastante difícil; há resistência – resistência generalizada, na verdade – de vários setores. No entanto, como demonstra o exemplo do diesel, acredito que em breve anunciaremos várias outras iniciativas significativas. O gelo, de fato, começou a se quebrar”, disse ele na conferência Russian Energy Week, em Moscou. “Estamos efetivamente implementando projetos com os Estados Unidos da América neste exato momento e continuaremos a fazê-lo até que a operação militar especial chegue ao fim”, acrescentou ele, usando o termo do Kremlin para se referir à guerra. Dmitriev disse que o Tesouro dos EUA havia solicitado ao fundo soberano da Rússia, que ele dirige, que ajudasse a resolver questões complexas de pagamento relacionadas ao acordo sobre o diesel. O acordo anunciado por Trump há uma semana envolve o fornecimento de diesel russo aos mercados dos EUA e globais, a fim de reduzir o preço do combustível – uma prioridade para o presidente dos EUA antes das eleições de meio de mandato do próximo mês.

artigo.texto: Advait Energy unit signs 1 GWh LFP cell supply deal with Hithium - ABEPL, a subsidiary of Advait Energy Transitions, signed a Master Supply Agreement with Hithium. - The deal covers the purchase of up to 1 GWh of 314 Ah LFP prismatic battery cells over one year. - Initial pricing is fixed at $49.5/kWh for the first 350 MWh tranche. - The agreement supports Advait's 2.5 GWh BESS assembly facility in Gangad, Gujarat. *this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only. Advait Battery Ecosystem Private Limited (ABEPL), a step-down subsidiary of Advait Energy Transitions Limited , has entered into a Master Supply Agreement with Hithium for the purchase of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) prismatic battery cells. The agreement, executed on September 18, 2026, structures cell offtake of up to 1 GWh over the next year. This partnership anchors the supply chain for Advait’s upcoming 2.5 GWh annual capacity cell-to-container Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) assembly facility in Gangad, Gujarat. Deal Structure and Pricing Under the terms disclosed in the exchange filing under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Hithium will supply 314 Ah LFP prismatic cells. The contractual value is set at $49.5/kWh for the initial tranche of up to 350 MWh. Pricing for volumes beyond this threshold will be determined based on future project receipts. Strategic Context Hithium is recognized as a BloombergNEF Tier 1 global energy storage manufacturer. For the first half of 2025 (H1 2025), Hithium reported net profit exceeding RMB 100 million ($14 million USD) and operating cash flow surpassing RMB 1 billion ($140 million USD). ABEPL, incorporated on April 27, 2026, is building an integrated BESS supply chain. The company has previously collaborated with Adaptive Engineering for engineering design and Energy Management System (EMS) architecture. The Hithium agreement addresses the critical cell sourcing component of this ecosystem. What the Numbers Show The pricing structure reveals a tiered approach to volume scaling. With a fixed rate of $49.5/kWh applied only to the first 350 MWh, approximately 65% of the potential 1 GWh annual offtake remains subject to future price negotiations. This suggests that while the initial supply chain risk is mitigated for the first third of the year's capacity, long-term cost certainty depends on subsequent project wins and market conditions for LFP cells. Historical Stock Returns for Advait Energy Transitions How might the floating pricing mechanism for the remaining 650 MWh of the annual offtake impact Advait's gross margins if global LFP cell prices decline? What is the timeline for Advait's 2.5 GWh BESS assembly facility in Gujarat to reach full operational capacity, and how does this align with the 1-year supply agreement? Given Hithium's strong H1 2025 financials, how does their current production capacity compare to Advait's potential future scaling beyond the initial 1 GWh commitment?

artigo.texto: Premier Energies and Germany's RCT Nexor Formalise 12 GWh Battery Storage Manufacturing Joint Venture Premier Energies has signed the shareholders agreement for its joint venture with RCT Nexor. The project plans a 12 GWh plant at Seetharampur, Telangana, with a 6 GWh first phase in FY2027-28. Premier Energies Ltd has formalised its battery energy storage system (BESS) manufacturing joint venture with Germany's RCT Group. Its wholly owned subsidiary, Premier Battery Technologies Pvt Ltd (PBTPL), signed a share allotment-cum-shareholders agreement on October 15, 2026. The other signatories are RCT Nexor Energy Pvt Ltd, formerly RCT Energy India Pvt Ltd, and Premier Energies Storage Solutions Pvt Ltd (PESSPL), the joint venture company. The storage market already counts large players: HiTHIUM has surpassed 200 GWh of cumulative deliveries from Chongqing, while GIGA Storage has declared its Albatross project ready to build, with 350 MW of storage in Lower Saxony. A 12 GWh plant planned in Telangana The joint venture plans to establish a 12 GWh BESS manufacturing facility at Seetharampur, in the Indian state of Telangana. According to Premier Energies, a first phase of 6 GWh is expected to be set up in FY2027-28. The site is intended to manufacture and assemble products for residential, small-business, commercial, industrial and utility-scale applications. The agreement follows a binding term sheet signed on September 10, 2026 by PBTPL and RCT India. Premier Energies says the joint venture would address demand for energy storage solutions across multiple market segments. The group, already active in solar cells and modules, also identifies BESS, inverters and transformers as areas for expanding its portfolio. Ownership and governance structure PESSPL is currently a wholly owned subsidiary of PBTPL. The agreement gives RCT Nexor Energy the right to subscribe to equity representing 15% of the joint venture's issued and paid-up capital, in four tranches linked to project milestones. It also grants the option, but not the obligation, to acquire an additional 5% for cash at the end of Phase I, subject to the agreement's terms. The board will comprise two nominees of PBTPL and one nominee of RCT Nexor Energy. Premier Energies states that no immediate share issuance is proposed under the agreement. RCT's technology contribution Germany-based RCT Group operates across several renewable technologies, including photovoltaic manufacturing engineering and energy storage. Its RCT Power arm has developed residential, commercial and grid-scale solutions, including systems designed for applications of up to 5 MWh per unit. It has also reported a 2.1 GWh order for grid-connected battery storage projects in Australia. These capabilities could help support the Indian joint venture's technology development and market reach. The Premier Energies stock-exchange filing does not, however, detail the specific technology-transfer and manufacturing responsibilities under the agreement with RCT Nexor. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: O Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) anunciou uma nova parceria para ampliar os investimentos em restauração florestal no Brasil. A iniciativa, batizada de ProFloresta+ 2, pretende mobilizar até R$ 6 bilhões para a compra de créditos de carbono. O objetivo é levar esse modelo de financiamento para todos os biomas do país, incentivando a recomposição da vegetação nativa como uma atividade econômica sustentável. O BNDES anunciou uma parceria com o Instituto Clima e Sociedade para ampliar os projetos de restauração florestal no Brasil. A iniciativa faz parte do ProFloresta+ 2, que poderá mobilizar até R$ 6 bilhões em compras de créditos de carbono e levar o modelo de financiamento a todos os biomas brasileiros. Leonardo Alves Corrêa, sócio-executivo da área de Direito Ambiental e Negócios Sustentáveis do VLF Advogados e professor da UFMG, está disponível para comentar como a restauração florestal vem se consolidando como atividade econômica, os desafios jurídicos para atrair investimentos privados e a importância dos contratos de longo prazo para viabilizar esses projetos. - O BNDES vai investir até R$ 6 bilhões em créditos de carbono. - A nova fase do programa, ProFloresta+ 2, abrange todos os biomas brasileiros. - Especialistas destacam a segurança jurídica como chave para atrair investidores privados. - A restauração florestal está se tornando uma fonte de renda e atividade econômica formal. - Contratos de longo prazo são necessários para garantir o sucesso dos projetos de décadas. Segurança jurídica atrai investidores para projetos ambientais A expansão desse mercado traz questões sobre segurança jurídica, responsabilidades ambientais e comercialização de créditos de carbono, especialmente em iniciativas que dependem de resultados ao longo de décadas.
