artigo.texto: MOUNT PLEASANT, Wis. — Mount Pleasant’s proposed Microsoft data center is reducing the number of buildings while increasing the project’s overall square footage. According to Village of Mount Pleasant Planning Commission documents, the number of buildings has been reduced from nine to seven. The project originally encompassed 5.2 million square feet at 12023 Durand Ave. Under the revised design, the total square footage will increase to 5,878,080 square feet, Village of Mount Pleasant Communications Director Sean Ryan said. Samuel Schultz, Mount Pleasant’s community development director, said the square footage will “likely fluctuate” as Microsoft continues refining its site plans. The documents also show plans for 10 parking lots, internal roads, stormwater ponds, sound walls and perimeter security fencing. “We continue to refine the design and layout of our expansion parcels in the Village of Mount Pleasant. The changes in no way reflect a reduction in our ambition, they have been made to ensure faster development, allowing us to access this increased capacity quicker. We will continue to evolve our design and keep the community updated prior to beginning any vertical construction,” a Microsoft spokesperson said in an email. The development’s total taxable value is projected at $6,095,690,000, which would generate $103,148,899 in incremental tax revenue, according to the documents. Schultz said the preliminary projections are based on a 40-year period. The documents also estimate the data center project would generate $7,694,420 per acre. The Village of Mount Pleasant Planning Commission met Thursday at 1 p.m. and unanimously approved the site plan modifications. The changes will now go to the Mount Pleasant Village Council for approval. The council’s next meeting is scheduled for Oct. 19 at 6 p.m. “These (plans) will continue to be refined over time as they both go to pull building permits, but also look at site plans, so this is just kind of the next step in their refinement of the site plan approval process,” Schultz said during the Planning Commission meeting. The traffic impact analysis for the data center project indicated it could take up to 10 years for the site to be fully completed, Schultz said. In July, Microsoft was sued by Sturtevant residents over noise complaints related to the data center. The Planning Commission requested that Microsoft add sound mitigation measures along the west side of the project.

artigo.texto: O mercado nacional de comércio de direitos de emissão de carbono da China acumulou mais de 930 milhões de toneladas em transações até o final de julho de 2026, segundo dados apresentados nesta quinta-feira, 13 de agosto, pelo ministro da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente, Huang Runqiu. O sistema chinês de comércio de emissões iniciou suas operações em 2021 e passou a desempenhar um papel importante na estratégia ambiental do país. Segundo Huang, o mecanismo tem ajudado setores industriais a reduzir suas emissões de carbono com custos menores e contribuído para a transição para uma economia de baixo carbono. A expansão do mercado está entre as medidas previstas no 15º Plano Quinquenal para a Construção de uma China Bonita, divulgado recentemente pelo país. O plano estabelece a ampliação gradual da cobertura do mercado nacional de emissões, além do aumento do número de empresas participantes. A meta também inclui reduzir em aproximadamente 3% as emissões de carbono por unidade de produto dos setores abrangidos pelo sistema. A China pretende ampliar o alcance do mercado de carbono para incluir outras atividades industriais de elevada emissão. Segundo Li Gao, vice-ministro de Ecologia e Meio Ambiente, a expansão deverá incluir setores como petroquímica e indústria química, que se somarão às áreas atualmente abrangidas, como geração de energia, siderurgia, produção de cimento e fundição de alumínio. Com a ampliação, aproximadamente 80% das emissões de dióxido de carbono da China deverão ficar sob controle efetivo do sistema nacional de comércio de direitos de emissão, de acordo com o vice-ministro. A estratégia busca utilizar mecanismos de mercado para estimular empresas a reduzir a intensidade das emissões e investir em tecnologias mais eficientes e menos poluentes. As autoridades chinesas também destacaram os avanços realizados nos últimos anos no enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas. Segundo o Ministério da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente, as estruturas energética, industrial e de transporte do país vêm passando por transformações voltadas à melhoria da eficiência e à redução das emissões. Além da expansão do mercado de carbono, o governo pretende continuar promovendo a transição verde em áreas consideradas estratégicas, incluindo energia, indústria, transporte e desenvolvimento urbano e rural. Outra frente será o controle de gases de efeito estufa diferentes do dióxido de carbono. Entre eles está o metano, que também deverá receber maior atenção nas políticas ambientais chinesas. A ampliação do mercado nacional de carbono representa, assim, uma das principais ferramentas econômicas utilizadas pela China para estimular a redução das emissões e apoiar suas metas de desenvolvimento de baixo carbono. artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 16 de outubro de 2026, às 10:20 Frankfurt, 16/10/2026 – A Schneider Electric elevou suas metas anuais pela segunda vez em 2026, após a continuidade do forte fluxo de pedidos ligados a data centers impulsionar as vendas do terceiro trimestre. O grupo francês de engenharia informou hoje que agora mira crescimento orgânico do Ebita ajustado (lucro antes de juros, impostos e amortização) entre 18% e 21% no ano, acima da meta anterior – já revisada para cima em julho – de 14% a 19%. A companhia também aumentou suas expectativas para o ano cheio tanto para crescimento orgânico de receita, agora estimado em 12% a 14%, quanto para rentabilidade. A Schneider passou a projetar expansão de sua margem de Ebita ajustado entre 1 ponto porcentual e 1,2 ponto porcentual, em base orgânica. Para o quarto trimestre, a empresa afirmou esperar que a demanda por data centers permaneça forte. Segundo a Schneider, o impulso de preços deve ajudar a compensar o impacto da inflação de matérias-primas e das tarifas no consolidado do ano. Assim como outros fornecedores de equipamentos elétricos, a Schneider vem surfando a onda de demanda por produtos usados em data centers, puxada pela expansão da inteligência artificial (IA), e tem direcionado parte desse ganho para aquisições. A empresa citou uma série recente de movimentos: um acordo de US$ 22,6 bilhões para comprar a desenvolvedora americana de software industrial PTC no começo do mês, uma oferta de aquisição de US$ 1,35 bilhão pela fabricante de dispositivos inteligentes Shelly Group no mês anterior e o acordo para adquirir a fornecedora de software para IA Cognite Holding por US$ 3,1 bilhões em junho. No terceiro trimestre, a demanda ligada a data centers mais do que dobrou e contribuiu para levar a receita da Schneider ao que a empresa descreveu como um recorde histórico para qualquer trimestre. A receita do terceiro trimestre foi de 11,46 bilhões de euros, alta de 18% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. Em termos orgânicos, a receita cresceu 17%, segundo a companhia. Os números superaram as expectativas do mercado, que apontavam receita de 11,13 bilhões de euros e crescimento orgânico de 14%, de acordo com estimativas de consenso fornecidas pela própria Schneider. O CEO Olivier Blum disse que, como esperado, data centers seguiram como principal motor de crescimento, com execução do backlog (carteira de pedidos) e crescimento de demanda em “três dígitos” no trimestre, aumentando a visibilidade de demanda para 2027 e 2028. artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia Leilão de armazenamento de energia elétrica será realizado em dezembro 16 de outubro de 2026, às 19:41 Há cerca de 11 dias da publicação do edital do Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na Forma de Potência (LRCAP) de 2026, na modalidade Armazenamento, a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) publicou uma resolução da Comissão Interministerial de Inovações e Aquisições do Programa de Aceleração do Crescimento (Novo PAC) que torna obrigatória a compra de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS, na sigla em inglês) de origem nacional em ações vinculadas ao programa. Pelo texto, o BESS passa a estar sujeito à exigência de aquisição exclusiva de produto manufaturado nacional. Na prática, empreendimentos que pretendam contratar potência no leilão com armazenamento deverão utilizar sistemas que atendam aos requisitos mínimos de nacionalização definidos no Regulamento de Credenciamento de Sistemas Estacionários de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), no âmbito do sistema de credenciamento de fornecedores da instituição (CFI). A regra se aplica à chamada Etapa 1 do regulamento, com possibilidade de enquadramento por uma entre quatro rotas de credenciamento previstas nessa fase, o que mantém o porcentual de 15% de conteúdo nacional. Segundo o diretor executivo da Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), Fabio Lima, essa resolução ocorre para enquadrar os BESS como obra do PAC. No leilão, há exigência de conteúdo local porque a legislação do PAC cria a prerrogativa de que essa comissão interministerial possa definir hipóteses em que o certame tenha algum nível de conteúdo local. “E o que definiram nessa resolução foi repetir de forma idêntica a exigência que já estava prevista para o leilão de armazenamento nacional”, disse Lima. Pela resolução, a comprovação do atendimento aos critérios de conteúdo nacional deverá ser apresentada à Aneel por meio de certificados emitidos pelo BNDES. O texto prevê duas etapas de validação: uma na fase pré-contratual, como requisito para a assinatura do Contrato de Potência de Reserva de Capacidade (CRCAP), e outra durante a implantação do projeto, como condição para o início da operação comercial do empreendimento. “Com a decisão, o governo reforça a estratégia de atrelar o avanço do armazenamento no setor elétrico a metas de industrialização e adensamento produtivo local, usando a contratação pública e os mecanismos de financiamento e credenciamento do BNDES como instrumentos para induzir a cadeia nacional”, diz o texto. Para Lima, o fato é que essa política de ter a exigência de índice de nacionalização gerou interesse das empresas. Hoje, oito companhias já se habilitaram como fornecedoras de BESS no Brasil. Antes havia apenas a Weg e a Moura como fabricantes inscritas no BNDES. “O governo tem que dosar a velocidade da exigência de conteúdo local com a velocidade com que o mercado ocorre. A consolidação da cadeia de fornecedores das partes e equipamentos, vai ocorrer de forma paulatina”, ressaltou o dirigente. Ele lembrou que o Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia (PDE 2036) prevê 7,2 gigawatts (GW) de armazenamento de grande porte, além das aplicações em geração distribuída (GD) e em clientes comerciais e industriais. “Os 7,2 GW são da ordem de 28 GWh. É um investimento bastante relevante”, disse Lima. Segundo ele, a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) está concluindo as primeiras levas de análise dos projetos que se credenciaram para o leilão. O Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) informou que quase 300 GW em projetos foram cadastrados para o certame. “Ao longo do mês de novembro, se consolida os resultados dos projetos. E aí se tem a fase de inscrição, em que se aporta as garantias de participação no leilão. E em dezembro você tem a sessão pública propriamente dita.” Veja também

artigo.texto: From robotic gloves to safer batteries, CUHK puts research to work Wearable device helps patients regain hand movement as university-developed battery technology targets energy storage HONG KONG — From helping stroke patients perform everyday tasks to developing safer ways to store electricity, researchers at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) are developing technologies for use beyond the laboratory. During a visit to the university on Sept. 1, a reporter tried on a robotic glove that moved the fingers with noticeable force, but without jerking them. For stroke survivors who cannot move their hands, that movement could help them do something as ordinary as holding a spoon or picking up a phone. The device uses air-powered artificial muscles developed by a team led by Raymond Tong, a professor of biomedical engineering at CUHK. Unlike conventional motor-driven rehabilitation equipment, the lightweight system uses a small pump to help patients open and close their hands. “Nowadays, you can see those exoskeletons are very rigid. They are very heavy,” Tong said, inviting the reporter to try the device. Patients can use it both for rehabilitation exercises and everyday tasks, including gripping objects, writing and eating. Tong said the system can also respond to signals associated with a patient’s intention to move. “They can use the brain to control it,” he said. “I just imagine moving the hand and the hand moves.” Tong said the team was conducting clinical trials involving people with strokes and spinal injuries, with plans to expand use in hospitals. He also described work with children who have difficulty standing or walking. Elsewhere on campus, researchers showed a battery designed to reduce the fire risks associated with conventional lithium-ion batteries. Developed by a team led by CUHK professor Yi-Chun Lu, the sulfur-based flow battery uses water-based electrolytes. Luquos Energy, a startup founded to commercialize the research, has installed a demonstration system on campus. “This is a completely different technology compared to lithium,” said Luquos Energy CEO Simon Zengyue Wang. “We do not use lithium. We use sulfur.” “The battery electrolyte is water, so it never catches fire,” Wang said. The company estimates its electrolyte could remain usable for more than 15 years, although that is not a verified real-world service life. Wang said the technology could serve solar installations and power-hungry artificial intelligence data centers because it can discharge electricity for “over eight hours, even 12 hours, even longer.” He said Luquos Energy was building a production line in Shenzhen and had already developed battery systems for projects including electric vehicle charging.

artigo.texto: European independent power producer (IPP), R.Power, has energised its first standalone energy storage project in Poland and is now supporting grid stability. The 5 MW/10 MWh Herby battery energy storage system (BESS) is the IPP’s first standalone energy storage project to be energised and serves as a precursor to an extensive rollout of operations across the company’s European BESS pipeline. Herby BESS has secured an optimisation agreement with Entrix, a European leading energy trader. Entrix is now managing the trading and optimisation across all relevant electricity markets, while the qualification process for balancing services provision is ongoing. The partnership provides a blueprint for integrating innovative optimisation approaches across R.Power’s wider European BESS operations. Herby began construction in 4Q25, having secured its long-term contract in Poland’s capacity market auction in December 2024 and also a supplementary capacity market contract organised in September 2026. The project paves the way for R.Power’s advanced utility scale BESS projects – Jedwabno, Dziegielewo, Gdansk, Scornicesti, and Studina – to follow in suit as R.Power scales up its battery energy storage capacity across Europe. Rafał Hajduk, Chief Commercial Officer at R.Power, commented: “Herby is the first standalone BESS in R.Power’s portfolio to reach the market. We look forward to working together with Entrix on this interesting asset with capacity market contracts and asymmetrical battery design. With a combined capacity of 1.6 GW/5.8 GWh across several large BESS assets in the pipeline today – including Jedwabno, Dzięgielewo, Gdańsk, Scornicesti, and Studina – we’re taking the next step on the journey to deliver the storage capacity Poland and Europe needs.”

artigo.texto: A dura busca pelo Retorno do Investimento nos data centers de Inteligência Artificial Donos de Data Centers de IA precisariam gerar uma receita acumulada de US$ 8,5 trilhões para cobrir os investimentos de capital anunciados para os próximos quatro anos, afirma o Gartner. Mais de US$ 3,5 trilhões em investimentos em infraestrutura de Inteligência Artificial (IA) podem estar sujeitos a perdas de valor até o final de 2030, caso os fornecedores de IA mantenham o ritmo atual de investimentos de capital, alerta o Gartner. “Em 2026, espera-se que os fornecedores de Inteligência Artificial gastem quase US$ 1 trilhão em infraestrutura de IA, e a previsão é de que invistam mais US$ 6 trilhões entre 2027 e 2030”, diz Will Sommer, Diretor Analista Sênior do Gartner. “No entanto, nossa pesquisa indica que as receitas de Inteligência Artificial nos segmentos corporativo e de consumo serão insuficientes para sustentar retornos lucrativos sobre todos os investimentos de capital em IA planejados para esse período.” De acordo com a consultoria, até 2030, os proprietários de Data Centers de IA precisariam gerar uma receita acumulada de US$ 8,5 trilhões para cobrir os investimentos de capital anunciados, os custos de financiamento e um retorno sobre o capital investido (ROIC) de 12%, considerada a taxa mínima de rentabilidade exigida para o capital de investimento. “No entanto, a previsão é de que a receita total de IA nos segmentos corporativo e de consumo atribuível aos Data Centers de IA nesse período não ultrapasse US$ 3,6 trilhões. Como a maioria dos fornecedores nativos de Inteligência Artificial opera com modelos de negócios que exigem poucos ativos, prevemos que menos da metade da receita de IA será obtida por fornecedores que possuem infraestrutura significativa de Inteligência Artificial”, afirma Sommer. A incapacidade de alcançar um ROIC sustentável em ativos que se depreciam rapidamente quase certamente exigiria baixas contábeis. Com base nas projeções do Gartner, uma trajetória contínua de investimento em infraestrutura de IA poderia deixar mais de US$ 4 trilhões em valor de ativos expostos ao risco de baixa contábil até 2032. Nesse cenário, a Gartner não espera que o ROIC de 12% seja alcançado antes do final de 2032, no mínimo.

artigo.texto: A landmark permitting reform bill has united U.S. senators from both parties, but it is dividing the artificial intelligence data center sector. Some industry leaders say it would make data centers easier to build, while others worry it would make them substantially more expensive. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is being called “the most significant permitting reform bill in years” — intended to accelerate the build-out of major infrastructure and other large-scale projects across the U.S. The bill enjoys support on both sides of the aisle and is expected to clear the Senate during the lame-duck session following November's midterm elections. If it is signed into law, BAAJA would likely have significant implications for the data center industry, potentially rewriting the federal rulebook on how data centers purchase electricity and connect to regional grids. But industry insiders are split on whether the legislation would ultimately be a net positive for the sector or usher in disaster for at least some firms pursuing large-scale digital infrastructure projects. Some within the industry — and some critics of the sector — say BAAJA is poised to fuel further acceleration of the AI data center boom by flattening permitting hurdles and codifying a clear pathway to acquiring power. But others say consumer protection provisions in the bill will make acquiring power much more expensive, adding significant development costs early in projects that could push smaller operators to the sidelines. “Upfront capex, especially speculative, is a death knell,” said Harmol Samra, CEO of AI data center provider Host Digital. “This is just going to slow everyone down.” BAAJA is centered on measures intended to speed up the construction of energy assets, power transmission and other infrastructure, plus other major industrial projects for industries like manufacturing and mining. To do so, the bill would impose firm deadlines for permit approvals, exempt more projects from lengthy reviews, limit how long approvals can be challenged and give previously approved projects greater legal protection. Controversially, it would also make significant changes to the National Environmental Policy Act, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act. Those provisions have drawn vocal opposition from some environmental groups, with the Center for Biological Diversity calling it a “back-door deal” meant specifically to accelerate data center development. “This would be a golden ticket for huge AI data centers and tech billionaires. Gutting environmental safeguards means opening the floodgates for more gas-powered data centers fouling the air and draining communities’ water supplies,” said Camden Weber, senior climate and energy policy specialist at the Center for Biological Diversity. While other environmental groups have been more receptive — particularly to provisions aimed at accelerating transmission infrastructure that could bring more renewable generation onto the grid — there is truth in the notion that data centers will benefit from faster permitting. Large campuses can face federal delays when projects affect wetlands or trigger environmental or historic preservation reviews. More consequentially, faster approvals for new transmission and generation could shorten the wait for electricity in markets where developers can wait years for grid connections. Yet beyond its permitting reforms, BAAJA also contains a separate set of provisions aimed squarely at data centers, specifically at one of the sector’s most contentious issues: who ends up paying for the billions of dollars of new power infrastructure needed to provide them with electricity. The measures, which apply to data centers larger than 20 megawatts, are intended to ensure that regular electricity customers don’t get stuck with the bill for new power plants and infrastructure for electric transmission built specifically for data centers. Concerns that homeowners, businesses and other existing customers are effectively subsidizing grid improvements driven mainly by data center demand have become a central talking point in a rising wave of opposition to data center development. And lawmakers from both parties have been eager to show they are taking these concerns seriously. The Trump administration’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, announced in March, aimed to address the same concern, with major tech firms committing to cover the full cost of power delivery and grid updates needed to serve them. But what constitutes “full cost” has remained a matter of interpretation. A report released this month by four Democratic senators found that tech giants generally accept responsibility for the cost of infrastructure built exclusively for them, such as a substation serving a single data center campus. But the answer is murkier when the new infrastructure also benefits other customers, such as a transmission line built primarily to deliver power to a new campus that also improves reliability elsewhere on the grid. Consumer advocates have argued that in such a case, the data center should bear all costs that would not have existed “but for” its arrival. Tech giants and other developers, according to the report, have generally only been willing to cover, at most, a portion of such shared costs and have fought with state regulators to shoulder as few of such shared grid costs as possible. “There is a significant gap between data center developers and the public regarding how much data centers should pay for shared infrastructure, and particularly for infrastructure built primarily, but not exclusively, for their benefit,” the report’s authors wrote. The standards for what constitutes a data center’s fair share of grid costs vary significantly across the balkanized U.S. grid system. artigo.texto: Pasadena Water and Power and elected officials held a kickoff event Oct. 7 for the upcoming construction of the Glenarm Battery Energy Storage System, a 25-megawatt, four-hour lithium iron phosphate battery at the city’s Glenarm Power Plant, 72 East Glenarm Street, that the City of Pasadena says will be completed by mid-2027. The battery will store carbon-free energy and discharge it during evening peak hours to support grid reliability, according to the city. The project is backed by up to $9.66 million from the California Energy Commission’s Distributed Electricity Backup Assets Program, created under Assembly Bill 205 to support the state’s grid during extreme events; the commission approved the grant May 8, 2025, and it requires the project to be finished before June 30, 2027. The city describes the battery as Pasadena’s first utility-scale system and a step toward its goal, set by a 2023 council resolution, of drawing 100% of its electricity from carbon-free sources by the end of 2030. Speakers included State Senator Sasha Renée Pérez, Assemblymember John Harabedian, Mayor Victor Gordo and Councilmember Jason Lyon, according to the city. Pasadena Water and Power General Manager David Reyes called the project “a significant step forward in our commitment to delivering clean, reliable energy.” The City Council approved the collaboration with Glenarm BESS, LLC, a special purpose entity created by San Jose-based EPC Energy Inc., in June 2024 for the battery’s design and future purchase, according to the city. The company is to design, own and operate the battery and charge the city $12.18 per kilowatt-month over 15 years, under a contract not to exceed $55.31 million. Infinite Grid Capital, LLC has since acquired full ownership of the company, a change the council consented to in December 2025. In June the council awarded a construction contract of up to $8,386,560 to Baker Electric & Renewables LLC of Escondido. The grant agreement requires the battery’s capacity to be available to the state’s grid during extreme events for five years after it comes online. Former Mayor Bill Paparian urged the council in a June 21 letter to delay the award and order a full environmental impact report or supplemental analysis, writing that the site sits about 455 feet from Blair High School and Middle School and citing the January 2025 fire at a battery plant in Moss Landing. He wrote that the project’s environmental review “leaves important gaps.” The council approved the contract unanimously on its consent calendar. The city’s environmental study concluded that mitigation would reduce potentially significant impacts, including hazards and hazardous materials, to less than significant, and the Energy Commission relied on it in finding no significant effect. The Moss Landing plant used nickel manganese cobalt batteries, which carry a greater risk of thermal runaway than lithium iron phosphate, according to Ric O’Connell, executive director of GridLab, who also wrote in February 2025 that “LFP systems are also not immune to safety issues.” Project information is at https://pwp.cityofpasadena.net/glenarm-battery-energy-storage-system-bess/. Construction inquiries go to Jessica Velazquez at JEVelazquez@CityOfPasadena.net.

artigo.texto: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited (NTPC REL) invites bids for an EPC package with land to develop up to 600 MW of solar capacity. The EPC project developer is required to arrange land for the solar project and the BESS project owner This comprises a (300 MW + 300 MW) ISTS-connected ground-mounted solar project near the Dhule Solar Project in Maharashtra. Bids have been invited until November 13, 2026. Brief Scope of Work Under the scope of work, the developer is require to handle design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, packing, forwarding, transportation, unloading, storage, and installation of the solar project. The bidders are expected to provide a 300 MW solar project under Block 1 for a minimum net worth / turnover threshold of Rs. 192 Crores. Under block 2, the bidder is expected to provide a 300 MW for a minimum financial requirement of Rs. 192 Crores, bringing the combined (Block 1 + Block 2) requirement to Rs. 384 Crores. The scope also requires the commissioning as well as the operation and maintenance (O&M) of the grid-connected solar PV project located near NTPC REL’s Dhule Solar Project. This includes the power evacuation system from the solar project to NTPC REL’s Dhule Solar Project PSS / ISTS substation, as well as the development of a terminal bay at NTPC REL’s Dhule Project PSS. Additionally, the scope includes identifying, acquiring, and completing the total transfer of ownership or lease of encumbrance-free land (including land for BESS) in favor of NTPC Renewable Energy Limited. The developer is required to supply, erect, and commission new 220 kV terminal line bays at NTPC REL’s Dhule Solar Project PSS. The EPC developer must develop a dedicated 220 kV transmission line, including Right of Way (ROW), from the solar plant to NTPC REL’s Dhule Solar Project PSS. The project comprises two blocks of 300 MW each. The evacuation scheme may involve either a single common PSS or two separate PSSs.

artigo.texto: Engie recently partnered with CMA CGM on a large biomethane project in Le Havre and expanded its global battery storage portfolio across Europe, while completing Chile’s first coal to gas power plant conversion. Taken together, these projects highlight Engie’s push to reposition its asset base toward low carbon fuels, grid flexibility and long term energy infrastructure. We will now look at how Engie’s expanded energy storage build out could influence the company’s broader investment narrative and risk profile. Scan opportunities alongside Engie by reviewing a curated 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks that explores how electricity networks handle storage, congestion, and the rise of low carbon generation. Engie Investment Narrative Recap Owning Engie means believing that a higher share of earnings can come from regulated networks, long term contracts and flexible low carbon assets rather than more volatile power prices. The current build out in storage and low carbon fuels leans in that direction but does not change the fact that high economic net debt of about €60b remains the key watchpoint. In the near term, the main positive swing factor is still execution on the performance and digitalisation program and integration of UK Power Networks. The biggest risk is that Renewables and Flex Power EBIT pressure persists, so new projects fail to fully offset weaker capture prices, leaving leverage and dividend coverage under closer scrutiny. The broad battery storage expansion across Poland, Romania, Spain, Belgium, Portugal, the UK and the Netherlands looks most relevant here. It directly plugs into Engie’s thesis of earning more predictable cash flows from flexibility assets that back data centers, grids and long duration contracts, rather than relying on favourable spot pricing. This roll out also sharpens execution risk. Engie has to deliver multiple large projects on time and on budget while debt is already high and renewables EBIT has come under pressure. For you as a shareholder, the key question is whether these new storage assets can enter service smoothly and support the planned earnings mix shift without stretching the balance sheet further. What The Analyst Forecasts Imply For Engie Engie’s storage rollout sits against a backdrop of analyst forecasts that already bake in fairly robust expansion in the wider business. Consensus assumes revenue can rise by 8.5% a year over the next three years, with profit margins edging from 5.8% today to 6.2% by 2029. That earnings mix shift is captured in projections that see earnings moving from €4.1b today to €5.6b in 2029, with the more optimistic forecasts reaching €6.3b, while share count is expected to climb by about 2.8% annually as Engie funds growth. On those numbers, the quoted price target assumes Engie reaches about €90.2b of revenue and €5.6b of earnings in 2029 and supports a higher valuation multiple over time. To align with that view, investors would effectively be treating the group as capable of sustaining a P/E of 17.9x those 2029 earnings, compared with 13.6x today and around 15.8x for the wider GB integrated utilities peer set. That gap puts the focus squarely on whether Engie can turn its battery, renewables and regulated networks pipeline into the steadier cash flows implied by those long term forecasts while carrying roughly €60b of economic net debt. Engie's narrative projects €90.2b revenue and €5.6b earnings by 2029. This assumes 8.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about €1.5b from €4.1b today. Uncover why Engie's fair value indicates a 30% potential upside to its current price, which could narrow quickly. Exploring Other Perspectives One alternate angle on Engie leans heavily on the UK Power Networks catalyst and paints a far more upbeat story. Those bullish analysts were already assuming revenue reaches about €100.2b and earnings €5.8b by 2029, compared with €90.2b and €5.6b in the baseline view, before any impact from these new biomethane and storage projects. artigo.texto: Norway's sovereign wealth fund is still avoiding battery storage, fearing a decline in returns Norway's sovereign wealth fund, the largest of its kind in the world, is not yet investing in battery storage. The reasons are the insufficient scale of available projects and the risk of so-called market cannibalization, in which a growing number of batteries gradually narrows the price spreads on which their operators make money. The fund nevertheless considers energy storage a potentially suitable complement to its investments in wind and solar power. “We see significant risk of market cannibalization from batteries,” said Borge Rygh Sivertsen, portfolio manager for new energy at Norway's sovereign wealth fund, at the Energirike conference in Haugesund, Norway. According to him, the economics of battery storage are based primarily on the differences between high and low electricity prices. Batteries buy electricity when prices are low and then sell it when electricity is more expensive. However, as the number of storage facilities grows, more operators compete for the same opportunities. If many batteries buy electricity during cheap hours and feed it into the grid when prices are high, the price spreads gradually narrow. This reduces the potential returns of individual projects and makes their future revenues less predictable. According to Sivertsen, this uncertainty is a significant obstacle to investment. The fund is therefore waiting for now, even though it considers storage a technology that could complement its portfolio of wind and solar power plants. Available projects are not large enough Another obstacle is the size of the investments. The Norwegian fund typically considers projects worth around 500 million euros, or approximately 5 billion Norwegian kroner. According to Sivertsen, it cannot invest in smaller projects on sufficiently competitive terms. The fund already invests in renewable energy in Europe. Through partnerships with RWE, Ørsted, Iberdrola and EnBW, it has acquired stakes in projects with a total installed capacity of 3.3 GW. The fund's investment mandate allows it to invest in renewable energy in Europe and North America, across the energy value chain from generation to electricity distribution. Energy storage is also covered, but its economic attractiveness must meet the fund's requirements. Investment environment clouded by uncertainty According to Sivertsen, geopolitical uncertainty, fluctuations in natural gas prices and higher inflation are also making energy projects harder to finance. These factors increase the cost of capital and make it harder for buyers and sellers to agree on project prices. The fund representative also noted that investors have recently been placing greater emphasis on energy security, while some have partially scaled back their financing of renewable energy. Uncertainty about future electricity supply and demand is therefore another risk that must be taken into account in investment decisions. Renewables currently account for approximately 1% of the value of Norway's sovereign wealth fund. According to Sivertsen, this share could rise to 2% under its investment mandate. artigo.texto: Stellenbosch solar and battery storage: Wine harvest shows why timing counts Stellenbosch’s procurement of up to 41.9 MW of solar photovoltaic capacity and 14.8 MWh of battery storage, awarded, 22 May 2026, comes as new data from Vergenoegd Löw shows how sharply electricity demand can rise during the wine harvest. The two developments point to a broader local energy issue: whether new solar and storage can help meet the needs of Stellenbosch’s commercial customers when demand is highest, beyond adding lower-cost power over the course of a year. At Vergenoegd Löw, an August 2026 PV-monitoring report provided to Cape Business News earlier this month shows what that seasonal demand looks like at an individual commercial operation. Harvest drives the electricity surge In February, the estate used more than twice as much electricity as it did in June. Its solar system generated the equivalent of 63% of that demand, so its grid electricity was only about a third higher. Compared with June, the estate’s reported load was 40 318 kWh higher in February. Grid electricity was only 6 603 kWh higher. Of interest is the coinciding timing of peak solar potential and the harvest season. February falls within the Cape wine harvest, when electricity demand rises sharply, while solar production is also strong. March followed the same pattern, with solar again covering more than half of the estate’s demand. January, the estate’s heaviest month for electricity, relied more on the grid and also drew on a generator. The estate still draws on the grid every month. What changes is the balance between on-site generation and grid electricity as demand and solar output rise and fall. For a seasonal commercial operation, generating more electricity on site during its busiest period can limit the increase in power that has to be bought from the grid. That matters as tariffs climb. Eskom’s tariff increases this year were close to 9%, from April for its direct customers and from July for municipalities. Almost half the load from PV Between January and August, the estate’s solar system generated the equivalent of almost half its electricity use. The monitoring report records 183.17 tonnes of CO₂ avoided over the same period. The harvest figures are more revealing than that average. In every other month, solar covered less than half of the estate’s demand. For a seasonal business, that timing is the central feature of the data: the harvest months, when demand climbs, are also the months in which solar covers the largest share of it. Stellenbosch is adding generation and storage The municipal project is on a very different scale, but its combination of solar and battery storage points to a wider change in Stellenbosch’s electricity system. The municipality’s tender, BSM 89/25, called for 41.9 MW of solar PV and 14.8 MWh of battery storage, procured through an independent power producer model. The RFP was issued in 2025, and the project was awarded in May 2026. For commercial electricity users, storage can address the gap between when solar is generated and when power is needed. At Vergenoegd Löw, the harvest provides a favourable match because its demand rises during a period of strong solar generation. The municipal buildout is also being accompanied by network investment. Stellenbosch has tendered for two 20 MVA, 66/11 kV transformers to replace three existing 7.5 MVA units at its main substation.

artigo.texto: The increasingly contentious national debate over data centers moved into Mesa last week as Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes told a town hall that their explosive growth threatens to leave communities with higher utility bills, a range of health and environmental problems and inadequate government oversight. Addressing over 250 people at a Mesa community center Oct. 14, Mayes questioned whether Arizona has done enough to protect residents as developers rush to build the enormous facilities needed to support artificial intelligence, cloud computing and other digital services. The setting was particularly appropriate. Mesa has become a major data center hub, with over 7.5 million square feet of existing and proposed facilities. Yet roughly three-quarters of those attending the meeting had traveled from Ahwatukee, where residents have organized against a 1-million-square-foot facility currently being constructed amid neighborhoods with thousands of homes. Phoenix officials contend California-based Menlo Equities was allowed to build the five-building data campus because the site had been rezoned since the mid-1990s. Critics contend that when data centers were included in that zoning category 30 years ago, no one could envision the mammoth facilities that have torn apart communities across the country. Like Mesa, Phoenix last year adopted a more targeted set of guidelines for data centers, but projects like Menlo’s were not covered because they had already been approved under the older zoning standards. Mayes, a Democrat seeking reelection, has called for a moratorium on data center construction “to get our house in order to determine the principles that should guide this build-up, if it happens, and to decide what’s needed to protect our communities in Arizona. “This issue is too important to let data center developers themselves decide what is right for our state and our communities,” Mayes told the audience. She then put data centers’ explosive growth into perspective for Arizonans: “The Phoenix area is now the second largest U.S. data center hub. … My office has identified more than 180 operating or planned data centers across Arizona.” Of those, 110 are operating, 10 are under construction and almost 40 more are planned, according to Mayes. The Legislature and Gov. Katie Hobbs agreed in June to impose a three-year moratorium starting July 1 on millions of dollars in tax incentives that data centers have been getting from the state. The state Commerce Authority reportedly received 113 applications for those incentives in the second half of June before the moratorium took effect. In the last 10 years, 123 applications were filed. Mayes said her office’s research has found that data center growth in Arizona poses especially dire circumstances amid the state’s unfolding water crisis. “If all planned data centers in the Phoenix area are built,” she said, “stress on our local water supplies will increase by 32%. That would occur at the same time that Arizona loses 30% of our Colorado River water supplies.” She also asserted that data centers’ demand for electricity would drive up customers’ utility bills. Ironically, just hours before her town hall, Chris Bauer, vice president and treasurer for Pinnacle West Capital Corporation and its primary subsidiary, Arizona Public Service Company (APS), told the audience at the East Valley Partnership’s Statespersons’ Luncheon his company intends to “make growth pay for growth. The attorney general currently is suing APS’ proposed 14% rate hike. Mayes also cited noise and even temperature impacts of data centers. She said data centers “regularly generate 94 decibels of noise.” Mesa’s noise ordinance has a 24-hour average sound limit of 60 decibels for residential zones and 65 for commercial zones. She also cited a recent Arizona State University study that says data centers can add 4 degrees to a neighborhood’s temperature downwind from a facility. Mayes outlined a series of demands she wants Arizona to develop for data centers, starting with transparency. She said some data center companies have required municipalities to enter nondisclosure agreements “which limit the ability of local governments … to discuss the project with their constituents.” She said she is currently suing unidentified municipalities over such agreements. She also said data centers should be forbidden from creating nuisances, that natural resources must be protected, that developers be required to pay fully for their power, and that the facilities “must give back.” “In Arizona, it is a tradition that any large development project gives back to the community it inevitably impacts, whether this is through taxes, fees, assessments, or even water storage credits,” she said. “We must ensure that communities that host data centers and that choose to host data centers indeed all Arizonans benefit from their development.” Mayes conceded her office is studying a major issue that has developed when municipalities in Arizona try to deny a data center from being built. Proposition 207, passed by an overwhelming majority of voters in 2006, requires any government level in Arizona to compensate a property owner if zoning or other restrictions lower the fair market value of the property. Earlier this year, Phoenix City Council reversed a denial of a permit for a data center after the property owner filed a claim for over $50 million. “We’re hearing a lot about Prop 207 from cities,” Mayes told the audience – well, mainly from the city of Phoenix, and we are analyzing that issue. So I’m not going to opine yet on Prop 207. But what I will say very clearly is that Prop 207 does not prevent me as your attorney general from filing a nuisance lawsuit against the AI data center.” She added, “I am certain that there are data centers that are being plopped in the middle of new neighborhoods that would meet the classical definition of a nuisance.” Mayes’ Republican opponent, Senate President Warren Pe

artigo.texto: Mesmo que seja para fazer uma pergunta, criar uma imagem, gerar um vídeo de poucos segundos ou editar um texto, consultar um chatbot de IA na nuvem aciona servidores cujo funcionamento depende permanentemente de muitos recursos físicos: espaço, eletricidade, sistemas de resfriamento e, principalmente, minerais e metais raros, necessários para a fabricação dos servidores, redes, unidades de processamento, sensores e cabeamentos dos data centers que hospedam o serviço.. A popularização de ferramentas como ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini e Perplexity no dia a dia das pessoas alimenta o crescimento acelerado dessa infraestrutura, que para funcionar conecta os interesses dos proprietários de minas e refinadoras às necessidades de grandes complexos de processamento de dados. Essa expansão abre uma nova fronteira extrativa: os benefícios econômicos gerados pela nova tecnologia circulam por cadeias globais, mas grande parte dos custos socioambientais dessa exploração são arcados pelos países que fornecem a matéria prima, como poucas contrapartidas. Uma governança mais justa do desenvolvimento e do uso global da Inteligência Artificial exige, portanto, identificar e responsabilizar claramente quem controla e, por isso, quem deve responder pelos impactos provocados por essa nova tecnologia. Escala industrial Comumente associado à ideia simplificada de “nuvem”, na verdade o funcionamento dos data centers que oferecem serviços e operam modelos de IA é caro e danoso ao ambiente. Atualmente, existem cerca de 12 mil data centers no planeta, entre unidades operacionais e projetos, dos quais cerca de 1.360 são considerados de hiperescala. No estado de Louisiana, nos EUA, por exemplo, a Meta constrói um complexo que abrigará o Hyperion, serviço global destinado ao treinamento de desenvolvedores de sistemas de IA. O projeto prevê uma área construída de cerca de 930 mil metros quadrados, e investimentos anunciados superiores a US$ 50 bilhões. A cadeia começa nas minas e se amplia com a energia Servidores, chips e redes necessários ao funcionamento de data centers de IA, grandes ou pequenos, exigem a utilização de cobre, silício, gálio, germânio, tântalo, terras raras, prata, ouro e metais do grupo da platina. Alguns desses materiais precisam atingir elevada pureza para uso eletrônico. Baterias e sistemas de fornecimento de energia ampliam essa dependência. Fabricar aparelhos com forte presença de componentes eletrônicos pode mobilizar entre 50 e 350 vezes o peso desses aparelhos em matérias-primas. A Agência Internacional de Energia estima que os data centers de IA existentes no mundo consumiram cerca de 485 terawatts (o equivalente a 485 trilhões de watts) por hora, só em 2025. E projeta um consumo de 950 terawatts por hora em 2030, considerando todo o setor. Empresas anunciam que grande parte dessa demanda deverá ser atendida por projetos de energia renovável. Embora as fontes solar e eólica sejam centrais para a descarbonização, seus equipamentos, as redes elétricas e os sistemas de armazenamento também exigem grandes quantidades de minerais. Um exemplo dessa infraestrutura é o parque solar Orion Solar Belt, no Texas, que reúne mais de 1,3 milhão de módulos fotovoltaicos de 700 watts cada. O empreendimento tem o Google como cliente âncora e fornece eletricidade à rede que abastece os data centers da empresa. Uma comparação hipotética ilustra a escala: para gerar os 950 terawatts por hora previstos para 2030 apenas com módulos solares de 700 watts, serão necessários cerca de 775 milhões de painéis. Os módulos solares podem operar por 25 a 35 anos, mas alguns equipamentos de data centers precisam ser substituídos em intervalos muito mais curtos, de poucos anos, e isso é outro grande problema. Um estudo de 2024 projetou o acúmulo de 1,2 milhão a 5 milhões de toneladas de resíduos eletrônicos pela IA generativa entre 2020 e 2030. Sem reutilização ou recuperação adequadas, perdem-se metais e aumentam os passivos ambientais para toda a sociedade. Os custos econômicos e sociais nos territórios produtores Além disso, fornecer minerais não assegura aos países de onde são extraídos nenhum controle sobre as tecnologias de maior valor agregado geradas para o desenvolvimento da IA. Como no século XVI, a tendência é que os ganhos com a comercialização do serviço concentrem-se nas empresas, enquanto as comunidades das regiões produtoras enfrentam poluição, riscos ocupacionais e disputas pela terra e pela água– esta última elemento fundamental para a operação a longo prazo de grandes data centers. Nesta complexidade, empregos, tributos e royalties precisariam ser acompanhados de proteção trabalhista, fiscalização e de serviços públicos. Nossas pesquisas bibliográficas e documentais reuniram evidências dessas desigualdades. As cadeias estudadas abastecem diferentes setores, incluindo eletrônica, baterias e sistemas de energia utilizados pelos data centers. Segundo estimativas do Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos, a República Democrática do Congo respondeu por cerca de 73% da produção mundial de cobalto em 2025. Investigações recentes documentaram a ocorrência de trabalho infantil, acidentes fatais e exposição a substâncias tóxicas nesta atividade no país, que é um dos mais pobres do mundo. Na Indonésia, responsável por aproximadamente dois terços da produção mundial de níquel em 2025, pesquisas registraram processamento dependente de carvão, contaminação e conflitos territoriais. No Chile e no Peru, líderes na produção de cobre, estudos identificaram exposição de comunidades a metais tóxicos. No Triângulo do Lítio, formado por Chile, Argentina e Bolívia, a extração de salmouras pressiona recursos hídricos em regiões áridas. Na China, a mineração de terras raras foi associada à contaminação da água e dos solos. Em Mianmar, investigações documentaram poluição e coerção contra comunidades em áreas mineradoras controladas por grupos armados. artigo.texto: GRIDCO Limited, Odisha’s renewable energy nodal agency under the Odisha Renewable Energy Policy 2022, has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) to appoint an experienced consultant for conducting an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the proposed 225 MW Upper Indravati Floating Solar Photovoltaic and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Project. The project, including its associated power evacuation infrastructure and transmission lines, is located across the Nabarangpur and Kalahandi districts of Odisha. The consultancy assignment aims to evaluate the potential environmental and social impacts of the proposed floating solar and battery storage development. The assessment will follow applicable Indian regulations, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) Performance Standards 2012, and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines. The selected consultant will be responsible for undertaking detailed technical, physical, biological, and socio-economic assessments to identify potential risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures. The scope of work includes evaluating the project footprint over the Indravati reservoir and examining its potential effects on water quality, aquatic ecosystems, biodiversity, and surrounding communities. The consultant will also conduct a Critical Habitat Assessment to identify ecologically sensitive areas that may require special protection. Hydrodynamic water quality modelling and oil spill modelling for synthetic transformer oils will be undertaken to assess potential environmental risks associated with project operations. Battery energy storage safety will be another important component of the assignment. The consultant will evaluate risks associated with fire incidents, thermal runaway, hazardous waste management, and other potential environmental and operational hazards linked to BESS installations. A Climate Change Risk Assessment will also be prepared to examine the project’s vulnerability to climate-related risks and identify suitable adaptation measures. In addition to the technical assessments, the selected consultant will prepare several environmental and social management documents. These will include an Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Livelihood Restoration Plan (LRP), and Indigenous Peoples Development Plan (IPDP). These plans are intended to establish appropriate procedures for managing environmental impacts, engaging affected stakeholders, addressing livelihood-related concerns, and protecting vulnerable communities. GRIDCO issued the RFP document on October 16, 2026. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for October 30, 2026, at 11:00 AM at the GRIDCO Conference Hall, with video conferencing facilities also available. Responses to queries and the publication of any corrigendum are scheduled for November 3, 2026. The last date for online bid submission is November 17, 2026, until 3:00 PM, while techno-commercial bids will be opened at 5:00 PM on the same day. Technical proposal evaluation and declaration of qualified bidders are scheduled for November 20, followed by price bid declaration on November 25. GRIDCO plans to issue the Letter of Award on December 2 and sign the contract agreement on December 23, 2026. The tender document costs ₹10,000 plus 18% GST, bringing the total fee to ₹11,800. Bidders must furnish an Earnest Money Deposit of ₹1 lakh, while the selected consultant will be required to submit a Performance Bank Guarantee of ₹2.5 lakh within 20 days of the work order. The guarantee must remain valid for 12 months, with an additional six-month claim period. Proposals must remain valid for at least 180 days from the submission deadline. artigo.texto: BOSTON, July 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Factorial Energy Inc.(Nasdaq: FAC) (“Factorial” or the “Company”), a global leader in next-generation solid-state battery technology, today announced it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with SK On Co., Ltd. (“SK On”), a leading global battery manufacturer. This partnership brings together Factorial’s advanced cell technology and scale-up expertise with SK On’s extensive global manufacturing network and pilot capabilities. A key objective of this collaboration is to assess whether and how SK On’s world-class manufacturing footprint and existing lithium-ion battery manufacturing infrastructure could support future development of solid-state battery technologies. SK On is recognized as a leading global manufacturer of electric vehicle batteries serving automotive OEMs including Hyundai Motor Group, Ford, Volkswagen, and Ferrari. The company has more than 200 GWh of annual production capacity worldwide, including approximately 100 GWh in the United States. Its U.S. manufacturing footprint includes 22 GWh of capacity in Commerce, Georgia, as well as operations in Tennessee. Under the MOU, Factorial and SK On will jointly evaluate the technical feasibility and manufacturing considerations for Factorial’s FEST® solid-state battery technologies, drawing on SK On’s battery technology and manufacturing expertise, as well as its global manufacturing capabilities. The collaboration highlights Factorial’s capital-light approach to industrialization, which is centered on developing batteries that can leverage established manufacturing infrastructure to accelerate the path to industrialization. “A battery breakthrough only matters if it can be manufactured at scale,” said Siyu Huang, CEO of Factorial. “That is what makes this partnership with SK On so significant. Their manufacturing footprint spans some of the world’s most advanced battery facilities, and their expertise will be critical in shaping how solid-state battery technology integrates into global production ecosystems.” Factorial’s solid‑state platforms are engineered to serve as the core energy foundation for next‑generation mobility, aerospace systems, and hyperscale data centers. Factorial’s high energy density batteries enable smaller, lighter batteries and deliver system level efficiency required for increasingly demanding missions across land, air, and orbit. “This collaboration provides an opportunity to evaluate the technical feasibility and manufacturing readiness of solid-state battery technologies, drawing on SK On’s battery technology and manufacturing expertise,” said Ki-soo Park, Head of the Institute of Future Technology at SK On. “SK On will continue to explore collaboration opportunities in next-generation battery technologies.” Through this collaboration, Factorial and SK On will explore opportunities to support the future development of solid-state battery technologies for mobility and high-performance markets, advancing the next generation of energy storage. This marks Factorial’s manufacturing-focused partnership with a global battery producer, reflecting the company’s strategy of scaling through established manufacturing ecosystems. The MOU is non-binding, except for certain customary binding provisions. The terms of the collaboration are expected to be set forth in definitive binding agreements. Through its proprietary FEST® and Solstice™ platforms, engineered for scalable manufacturing, Factorial delivers industry-leading performance across aerospace, energy storage and mobility applications. Mercedes-Benz’ real-world road testing in a lightly modified test vehicle achieved over 1,200 km of range on a single charge, while Stellantis-lab testing verified 77 Ah cells demonstrating high energy density, fast-charging, and robust use for energy and power performance across temperature extremes, with the technology successfully integrated into a fully built Dodge Charger Daytona demonstration vehicle. artigo.texto: Claro e Vivo questionam data centers como obrigação no leilão de 6 GHz Anatel defende vínculo com telecomunicações e prevê acesso aberto por 15 anos; Abrint pede proteção aos investimentos existentes. Vivo e Claro questionaram a inclusão de investimentos em data centers entre as obrigações das vencedoras do futuro leilão de 6 GHz e na audiência pública da Anatel realizada nesta sexta-feira, 16. As empresas defenderam que os compromissos associados à compra do espectro priorizem a expansão da conectividade. A agência sustentou que a infraestrutura de processamento de dados está ligada à prestação dos serviços de telecomunicações e à experiência dos usuários. A proposta em consulta prevê financiar núcleos regionais neutros e nós de borda, com prioridade para áreas menos atendidas por esse tipo de infraestrutura. Os recursos seriam aportados pelas vencedoras e administrados por uma entidade constituída por elas, sob a governança de um grupo presidido pela Anatel. Monique Barros, da Claro, afirmou que o questionamento da empresa está na vinculação do financiamento dos data centers à aquisição de frequências para redes móveis. “A questão que colocamos para reflexão não é sobre a importância do data center, e sim se a sua implementação deve constituir compromisso vinculado à aquisição de espectro”, declarou. A companhia apontou necessidades de investimento em cobertura de rodovias, áreas remotas e evolução tecnológica. “Essa evolução do serviço de telecomunicações devia ser o único foco dos compromissos dos editais de licitação do nosso setor”, acrescentou Monique. Rafael Andrade de Oliveira, representante da Vivo, argumentou que a implantação de data centers não está entre as modalidades de compromisso previstas no artigo 9º do Decreto nº 9.612/2018, que trata das políticas públicas de telecomunicações. A Vivo defendeu compromissos voltados à conectividade e executados diretamente pelas vencedoras, dispensando a entidade administradora. A GSMA, representada por Larissa Jales, também pediu aprofundamento da discussão sobre valoração, governança e relação dessas obrigações com as autorizações de radiofrequência. Demanda assegurada por cinco anos Na apresentação da proposta, a Anatel detalhou que as operadoras vencedoras deverão assegurar demanda mínima correspondente a 30% da capacidade energizada de cada núcleo nos primeiros 60 meses. O objetivo apresentado é dar condições iniciais de funcionamento aos projetos. Após 36 meses, nenhum grupo poderá ocupar mais de 40% da capacidade. A infraestrutura deverá oferecer acesso aberto por pelo menos 15 anos, mediante oferta pública de referência homologada pela agência. Também está previsto uso de, no mínimo, 80% de energia renovável. A entidade administradora ficará responsável pela gestão dos recursos, seleção, acompanhamento e auditoria dos projetos, mas não será executora dos projetos. A escolha das localidades incluirá critérios de priorização, teste de mercado para identificar investimentos privados existentes ou previstos e avaliação do déficit de viabilidade econômica. Recursos sem projetos elegíveis poderão ser direcionados a fibra e cobertura móvel. Abrint pede proteção aos investimentos A Abrint reconheceu o objetivo de aproximar processamento e interconexão dos usuários, mas pediu esclarecimentos sobre os critérios de localização e a verificação da neutralidade das instalações. “Os provedores regionais também vêm investindo em Edge Data Centers”, destacou Artur Coimbra, representante da associação. A entidade quer evitar que projetos financiados com recursos do leilão disputem os mesmos clientes em condições favorecidas, comprometendo investimentos já realizados. “A prioridade deve decorrer da necessidade demonstrada e da insuficiência da oferta disponível”, acrescentou Coimbra. A equipe da Anatel disse que evitar essa sobreposição é uma preocupação da proposta e solicitou contribuições para aperfeiçoar os mecanismos. Também defendeu que a inclusão de data centers acompanha a necessidade de considerar outras infraestruturas associadas às telecomunicações, além das redes de acesso e transporte.

artigo.texto: Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range. Ore from the Cahaya and Hengjaya mines was traced through regional smelters and Chinese processing plants run by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, a cathode manufacturer that supplies CATL, the world’s largest battery maker. Huayou’s corporate reports list US and European carmakers as end-users, while additional corporate files and trade data show a separate route from Huayou to LG, a South Korean group that also supplies battery products to leading carmakers, via Poland. Satellite analysis shows the mines have led to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by the indigenous Tolaki people. “We used to ask the forest for protection in return for our offerings,” said Wadimula, a Tolaki elder whose home sits on the edge of the 21,000-hectare Cahaya mining concession. “Destroying it means destroying our own life.” Electric vehicles are less environmentally harmful than fossil fuel-burning engines, which spew gases that foul the air and heat the planet, but western carmakers have struggled to clean up supply chains for batteries built with critical minerals from Africa, Asia and South America. Environmental groups warn that a failure to curb the boom of material-hungry SUVs is exacerbating the destruction by increasing the quantity mined. Ore from the two mining concessions is sent to a nickel smelter in an industrial complex in Morowali, on Indonesia’s eastern coast, operated by Huayou’s local subsidiary, where limonite is refined into mixed hydroxide precipitate, the primary raw material used to make battery cathodes. In 2024, $606m worth of mixed hydroxide precipitate was shipped from the Morowali plant to ports in China, followed by further shipments worth $470m in 2025. The processed ore was transported overland to Huayou cathode manufacturing sites in Quzhou, near Shanghai, and Yulin, near the border with Vietnam. Public filings do not disclose specific volumes or timings of sales from Huayou to CATL, which would be needed to directly connect specific ore shipments to car batteries, but Huayou confirmed group-level supplies to CATL in response to a regulatory inquiry by the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2024. Chengdu B&M, a downstream subsidiary of Huayou, has also confirmed the supply of “large quantities” to CATL. The investigation, published in partnership with Voxeurop and other European media partners, traced shipments from mines and refineries in Sulawesi to China, and then again from Huayou cathode and CATL battery factories to the assembly lines of carmakers in the US and Europe. Volkswagen’s facility in Braunschweig, for instance, received a shipment in October 2024 of 24 tonnes of cell modules worth about $390,000, according to data from Volza, a trade platform. The shift to a carbon-free economy is pushing up demand for critical minerals in countries with weak environmental safeguards, though experts have argued the mining boom can be tempered without slowing the shift away from dirty fuels. In 2023, a report found lithium demand in the US transport sector could be reduced by 18% to 66% compared with a business-as-usual scenario, by improving public transport, walking and cycling more, and buying smaller cars. Better recycling could bring demand reductions as high as 92%, the report found. Global demand for nickel is set to double to 5.5m tonnes by 2040, according to the International Energy Agency, much of it mined in Indonesia and then refined in China. The loss of trees in mining concessions means the carbon footprint of nickel from the worst mines may be up to 500 times greater than previously reported, a study in Nature Communications found last year. The Cahaya and Hengjaya mines are located in woodlands designated as “production forest”, which are intended for forestry rather than industrial activities. However, successive Indonesian governments have weakened safeguards and carved out exemptions for miners as demand for nickel has soared. Nickel mining may be responsible for two-thirds of the forest loss recorded since 2001 within the area encompassed by the Cahaya concession, and over half of the loss in the Hengjaya concession, spatial analysis conducted by geospatial firm The TreeMap suggests. Sulawesi Cahaya Mineral (SCM), the company that operates the Cahaya mine, contributed to clearing an additional 330 hectares of forest in 2024, according to an analysis by Auriga, an Indonesian nonprofit. The same year, it delivered 11m tonnes of limonite ore – almost all of its production – to Huayou’s smelter. Deliveries increased to nearly 12.5m tonnes throughout 2025. The plant also continued to receive ore from the Hengjaya mine by road, local lorry drivers said. SCM received two administrative sanctions last year for illegally clearing more than 450 hectares of forest beyond the boundaries of its permitted clearing area. The company is a subsidiary of Merdeka Battery Materials, part of a group whose shareholders include Huayou and CATL. The carmakers identified as end-users of Huayou cathodes or recipients of shipments from CATL include Volkswagen, Volvo, Ford, General Motors, Tesla, BMW, Stellantis and Hyundai. Mercedes-Benz was separately linked to Huayou. Many of the companies said they did not source nickel directly, they assessed and mitigated adverse impacts, and they required suppliers to comply with responsible sourcing standards.

A Everpure divulgou uma pesquisa global que revela que 88% dos líderes C-level de grandes companhias acreditam que uma falha na soberania de dados pode lhes custar o emprego, enquanto 91% temem prejuízos financeiros e danos à reputação corporativa.
Apesar desses riscos, 64% das organizações pesquisadas operam sem uma estratégia formal de soberania de dados, expondo uma vulnerabilidade na gestão moderna de dados corporativos diante do atual cenário de incerteza geopolítica.  A soberania de dados tornou-se uma questão crítica para os negócios, diante de riscos que vão da extração de dados imposta por autoridades estrangeiras a possíveis incidentes de negação de serviço (DoS).
Para avaliar a relação entre as prioridades estratégicas e o preparo operacional, o Global Data Sovereignty Report 2026, da Everpure, ouviu 2.100 líderes empresariais em oito países, e os resultados mostram que a preocupação com esses riscos ainda não se reflete na preparação para enfrentá-los.
“No Brasil, temos observado empresas reavaliando onde manter seus dados mais sensíveis à medida que os projetos de IA avançam dos testes para a produção.  Custos, requisitos regulatórios e a necessidade de maior controle sobre os dados estão levando algumas empresas a reconsiderar o que manter na nuvem e o que faz mais sentido trazer para sua própria infraestrutura ou para data centers de terceiros.
Ao mesmo tempo, avançar com IA exige uma base sólida de dados, com qualidade, governança e políticas claras de gestão.
São temas que vêm ganhando espaço nas discussões com as empresas brasileiras”, explica Claudio Tancredi, country manager da EverPure no Brasil.  Preocupação com a soberania de dados:
90% das organizações reconhecem a soberania de dados como uma preocupação para os negócios, e a maioria espera consequências graves para as finanças ou para suas lideranças em caso de falha.
85% estão dispostas a abrir mão de recursos e funcionalidades avançadas para contratar um provedor local ou soberano.  ?  40% já limitam o uso de provedores de SaaS que dependem de infraestrutura fora do país.
Falta de preparo para lidar com riscos:
  • Apesar desses resultados, 64% das organizações operam sem uma estratégia formal de soberania de dados.
  • 62% não têm visibilidade completa sobre quem pode acessar, controlar e gerenciar seus dados.
  • 56% não têm planos para lidar com extração de dados por motivos geopolíticos ou com interrupção de serviços.
  • 56% admitem não ter as competências e a capacidade necessárias para executar iniciativas de soberania, enquanto 36% enfrentam dificuldades para obter o apoio da alta liderança.
Apenas 9% consideram como prioridade máxima a proteção contra o acesso a dados por autoridades de outras jurisdições.  Os resultados revelam uma “lacuna de soberania” entre o reconhecimento dos riscos pelos executivos e o preparo operacional para enfrentá-los.
Muitas empresas ainda tratam a soberania como uma questão de rotina de cibersegurança ou conformidade.
Com isso, não asseguram o controle sobre seus dados nem conseguem se proteger de ameaças geopolíticas que podem ter consequências significativas para os negócios.
“Os líderes seniores entendem que seus empregos estão em jogo quando se trata de soberania de dados, mas muitos ainda se concentram nos riscos errados.  A soberania não diz respeito apenas ao local onde os dados são armazenados, mas à visibilidade e ao controle completos sobre eles por meio de uma gestão moderna de dados.
Quem pode acessar os dados, quais jurisdições se aplicam e se os dados ou serviços críticos para o negócio podem sofrer interrupções são perguntas fundamentais que toda organização deveria fazer”, diz Alex McMullan, diretor internacional de Tecnologia da Everpure.
“A soberania digital deixou de ser uma discussão sobre conformidade e se tornou uma preocupação crítica para os conselhos de administração.  O desafio para os executivos não se limita a saber onde seus dados estão hospedados.
Trata-se de ter controle total sobre todos os acessos e transferências de dados, incluindo todos os metadados, assegurar proteção contra solicitações extraterritoriais de dados e gerenciar os riscos de TI e de fornecedores diante das incertezas geopolíticas”, diz Rahiel Nasir, diretor de pesquisa e analista principal de Soberania Digital Mundial da IDC.
Recomendação da Everpure: soberania desde a concepção Uma estratégia de soberania bem-sucedida exige transformar o reconhecimento passivo dos riscos em ações direcionadas e concretas.
Para isso, as organizações podem seguir um conjunto de etapas interligadas para alcançar a soberania desde a concepção (ou soberania por design): uma abordagem orientada pelos negócios e pela avaliação de riscos, na qual os controles de soberania e a governança são aplicados de acordo com o risco de cada conjunto de dados, aplicação e carga de trabalho.
O foco se desloca da soberania nacional para a soberania corporativa, uma abordagem baseada no apetite ao risco e na visão sobre regulação específicos de cada organização.  Esse modelo permite proteger ativos críticos dos principais riscos de soberania sem abrir mão da flexibilidade, da inovação ou da escala oferecidas pelos provedores globais de SaaS e nuvem.
O Everpure Data Intelligence apoia essa abordagem ao identificar, classificar e contextualizar dados corporativos na plataforma Everpure, em nuvens públicas, aplicações SaaS e sistemas de armazenamento de terceiros.
Com visibilidade completa desse ambiente, as empresas podem tomar decisões bem fundamentadas sobre a governança e a proteção de seus dados.  Ao priorizar os dados e a mitigação de riscos, as organizações podem incorporar a soberania desde a concepção e transformá-la em uma fonte de resiliência e vantagem competitiva, em vez de uma barreira à inovação.
Metodologia Encomendada pela Everpure à Vanson Bourne, a pesquisa ouviu 2.100 executivos C-level e líderes de TI de grandes empresas em junho de 2026.  O estudo foi realizado em oito países: Reino Unido, França, Alemanha, Austrália, Japão, Coreia do Sul, Singapura e Índia.  Esses países representam diferentes contextos regulatórios e geopolíticos nos quais a soberania de dados se tornou um fator determinante para os resultados dos negócios.
